                                                                           ( PRAISE THE LORD )

Ethics in general is to study on moral right and wrong, the study of good and evil.
In terms of Christian Theology, ethics is viewed as a means of determining how do we receive blessings based on human acts and attitudes.

While studying Christian ethics we need to study on 2 important aspects
God's Divine Nature
God's Divine Actions 

God's Divine Nature
God is not accountable to any standards outside of himself, and that everything that accords with God is good and light. 

Scripture says in 1 John verse 5, that God is light and that there is no darkness in him.

Light is considered as a metaphor of God, it is a moral evaluation and darkness is equated with Sin & Lies

Divine Actions
God shows his approval for what is right by bestowing blessings. Similary God shows hatred for what is wrong and evil by withholding blessings and pouring out curses

In the old testament scriptures, God instructs the Israelites to strictly obey the commandments, on doing so - they would be blessed !!
Disobedience would invite God's wrath, including death and destruction

Unless a work or action is performed with right motive, it is not a work that God will reward with blessings. Two important things that we need to always consider through our actions and works are 
1) Faith 
2) Love

FAITH 
Faith plays a very important role in our life, any work done without a purified heart of faith is considered to be sinful and it does not please God. This criteria of the right motive is closely associated with good Christian Ethics.

Works of Faith can only be demonstrated by the indwelling of the Holy Spirit, and our actions and works accordingly  will culminate in rewards and blessings from God. Our faith should be consistent with growth, as it is also the means of purification within believers, motivating to produce good works.

Faith without works is dead - as it says in the book of James, 
The kind of faith that purifies the heart, faith that saves, faith that motivates to good works. 

In the book of Hebrews it says, Without faith it is impossible to please God. 

Unless we try to please God and see blessings, our works and actions should be based on faith. 

Also everything that is done without faith is considered to be sin, as instructed by Apostle Paul in the book of Romans.

LOVE :
Apostle Paul says in 1st Corinthians 13 - Paul taught that our works are unproductive if it is not motivated by love. 

Love plays an important role in our Christian life, all our works and even spiritual gifts, for results to be evident should be motivated by love. Everything else will not receive the approval from our God.

When Jesus spoke about the greatest commandment, it begins with Love

Love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul and with all your mind.

Love is an aspect of every law God requires us to obey. Love is the standard that God has set for maknkind to follow, wheter it is loving God or neighbor.

The threefold criteria for good works described in this lesson are as follows :

All our works should be based on 
1) Proper Motive
2) Proper Standard 
3) Proper Goal

Proper Motive
All our works should have proper motive and it should be governed by two strong pillars of Faith & Love. Everything that we do, all our works if not done by faith & love will not be merited as per God's standards. The basic criteria for all our works to have a proper motive is Faith and Love

Proper Standard
All our works and actions should be of proper standard 
Westminster Confession of Faith says, that all our works that God commands, but unless done in a right manner according to the Word, they are sinful.
All sin violates God's law.
In order for our works to be of of proper standard it has to be governed by 3 aspects

1) Commands of Scripture
All the commands of Scripture are designed to guide us. 
2) All of Scripture 
Proper standard requires submission to the whole bible. God's word as a whole is a criterion for good works. 
3) General Revelation
God's revelation in creation itself is part of his word, that is commonly called as general revelation is also a standard for good works.

Good works must conform to 
God's Word - as Revealed in the Law, In all of Scriptiure and in General Revelation of Creation.

Perspectives are Ethical judgment involving the application of God's Word to a situation by a person. 
The three different perspective to be emplyed when approaching ethics
1) Situational Perspective
2) Normative Perspective 
3) Existential Perspective

1) Situational Perspective
This type of perspective focuses on the end or the result of actions. Always asking questions like, what are the best means of achieving God's purposes ? It also incudes appeals to moral behavior based on prior examples and other morally good characters as mentioned in the Scripture. We are to apply the scripture in our situations and follow the lead given in the word of God.

2) Normative Perspective
Refers to the fact that God's word is the norm or standard for ethics. We are doing ethics from normative perspecitve when we look at the word of God for directives as to what is to be done.

3) Existential Perspecitve
When we approach ethics by asking questions that are specific to the people involved, we are doing ethics from an existential perspective. It focuses on the self in confrontation and interaction with God.

God has the ultimate perogative to determind whether any particular action, emotions and thoughts meet or transgress his moral requirements and he has the ultimate right and power to act on his determinations. 

When we consider the scripture in the Gospel of John chapter 5, it says that 
My judgement is just, for I seek not to please myself but him who sent me. 

God in himself is the highest court in the universe. He will make the ultimate determination of wheterher or not we have lived morally or immorally and all his judgements will be true. No one can challenge his authority.  No one can challenge God's absolute authority, as it also follows absolute power. 

As the absolute judge of morality, God consistently applies the absolute moral standard of his character in every judgement. His judgements are perfect, exhibiting flawless insight and wisdom.

The three categories of revelation that are part of God's Word are as follows :
1) Special Revelation 
Special revelation is made up of Scripture, prophecy, dreams and visions
The complexity of speical revelation is that it come in various forms. It involves God communicating with people in ways that transcend the normal ways of creation. 
In some cases God appears visibly, whereas in some cases speaks audibly to groups or individuals. In other cases he speaks through an angel. God also provides special revelation to write down and recorded in Scripture.  These types of special revelation are very special as they represent the extraordinary or supernatural communication between God and man. 

2) General Revelation :
General Revelation is what happens in history, in the universe, weather, plants, animals and human beings
It speaks about the way creation and history tell us true things about God and his moral requirements, But due to the fall of Adam and Eve, and the fallen world, the General Revelation does not present us with a clear picture of God's character. But the Bible assures us that general revelation still speaks clearly enough to teach us true things about God.

3) Existential Revelation 
God reveals himself in and through persons has always been recognized as a part of general revelation. 
It can be further divided into External and Internal aspects
External includes the revelation through human beings, created in the image og God. Human beings reflect God;s glory and dignity. Our image reflects God's character. 

Internal : 
Internal types of existential revelation involves the Holy Spirit working within human beings to reveal truth about God. Divine gifts that form part of this revelation in enabling to grow spritiually.

When God created man in his own image , God had given Adam exercising authority. When Adam named the animals he was thinking and exercising the divinely delegated authority, whenever human beings think and judge in an exercisde we are reflective God's character.

Similary Jesus has also taught in the Scripture - where every matter may be established by the testimony of two or three witnesses.

Jesus supports their exercise of the authority that he has delegated the church.

Internal Existential Revelation talks about the ways that the Holy Spirit works with human beings to reveal truth about God.
Theologians consider 2 important topics
Illumination & Inward leading of the Holy Spirit 

Illumination of the Holy Spirit, is a divine gift of understanding that God gives to believers and even to unbelievers. Whe Holy Spirit illuminates a person's mind the ability or knowledge of that person increases and he is able to grasp information that he previously lacked. 

Inward Leading - is one of the most common ways in which Holy Spirit works within individuals to reveal truth about God's character. We see inward leading displayed clearly in our individual consciences and as well in our feelings that God would provide us while taking a particular course of action. 

In all these things God's character or standard is revealed unto us as we consistently study the scriptures.

1st John 1: 7 says that

To understand historical analysis we need to review some broad perspectives  that Holy Spirit has led the church to pursue the exegesis of Scripture in three ways :
literary analysis, historical analysis, thematic analysis
Historical analysis looks at scripture as a window to history, exploring historical events lying behind the Bible. It is especially concerned with the "acts of God".
Biblical theology approaches the Scripture primarily with historical analysis. It looks at the Bible as a window that gives access to history. In this the focus of exegesis shifts from traditional theological themes to the historical events described in the Bible ,a very different set of priorities and concerns emerge. While sound Biblical theology is based on historical analysis of the Scriptures , we should turn to the fact that it is primarily concerned with the acts of God.

Historical analysis can take different forms  of at least two main tendencies:
FACTUAL HISTORICAL ANALYSIS AND THEOLOGICAL HISTORICAL ANALYSIS
These two tendencies go hand in hand , but their main concerns are quite different
A factual approach to historical analysis is concerned with questions like the date f the exodus under Moses, the historical circumstances that gave rise to Israel's monarchy , evidences certain battles and other crucial events. The goal of factual historical analysis is rather straight forward.
Theological historical analysis-
It is  the theological significance of the acts of God reported in Scripture.

On the one hand a theological matter is anything that refers directly to God . The term "diachronic "derives from two Greek word: first, the preposition "dia" which often means "through"or "throughout": and second, the Greek noun Chronos which means time.
Diachrony is a concern with the passage of time. In the case of the Biblical theology, the term "diachronics" points to the way Old Testament Theology transformed, changed,or developed throughout time.
Diachronic approaches to the Bible concentrate on how theological structures progressively unfolded through time. A diachronic approach however, is much more concerned with changes that occurred in theological structures
for example it asks questions like"How did God's revelation at the burning bush anticipate his work in Egypt?"These type of issues become of central importance in diachronic approaches to this part of Old Testament.

We use term development instead of simply speaking of diachronic changes to suggest two main ideas. First, changes in Old Testament theological structures always move towards fulfilling God's purposes for history. And Second , we speak of developments because theological changes only occur through God's providential involvement in history. 
Divine purposes:
The Scripture affirm that everything in history, including shifts in theology, always accomplish God's unfailing purposes for his creation.Isaiah 46:10.God's goals for history exist not only as broad , long -term goals but also as particular , short term goals.God also has an all -encompassing purpose for history.God began history with great destiny in mind and every event in history will, without fail , reach his glorious end.
Divine Providence:
The road of the Old Testament is actually filled with steep inclines , fast descents, and sharp turns to the left and to the right. these abrupt shifts are caused by God's providence, his complex involvement with His creation.God wanted these theological shifts to take place.
God offered the first generation of Exodus , the possession of the promised land , but their infidelity led to their rejection . yet none of these human changes were outside of God's Sovereign control.

There are three basic typs of revelation, special revelation such as the Bible, General revealation which comes to us through the creation in general and existential revelation which comes to us through persons. 

But based on these for us to make ethical decisions we have to consider three important aspects they are 
FACTS
GOALS
MEANS

Facts :
Through revelation God speaks to us facts about himself and what he requires. Undrestand that God is the supreme authority over all creation, his aauthority is absolute and his character is perfect. God's revelation also teaches us about special set of facts that are particularly important for ethics.

Goals :
Goals in ethics are the targeted outcome that we have in mind. It is similar to the set of goals that we keep in mind, that we set to accomplish. Revelation provides us with goals that we ust adopt in Christian ethics.

Scripture teaches us about goals for doing good to our neighbors, raising children, striving for unity of the church. But the most important revelation is it presents God's glory as our primary and most important goal in life.

Means :
Any ethical question in biblical manner requires - to find the appropriate means to achieve as revealed by God. Setting goals, assessing facts etc are things that influence our action. But our actions themselves are the means we have chosen to accomplish our goals. Godly means are equally important to achieve our goals and to understand the facts about God.

Facts are very important for us to know more about God in order to make ethical decisions. 
God's character should be our ultimate norm or standard, and obligates us to live by the standard of his character. 
Through revelation, God tells us facts about himself and facts about what he requires. Without the knowledge about the facts, we would still obey God, but without much knowledge.

God is the supreme authority over all of creation. His authority is absolute, His character perfect. Whenever we receive a revelation about his character, it is a means by which God exercises control over humans, similary to governments exercising control over it's citizens through their laws. 

God not only communicates facts to us, but God's revelation also teaches us about special set of facts that are particulary important for ethics ; the proper goals of Christian behavior and decision making.

Goals in ethics are the expected outcomes of our endeavors that we have in our mind. Goals are similar to that which we set in our mind to accomplish. Goals can be small or large. They can be immediate goals or that which we plan in the distant future. But in every case our goals give direction to our action.

Scripture teaches us about goals of doing good to our neighbors, raising children in Christ, striving for the unity of church. But the most important goals is God's glory.

God glory in revelation reveals that we must be loyal to God and that we should praise him and glorify God in everything that we do. Scripture teaches us to set God's glory as our highest goal.

Existential revelation helps us to discern good goals from evil goals, especially through our consciences. Holy Spirit is another source of existential revelation, moving within us so that we pursue good goals and shun evil ones.

God uses all three forms of revelation, special, general and existential in order to teach us the goals that God approves.

Christians inclined to follow a rigorous strategy towards revelation, resulting in tending to err on the side of overly restricting behavior rather than on the side of permitting it.

Rigor often views the situation in Bible as being similar to our own and applies the Scripture directly to our lives without consideration or scope to think about how it differs from the modern world, in terms of facts and goals. 

Christians endorsing a rigorous strategy, mistakenly believe that when the Bible's facts, goals and means appear to be vague, the proper response is to apply Scripture in restrictive ways. By doing so we often end up forbidding some things that God permits and other things that God actually commands.

Dangers :
It destroys Christian Freedom by prohibiting behavior that are wrong under certain conditions. But good under other conditions. As matters of conscience are not clear, a strategy of rigor would tend to prohibit certain actions resulting in missing Godly blessings.

A strategy of rigor also inspires despair in believers by turning God's world into a heavy burden. 

Avoid falling into this strategy :
Realize that modern situations are sufficiently different from biblical situations, we cannot just apply or copy the applications to the present modern era, without giving it further considerations.

We can avoid a strategy of rigor by remembering that Scripture is sufficiently clear to communicate God's will with regard to ethics.

Jesus spoke about the Kingdom of God in the Sermon on the Mount found in the Gospel of Mathew Chapter 5

The Sermon on the mount is well known, Jesus began by encouraging people to live ethically in terms of the Kingdom of God.

Lets consider the three different sections wherein Jesus emphasized the importance of the Kingdom of God

1) Mathew 5:3 - the blessing was "theirs is the kingdom of heaven" Though Mathew here used the phrase the "Kingdom of Heaven" biblical scholars have agreed that this term is is the same as Kingdom of God. 

2) Mathew 5:5 - the blessing was "they will inherit the earth" this was also a kingdom blessing, and it referred to the new earth that God will create when his kingdom will come in it's fullness.

3) Mathew 5:9 - the blessing was "they shall be called the sons of God" Even this statement of blessedness refers to the kingship and kingdom of God. In the times of old biblical times, human kings were called "father" by their subjects. Same is true about the scriptures. God is our heavenly father. 

Each of the blessings Jesus mentioned was connected to the concept of the kingdom of God.

The Three main components of the Kingdom of God are 

KING (role of the King) 
PEOPLE (Citizens of the Kingdom) 
COVENANTS (that govern the relationship between king and his people)

King :
The concept of King is unfamiliar to the modern people but in oden times Kings were expected to fulfill their responsibilities to the citizens of the country. They were to protect and provide for them and to treat them with kindness. In return King will charge them taxes and raise armies and regulate the many aspects of life.
Good Kings ruled wisely to benefit the people. 

In the Bible God is presented as the Supreme King or emperor over all creation.
All the earthly kings are his vassals or servan kings. 
Though David and thereafter his son Solomon sat on the throne of the Lord in Jerusalem. The throne still belongd to God so that the human kings were just representatives or vassals of God.

People :
The people here refers to those whom God has called to himself in contrast to the people of the world. 

Old testament refers to Abraham and his descendants. In the New Testament, it refers to the Church, since christians of all races have been adopted into the family of Abraham in Christ.

Under the kingship of Jesus the focus of God's kingdom became ecclesiastical it was centered on the church. God's kingdom includes people from every race and continues to spread to the ends of the earth.

Covenants :
God administered his kingdom through covenants. God's expressed good will towards his people through covenants, wherein clearly the parameters were mentioned regarding the consequences for obedience & disobedience and it was binding covenant for both parties.

There are 6 major covenants between God and his people, beginning with Adam to that of Noah, Abraham, Moses, David and finlly the Final Covenant in Christ Jesus.

Traditionally Bible has summarized the kingdom of God through three historical phases :

Initial Phase (Creation)
Rebellion (Humanity's fall into sin)
Final Peace (Redemption)

1) Initial Phase : 
Under creation story, humanity lived in perfect harmony with God. Human life was full of joy and gladness, of thanksgiving and singing. in the garden there was great peace.
There was no enemy to threaten them, no war, no violence, no sickness, no drought or flood or fire to destroy them etc.
God cared tenderly for Adam and Eve, and even met them and walked with them in the cool of the garden.

2) Rebellion 
As we study Genesis 3, we are aware of humanity's initial rebellion against God through disobedience & the fall of man. Serpent tempted Eve to eat the forbidden tree and shared the fruit with Adam. By sinnning humanity violated one of the covenant obligation.

God threw Adam & Eve out of the Garden and forced them to live in a world wherein it was the cursed ground followed by pain in childbirth and along with sickness and famine with wild animals and threats of war. They stil lhad to fulfill the covenant obligations but they were experiencing the negative considequences due to sin. 

Humanity has continued to rebel against God throughout history. God has punished humans with covenant curses. 

3) Final Peace
God began to restore peace to his kindom immediately after humanity's fall into sin. God did not wipe out humanity completely when they sinned, but he allowed them to live. God introduced the first steps, promise of salvation through Genesis 3:15. Throughout history God was working toward the goal of full redemption and success of his kingdom.

At the appearance of Christ, the restoration of final peace took a huge leap and reached the final stages of fulfillment. Jesus came to earth as a vassal king in order to establish a faithful kingd om earth. His work still continues and he will come again in glory and restore the kingdom, bring the whole world under final peace.

God's laws are a delight and it adds joy to our life. As humans when we obey the laws laid down by God, in return we receive blessings that God has itended for obedient citizens of his kingdom.

Law's reveals God to us, teaching us how to please him and how to obtain his blessings. Laws were given for our good and for our prosperity and for our joy.

David summarized in Psalms 19

The law of the Lord is perfect, reviving the sould. The precepts of the Lord are right giving joy to the heart

God has given us rules to follow in order to produce joy in our lives. And those rules are his law. So when we obey God's law, we enjoy him and we glory him at the same time. We enjoy him because he blesses our obedience and because it pleases us to bring pleasure to the God we love. And our godly joy brings glory to God by fulfilling his purpose. In all of these ways, the role of the Law shows us that enjoying God is an important part of God's goal for humanity.

In our present modern age, our enjoyment of God is often hindered by our suffering. But we also need to understand that God's plan for us is through suffering, it further enhances our faith and improves our understanding of God's grace and knowledge about him. 

A close analysis of the Scripture teaches us that God uses suffering as a tool that proves our faith and brings us to spiritual maturit and that ultimately results in our joy.

Manytimes we do not understand the full purpose and plan in our sufferings. But if you further study the scriptures and draw closer to God, we will experience more the grace of God in our sufferings and challenges of life. Also our experiences of joy will bring great glory to our divine King. 

Our view of the laws and the scriptures need to be focussed on drawing nearer to our creator.  To increase our trust factor in God and to understand that we are the clay in the hands of our master builder.

Biblical theology is the theological reflection drawn from the historical analysis of acts of God reported in Scripture.Historical analysis is especially concerned with "acts of God".
The holy Spirit has led the church to pursue the exegesis of Scripture in three main ways : literary analysis, historical analysis and thematic analysis. Historical analysis looks at Scripture as a window to history, exploring historical events lying behind the Bible.
Biblical theology approaches the Scriptures primarily with historical analysis. It looks at the bible as a window that gives access to the history. When the focus shifts from theological themes to the historical events described in the Bible, a very different set of priorities and concerns emerge .

Biblical theological reflection is based on the historical analysis of the acts of God in Scripture. historical analysis take two different forms: factual historical analysis and theological historical analysis. These two tendencies go hand in hand , but their concerns are quite different.
Factual approach are concerned with  the events are reported in scripture fit within the large environment ancient Near East. A factual approach to historical analysis is concerned with questions like the date of the exodus under Moses etc.
The goal of factual historical analysis is straight forward.It is to establish a reliable account of the facts of history along with the data we gather from extra biblical resources.
Christians agree with Aquinas that theology has two main concerns .A theological matter is anything that refers directly to God.  And on the other hand theological matter is anything that describes other subjects in relation to God. Biblical theology opens the way for enhancing and enlarging our understanding of all of these theological subjects like the human race, sin, salvation etc

There are many cultural changes that set the stage for biblical theology .Biblical theology is in large measure a response to cultural shifts that can be traced back to the Enlightenment of the 17th century.
Simply put biblical theology is a Christian response to a prominent intellectual movement in the modern period, often called modern historic ism.
One of the most well known Enlightenment figures who expressed this cultural shift was the German philosopher George Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel, known for his proposal that every aspect of reality is caught up in logical patterns of historical progress known as the dialectic. 
The study of geology, biology, and similar shifts toward modern historicism took place in the nearly academic discipline including theology.
Everything in life was thought to be understand most thoroughly when it was assessed in terms of the flow of history.

As per Gabler Christians should believe in the modern world through rational reflection on science and religion. Gabler believed that the findings f the biblical theology might be of some interest from time to time ,but modern Christians should believe only the parts of the bible that pass the standards of the modern rational and scientific analysis. From the perspective, the crossing of the Red Sea was nothing more than that a strong wind blowing through a marsh.
We might have expected them simply to set aside biblical theology since they thought that the Bible was riddled with misleading historical claims. 
But the field of Biblical theology did not die when critical theologians rejected biblical authority. Instead they found other ways to use scriptures for contemporary theology. Instead of treating the Bible as true history, they began to look at scriptures as expressions of ancient religious sentiments presented as historical claims, and they explored how these ancient religious feelings and experiences might be useful to modern Christians .

The divine goal of all world history is the extension of God's perfect heavenly reign to every corner of the earth . When God's will is done as perfectly on earth as it is in heaven, every creature will bow before God and honor him as the divine king., the supreme creator of all. 
The opening chapters of the Bible describes the way God began to turn the chaotic world into his kingdom by ordering creation and placing his image in the garden of Eden and by commanding humanity to extend to the ends of the earth.
The rest of the Old Testament reports how God chose Israel as his special people and commissioned them to the lead the rest of humanity in spreading the kingdom of God to the ends of the earth, but Israel also failed terribly.
Despite these failures, God did not give up on his grand purpose. As the NEW Testament reveals , God sent his eternal son in to the world. through his death, resurrection and ascension, the ministry of the holy Spirit through his body and his glorious return, Christ is completing the task originally given to humanity. 
In this approach to biblical theology, every event in biblical history is part of this grand scheme.
The vast variety of divine actions , great and small will bring ultimate glory to God through the establishment of his kingdom in the new heavens and new earth, thus completing the goal,of biblical history to bring God glory.

The word "synchronic" is derived from two Greek words: the preposition "sun" which means "with" or "together" and the noun chronos means "time". In relation to the historical events , it describes occurrences that took place "together in time" or "at the same time".
The term synchronic is used to indicate how biblical theologians often explore sets of events in Old Testament history that happened at the same time.
Illustration:
In a movie, the directors tell their stories in a flow from beginning to the end. They depict how one event leads to another and so on. The movies is on , whole unit is broken down into smaller parts called scenes. every scene tells a portion of the larger story. Each story represents a synchronic moment in the movie, period of time in the film. 
Similarly . The sychronic study of the Old Testament takes the same approach. The Biblical theologians concentrate their attention on particular periods of the time in the Old Testament  as if they were scenes in a movie rather on the flow of its entire story.Sometimes biblical theologians focus on relatively brief historical moments, but other times they concern themselves with relatively long periods

Synthesis means combining different components of something into a whole. Synchronic synthesis describes the way different components of a particular periods of history fit together in a coherent, logical structure.
Many critical scholars distinguished biblical theology from systematic theology by pointing out the role of logic in each.Critical theologians believed that logic was a primary feature of the"greek mindset", but was relatively foreign to the "hebrew" mindset.

variety of genres
different emphases
 no all en-compassing system

In third place Old Testament writers turned their readers attention towards the future as in Isaiah 40:1-11

True stories about historical peoples, place and events that reveal many details about history through:

It is important while discerning historical information not to expect them to be like modern journalistic historical writing. Historians must seek to be as exacting as their counter parts in science s like chemistry and biology. True historical records will include every significant fact about a situation to give a balance account. They will avoid all subjective evaluations that will prejudice readers.

Old testament narratives wrote in ways that were determined largely by their didactic purposed and not by our modern sensibilities. These narratives were only as comprehensive as suited the didactic purposes of their writers. they dint not include every significant fact. For example in Solomon's life 2 Chronicles 1-9 , they emitted every negative dimension of Solomon's reign.
They were only as precise as their didactic purposes required. They did not meet the modern criterion of good history writing

Old Testament writers were only as precise as their didactic purposes required . There is vital difference between precision and truth. In every aspect of life, precision is always a matter of degree and so long as we respond with as much precision as is needed , no one accuses us of misrepresenting facts. This was true with the Old Testament authors .they were only as precise as they needed to be reach their didactic goals.
1 Kings 9:5 and 2 Chronicles 7:18, we can read God spoke to David and God covenanted with David respectively. so we can see here that Old Testament narratives were not designed to repeat words and thoughts if god or anyone else with absolute precision. What they wrote was historically true. They did not misrepresent what God said.
Numbers of people, measurements and geographical references often do not modern significant standards. But this lack of modern precision does not mean the accounts are untrue.
In summary we can say with confidence that old testament narratives were not designed to meet modern standards of history writing, but they represent fully reliable historical information that will enables us to construct synchronic synthesis Testament theology .

The creed was a collective work that gradually developed over several centuries. Rules of Faith: summaries of beliefs and practices: To preserve the teachings of the church and train its people (especially leaders) Often these rules varied from from congregation to congregation. Generally speaking, they included affirmations of important doctrines as well as teachings and traditions. 
Creeds were the summaries of doctrinal portions of church's rules of faith. These were recited in liturgical settings. One ancient creed that rose to prominence was from the church in Rome, often called the Roman Creed, which was similar to the Apostolic Creed. the Apostolic creed eventually came into widespread use, especially in Western churches. In the early centuries, its precise wording varied from church to church. But in the eighth century the wording was generally standardized into the form that we recognize and use today.

The bible is our only inspired infallible rule of faith and practice. Creeds, are fallible teaching tools that summarize our understanding of Scripture. And the apostles' creed was created to help Christians learn and remain true to the teachings of the bible. The purpose of the apostles creed is as follows;
1. Scripture- Scripture in all its parts was word of Christ, and that it was the source of all true doctrine. Basis of doctrine, Sola scriptura- this is the perspective that scripture is the only infallible rule of faith, and final arbiter in any theological controversy.
2. Traditional teaching- The early church depended on the traditional teachings of the church to summarize and protect the teachings of scripture. Christian leaders created summaries so that all Christians would know and affirm the basic content of faith. 
3. Apostolic Creed- the apostles' creed was largely used to confirm that new Christians believed the fundamental teachings of the Bible.  The goal was to ensure that the churches did not stray from the original meaning of scripture.

The creed is based on the belief that there is only one God and that this God exists in three persons. The trinity is one of the most important beliefs of Christianity. One essence- only one God. By the term person, we mean a distinct, self aware personality. And by the term essence, we are referring to God's fundamental nature or the substance of which he consists. 
Three persons: The Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit- distinct from one another. 
Father- Almighty, Maker of heaven and earth. The creed'd description of Father doesn't distinguish Christianity from other religions that express belief in a sovereign creator.
Son- The creed mentions Jesus' incarnation, his coming to earth as human baby, and living a genuinely human life. And it speaks of his suffering, death, burial, resurrection and ascension into heaven.
Holy Spirit- The creed associates the Holy Spirit with the church, and with our experience of salvation both now and in the future. The creed says enough about God and his persons to distinguish those who affirm the historic Christian faith from those who do not.

1. Participation- The creed emphasizes the importance of participating in the church. The bible teaches Christians to form an actual physical community and it insists that this community is extremely important to every believer. It is not to be limited to spiritual fellowship, although it is true that Christians have spiritual communion with each other through Christ and his Spirit. Rather, our community is to be like a family or neighborhood. It is to consist of people who interact with each other face to face. 
2. Preservation- The creed affirms the fact that Christ appointed his church in part to protect and proclaim the gospel and other truths. According to Jude, part of church's job is to contend for faith, to protect the truths and beliefs that have been entrusted to it against those who promote false teachings and practices. We have to keep trying to preserve doctrine in the church.

The Apostle's Creed is foundational to theology because it introduces us to the teachings of apostles recorded in scripture. 
1. Standard- The apostles' creed functions as a doctrinal standard because it presents several of the biggest most important ideas of Christianity. These ideas are taught so clearly in Scripture that they should be recognized and embraced by everyone. Using the creed as a standard helps us remain faithful to scripture when convincing false teachers present us with bad theology. So, it helps to have a short list of essential beliefs that can anchor us to the teachings of Scripture and the apostles' creed provides such an anchor. 
2. Logical Basis- Logically basic ideas are the sources of other ideas. The creed provides the big doctrines so we can: see the relationship between the different beliefs in our theological systems. Doctrines that are more remote from Scripture in ways that harmonize with our fundamental beliefs helps us remain faithful to scripture.

The english word "diachronic "derives from the two Greek Words :first the preposition dia which often means "through" or "throughout" and the second , the Greek Nouns Chronos which means "time". Diachrony  is a concern with the passage of time. 
In the case of biblical theology, the term "diachronic "points to the ways the Old Testament  theology transformed , changed or developed through the time.
Diachronic approches to the Bible concentrate on how theological structures progressively unfoldes through the time. It says about God's revelations took place or developed as history moved forward.
Looking at the Old Testament diachronically is like concentrating on the storyline of a movie as it moves from scene to scene.
It's to focus on the ways a film progressively unfolds its drama from beginning to the end.

We use the tem "development "instead of simply speaking of diachronic changes to suggest two main ideas. First the changes in Old Testament theological structures always move toward fulfilling God's purposes for history and second , we speak of development because theological changes only occur through God's providential involvement in history.
1.Divine purposes-
Isaiah 46:10 reflects a common outlook throughout God's unfailing purposes for his creation. When we go through the Scriptures , they affirm that everything in history including shifts in theology, always accomplish God's unfailing purposes for his creation.
God;s goals for history exist not inky as broad, long term goals , but also short term goals. God has an all-encompassing kingdom purpose for history.From the beginning, his design has been to glorify himself by extending his heavenly kingdom to the entire earth through the work of his image and this unites all of God's purposes
2. Divine providence:
When we look at Old testament , we see that the road is actually filled with steep inclines, fast descents and sharp turns to the left an the right.These abrupt shifts are caused by God's providence, his complex involvement with his creation. The only explanation that we can hold with certainity is that God simply wanted these theological shifts to take place.

Biblical Typology is the study of diachronic developments between the theological structures closely associated with significant persons , institutions and events in scripture.
in simple language , we might say that typology is the study of the types. The word "type" derives from the Greek word tupos.
Biblical theology applies the term typology to any diachronic development of topics in Old Testament theology. On occasions , biblical theologians will speak of the typology of the doctrine of God, or the typology of worship, and simply mean that these are then ways developed in the Bible.
For example Jesus spoke of   a typological connection between Moses' bronze serpent and himself.
1. Typology functions as a figure of speech For example Romans 5:14 the apostle Paul declared that Adam was a pattern or type
2. A second feature of biblical theology is that compared elements are quite varied. In Peter 3:21 Peter compared the event of Noah's flood with baptism
3. In the third place , typologies in the Bible always compare the theological structures that are closely associated with their elements.
4.A fourth characteristic of typologies in Scripture is that they always reflect diachronic developments

God as he is presented in scripture by looking at two subjects. The ''singularity'' of God, the fact that he is the only God that exists. And the ''simplicity'' of God, noting that he really is only one God, despite the fact that he has three persons. 
1. Polytheism- Belief in the the existence of multiple Gods. In polytheism, no one God can claim to be the only supernatural being who exercises control over the universe. One reason for this was so common that polytheism was often required by law.
2. Monotheism- Belief in only one God. Scripture asserts that there is only one God- 1 Kings 8.60- The Lord is God...there is no other. Psalms 86.10- You alone are God. 
3. Christianity- The creed does not explicitly say that there is only one God. It is organized around a Trinitarian Formula. It indicates that the God of Christianity is the only one who deserves to be called "God."

God has three persons, but only one essence. The term "person" refers to distinct, self aware personality and that the term "essence" refers to God's fundamental nature, or the substance of which he consists God's essence is not a composite of different substances; but a unified whole consisting of only one substance. God has a simple unified essence, they were denying that the Father, Son and Holy Spirit were three separate Gods that somehow joined together in the trinity. And instead, they were affirming that these three persons had always existed together as only one God. We believe in only one God- one divine being- who exists in three persons.

The word ontological means being related to being. It is considering how the three persons of the Trinity are integrated with one another, and how they share a single essence. From the perspective of ontology, all three of God's persons are infinite, eternal and unchangeable. And each has the same essential divine attributes, such as wisdom, power, holiness, justice, goodness and truth. 
The word ''economic'' means ''relating to household management.'' When we consider how God's persons interact with each other, how they relate to one another as individual persons. 
From both the ontological and economic perspective the Father is said to be the first person, generated by the Father, and the Holy Spirit is said to proceed from the Father. Besides being the first person of the ontological Trinity, the Father is also called the first person of the economic Trinity. 
The Son is generated by the Father (externally generated) and Holy Spirit proceed from the Father (externally proceeds) in the ontological trinity.
In economic trinity, authority is over the Son and the over the Holy Spirit.

Fatherhood- Scriptures that talk about God's fatherhood come from the Old Testament, prior to the time that God clearly revealed his truine nature. The word "Father" refers and foremost to the entire Trinity, and not just to the person of the Father. 
1. Creator- Scripture refers to God as father of everything he has created. For instance, in passages like Deut 32.6, Isa 43.6-7, God's general fatherhood over creation motivates him to show great patience with our fallen world and with sinful humanity in particular.

2. King- God was called father because he was the great king that ruled over all the kings of the world, and because he ruled directly over his chosen nation Israel. Jesus instructed his disciples to pray to "Our Father in Heaven."

3. Family Head- In the old testament, God is portrayed as family head of nation Israel. Everyone is familiar with concept of family head. Well, Scripture often describes God's relationship to his people in the same terms. This description also continues in New Testament.

1. Absolute- The father has complete freedom to do whatever he wants with his creation. Scripture often compares his absolute authority to a potter's authority over his clay. We find this description in places like Isa 29.16, Isa 45.9 etc. God is the creator of all, has the freedom and right to do whatever he wants with what he creates. 
2. Exclusive- Besides having absolute authority the Father also has exclusive authority over everything he created. The Father's authority as creator is exclusive in sense that no creature possess absolute authority. Absolute authority belongs only to the creator and God is the only creator. The authority ultimately resided in the Father,and was his exclusive prerogative. 
3. Exhaustive- God's authority is exhaustive, we mean that it extends over everything he has created, in every detail. And there is at least important implications of the fact. First, everyone is under God's authority. There is no person or other creation the obligation to obey God. Second, Everything is under God's authority. His authority extends to every detail of what he has created. Everything in creation either functions as God wants it to, and therefore good or rebels against him, is therefore evil.

There are two perspectives: 
Ontological Trinity- We are focusing on God's being and existence. From this perspective, the Holy Spirit is equal in power and glory to the Father and the Son. All three of God's persons are infinite, eternal and unchangeable. and each has the same essential divine attributes such as wisdom, power, holiness, justice, goodness and truth. 
Economic Trinity- we are considering how God's persons interact with each other. From this perspective, each person of the GodHead has different responsibilities, different authority and a different assigned role. The Spirit's authority is subject to higher authority of the Father and the Son. and the Spirit's role is largely to carry out their instructions and to bring them glory. The Holy Spirit is called the third person of the Trinity.

The concept of the church in the New Testament finds it roots in the Old Testament. The NT speaks many times of the church using the word ekklesia. But this term comes from the Greek translation of Old Testament, Septuagint. Ekklesia and its Hebrew counterpart is frequently used to identify the gathered nation of Israel. In the New Testament, ekklesia became a technical term referring to the church while being used to the assembly of Old Testament Israel. For example, in Acts 7.38- the Greek word translated assembly is ekklesia, which is commonly translated to ''church.'' This means that the assembly of Israel was Old Testament equivalent to our New Testament Church.
We can see that the Old Testament church has been improved and built into the New Testament church. They are different in some important ways and they represent different stages of growth, but are still the same church.

In the original context of Jesus ministry, the only church that existed was Jewish synagogues scattered throughout the region and the temple of Jerusalem. They were the Old Testament forms of Israel's assemblies, but Jesus still called them, ''the church.'' Firstly, the New Testament presents Jesus as the fulfillment of God's promises to Israel. As we see in Romans 8.1-4 and Galatians 3.16-29, Jesus is shown as the faithful Israelite who keeps God's covenant and inherits all the blessing, God promised to Abraham and Moses. 
Secondly, Jesus is the founder of  the New Testament church, who brought the restoration and renewal that changed the failing Old Testament into the New Testament church. He is called the head of the church in Ephesians 5.23 and Colossians 1.18. He is also called the husband of the church in Ephesians 5.22-23. 
Thus Jesus built his church in these ways that relied and advanced the Old Testament church.

Jesus ordained the New Testament church as the restoration and development of Old Testament Israel, one important implication is that there is fundamental continuity between the Israel in the Old Testament and the present Christian church in the New Testament. Practically, we should expect the community of God's people in the New Testament to reflect its Old Testament. 
Purpose- to turn the world into God's earthly kingdom. Redemption of humanity and creation has always been the purpose of God's church in both the testaments. 
Believers and Unbelievers- both assemblies include believers and unbelievers. The continuity between Old Testament church and New Testament in the present time is that both assemblies of God's people include believers and unbelievers.
Obligations- Both the testaments, people of God were given the responsibility to love God, spread His Kingdom throughout the world,and bring him glory. Greatest commandment is Heartfelt love for God as in 1 John 5.3.

The word ''catholic'' means universal; or including all Christians in all congregations. word Catholic coming from the Latin word Catholicus derives from Greek preposition  .Kata and the adjective holos means whole or ''complete.'' It is a description of the unity that exists between all churches that faithfully follow Christ. The Apostolic Creed speaks of the catholicity of the church, it does not have in mind an organization of all Christian congregations. Rather, it tells about the unity of the Holy Spirit that exists all legitimate Christian Churches. In history, it meant to extend the name ''church'' to every Christian congregation. At this time, these churches began to use the word ''catholic'' in new exclusive sense. By insisting that their own churches were catholic or universal, each meant to identify itself as the only valid church, and to condemn rival churches.

The visible church is said to be as one worldwide fellowship of all people in covenant with God under headship of Christ. There is no single denomination whose government extends over all Christian congregation. Rather the unity of the visible church is based on the fact that each church is in covenant with same God, and under the covenant headship of the same Christ. The three traditional marks of the church are as follows,
Preaching of the word. God has given the Bible to the whole visible church and he gave the Holy Spirit to help us understand it. Scripture exhorts the whole church to read, understand, and to teach God's word as we see in Matthew 28.20, 1 Timothy 4.17 etc.
Second mark is the right administration of the sacraments of baptism and the Lord's Supper. These sacraments belong to the visible church not just to one denomination.
third mark is the formal church discipline such as excommunication. No christian enjoys formal church discipline. And this had led churches to avoid the use of formal discipline.

Love is central to Bible's teaching, we are exhorted to love the Lord and also to love each other. 

Loyalty is the cornerstone of the concept of love. 
In the Old Testament period, God is our king and he rules over us, Suzerain love was expressed largely in the form of covenant loyalty to his people. We are bound in covenant with God. The most important way we can show our love form him is through our earnest covenant loyalty
In the New Testament - Jesus is our Lord and King, and we are to render love to him through loyal obedience.
We cannot place other loyalties ahead of our loyalty to him. 
Loyalty is a positive virtue, motivating us to serve our Lord and King

Orientation:
Our lives must be comprehensively oriented around God. God and his kingdom should be our highest priorities, our focus and our desires should revolve around God. Scripture teaches us to be fully committed to God and his people.
The prime example for proper orientation is the life of Jesus. 
Jesus life revolved around God and the people he came to save. This orientation motivated him to obey God perfectly in all things.

Responsibility
Our loving submission to God should motivate us to seek out additional ways that we are responsible to him.
Seeking our reponsibilities before God, provides us unlimited allegiance to God.
Understanding that we are obligated to God in every area of our life, we are in a better position to make decision that God approves.

The actions of God in atoning grace and common grace can be explained as follows :

ATONING GRACE 
God always acts according to his character, all his actions are perfect expressions of his character. Scripture exhorts us to pattern both our character and our actions after God.

Jesus taught that we are to imitate God's forgiveness. We are to forgive those who sin against us because God has forgiven us.

As sinners we were offensive to God. We hated God and were his enemies. We deserved punishment no mercy. But God loved us and gave his only begotten son as sacrifice for our sins. And following his example we should be willing to suffer on behaf of others.

We are asked to show the same kind of love towards others that God showed in the atonment, by giving up our comforts and supporting others sharing our wealth and possessions, and even our lives to protect, care for our brothers and sisters. To love the people around us wholeheartedly

COMMON GRACE
Common grace refers to God's kindness to those who will never be saved. 
Jesus referred to God's common grace as an expression of his love to all humanity and it is true and genuine, it provides us a model we are to imitate.

Jesus taught that God's perfection includes his love for evil people, even for those who will never come to faith in Christ.
God expresses his love in many ways, sch as through sunshine, rain etc. God is kind to all people, providing stability and productivity for them in nature and allowing them to thrive in this life

The problem of sin is that it separates us from God's blessings and places under His curse. It condemns us. Apart from Christ, there is no other way to save ourselves from its presence or its consequences. Bible uses words like lawlessness, rebellion, transgression, offense, evil, and missing the mark to describe things that are sinful. It is violation of God's law. Omitting or neglecting the Law, is called the sin of omission and the transgression of law is doing what scripture forbids. This is the sin of commission. 
Sin originated from the rebellion against God, when Adam and Eve disobeyed and violated God's law and willingly chose to sin. Love for God is manifested in obedience to his law. 
And because of this, the consequences was that God judged and cursed the entire human race resulting in Spiritual death, corruption, and physical death. Sin earned humanity eternal suffering under God's judgement in hell.

God was not willing to let the entire human race remain under the curse of sin. So He sent us the redeemer, Jesus Christ to solve the problem of sin. 

1. Father- The Father sent the Son into the world and appointed him as the redeemer. He is the great architect of redemption. 
2. Son- Son was sent to the world becoming incarnate as Jesus, the long awaited Messiah, in order to atone for human sin. Jesus atoned for sin by dying on the cross in place of sinners. He received the divine curse that had been warranted by our sin. 
3. Holy Spirit- It reconciles us to God for forgiving all the sins we have committed. He gives us new spiritual life by regenerating our spirits, implications of the saving grace, continuity to forgiveness to us and maintains our faith, and leads us to daily repentance. 

We have been given the right to make petition to all three divine persons, give thanks to all three persons of God and take great confidence n our salvation, knowing that all three persons of the Trinity love us and work to ensure our redemption.

Motive can be the purpose for which we take an action. Motives are essentially the same as goals. 
Motive serve as causes, and our actions are the affects they produce. The list of motives include, our character traits, desires, feelings, commitments etc.

Bible makes it clear that if we are truly ethical, we must be rooted in God honoring motives. 

David taught Solomon that obedience to God must flow from the depths of our inner person, and it involes wholehearted devotion and willing mind, as God hates hypocrisy.

God is not interested only in the outward obedience. He requires every heart and motive behind the thoughts to be truly committed to him, genuine obedience from our deepest thougts and desires. 

God requires wholehearted obedience, that flows from the heart with good motives.

Bible condemns lip service, or evil motives calling it hypocrisy.

The virtue of Christian love should motivate us to act in loving ways. Similarly people who are joyful in the Spirit should be motivated by their joy. Peaceful peple motivated by the peace within them.

The greatest example we can look at would be the life of Jesus Christ, which provides us a lasting impact with genuine values both inward and outward and motivates us to do our best in glorfying God both externally and internally.

The process of forgiveness involves an element of individual responsibility.
1. Conditions- Faith in God- God's divine sovereignty, loyal submission to him, and trust that he will show us mercy for sake of our redeemer Jesus Christ should be acknowledged. Those who fear the Lord receive his forgiveness. Genuine sorrow over sin and true regret over violating God's law shows the brokenness of heart. 
2. Means- Sometimes Christians fail to distinguish between means of grace and basis of grace. The basis of grace is the merit of Christ. The tool is prayer and means of grace is faith. Prayer is an ordinary means for appealing to God for grace and forgiveness. We can receive forgiveness by asking for it with a broken heart. Prayer of intercession acts as extra ordinary means of forgiveness. Sacraments, which refer to Lord's supper and baptism, become means to ask for forgiveness.

Faith is the means of initial salvation, it is a tool that God uses to apply salvation to sinful individuals. There is nothing in our faith that deserves or earns salvation. On the contrary Christ freely gives us salvation through faith.
It is God's gracious act by which he forgives our sins. And it changes our status forever.

The good works that follows are the first evidences of our salvation since they can only be motivated by a genuine saving faith.

Saving faith involves our hearts. creating within us an inward desire to think, speak and act in ways that pleases God
Spending more time in the Word, meditating on God's promises with continual repentance on daily basis with genuine faith and commitment - helps us to grow spiritually in faith in our salvation journey, motivating us to grow form the point from where we began. This growth is visible both internally and externally.

True faith characterizes us to good works, through out our lives and with the guidance of the Holy Spirit - the equation changes completely, because it is God who works in our life to do his good will.

God created human beings to consist of physical bodies and non physical souls, as according to Hebrews 4.12 and 1 Thessalonians 5.23. Before our fall into the sin, our bodies and our souls were unaffected by sin and its corrupting powers. But when Adam and Eve fell into sin, sin corrupted not only their souls, but also their bodies. And this corruption of their bodies ultimately resulted in their physical death. 
When Adam and Eve sinned against God, he cursed them both with that they would be mortal. They would die and return to dust. Since all human beings descend from Adam and Eve, we all are born with similar corruption. 
Sin affected Adam and Eve in both spiritual and physical ways. Our souls come into the world in a state that Bible describes as spiritual death. We are all under God's judgement and have lost all ability to please him. This corruption results in physical hardship, sickness and eventually death, as said in Romans 6.12-19 and 7.4-25. Sin therefore, corrupts all that we are- our entire being, body and soul.

The three stages of redemption is as follows,
1. Present Life;- Salvation of our bodies begins with the indwelling of the Holy Spirit. Bible teaches that salvation of our bodies begins when we come to faith, with the indwelling of Holy Spirit. and our bodies continue to benefit through it, by the process of sanctification. Sanctification of our bodies is similar to the sanctification of our souls.
2. Intermediate State- During this state, our souls dwell with Christ in heaven while our bodies remain on earth. When we die, our bodies are temporarily separated from our souls. Our bodies are still corrupted by sin, as proven by the fact that they can decay. But the sin that corrupts them can no longer influence us to commit sin.
3. New Life- Our bodies will receive new, perfect life when they are restored to life in the general resurrection. In the resurrection, the consequences of sin will finally and forever be completely put away from us.

Imagination refers to our ability to form mental images of things beyond our experience. Imaginative abilities are vital to learning and thinking about God the world and ourselves

To study further we need to consider three factors that affect imagination

CREATIVITY
Imagination is a form of creativity, it involves in everything we make or create. We use imagination on our day to day lives and in many creative ways.
Imagination is involved in everything we make or create. Scientists use thier imaginations to come up with theories and ways of testing them. 

For instance in the old testament we read about Nathan the prophet confronting King David using an imaginary situation, and he asks David to draw a conclusion on that situation.

TIME
Time is another important factor, since we have to consider that Jesus Christ is no longer on earth teaching his disciples, we have to consider the period in which all these events happened in history. We have to draw out our imaginations accordingly. Bible requires us to pursue goals for the future in glorification of God through the triumph of his kingdom. But since these events are yet to happen, we have to figure out the best means to use to reach this goal and this cannot happen unless we imagine the future. 

DISTANCE
Most of the historical places mentioned in the Bible are places which we have never seen for ourselves, but we need to imagine those places and study the scriptures with regards to the context and place. When people and things are so far rom beyond our range of senses, we cannot have it as part of experience, but instead we need to use our imaginations to think about the place they lived in and the situation around them. We have to strongly rely on the Holy Spirit to evaluation our imagination according to God's word and then to harmonize it with our abilities to understand and study the Scripture further.

Assessing knowledge is an important step in the process of making ethical decisions, it can be divided into three categories
Reason
Conscience
Emotions 

REASON :
Reason is defined as the capcity to make logical inferences. 
As a Christian, right reasoning is the ability to think in orderly ways and to make judgements in accordance with biblical pattern
Reasoning enables us to make sense of the situation, both by helping us understand the facts and to compare these facts with the word of God. All the knowledge that we acquire through sensory experience requires a measure of reasoning. 
Jesus taught us that since God feeds the birds, which have little value, how much more will he feed his people who have more value.
Scripture uses reasons all the time and it calls us to do the same. It constantly present logical, moral arguments.

CONSCIENCE 
It is God given ability to discern both good and evil. It is also referred to as the sense of conviction that our thoughts, words and deeds are either pleasing or offensive to God.
Conscience enables us to assess the knowledge we have acquired and to judge it against the standard of God's word. It approves us when we believe we are acting in accord with God's word and it condemns us when we believe we are violating God's word.

EMOTIONS
Emotions are inner feelings, they are affective in our ethincal sensitivity.
Emotions are God given human abilities that enable us to assess our knowledge in many diferent ways. Our emotions are the initial interpretation of the facts.
Our emotions can be very useful tools for determining how God's word applies to our lives
Feeling of compassion can result in helping those in need
Anger can persuade us to follow pursuing justice
Experiences of Joy can enable us to affirm God's goodnees even in difficult times
Feeling of guilt can alert us to times we have fallen into sin

Will is the capacity for making decisions, it is our ability to make choices. 
When we consider our will, it is to view our entire decision making process from the perspective of the choices that we make, especially from the perspective of the final outcome.

For Christians this eans that while Holy Spirit enables us to make decisions that please God, there is always the possiblity that indwelling sin will persuade us to make sinful decisions. 

Our will may be neither active nor passive. We make decisions in a passive unconscious manner wuch as by force or habit. But at other times the ethical questions we face require reflection and conscious decisions.

There are many other ethical issues that we handle in a passive manner such as those that we deal with habitually or we respond to in a reflective manner.

If we really need to please our Lord, we must submit our will to him at every turn. We must will that God's word commands and we must allow the Holy Spirit working within us to influence our will.

The word derives from Greek words related to the verb hermeneuo, which means ''interpret'' or ''explain.'' Hermeneutics refers to the interpretation or explanation of some kind of message or communication. 
Freiedrich Schleiermarcher [1768-1834] is the father of modern hermeneutics. In 1819 he spoke of the need for ''general hermeneutics'',a unified theory for understanding all literature. 
Biblical hermeneutics is the study of interpreting the meaning and significance of Scripture. Informal approaches to the Bible are of great value, and these lessons will build on what most of us already understand. But we'll also move beyond informal hermeneutics and explore the kinds of issues that move to the foreground in academic, scholarly interpretation of the Bible.

The biblical roots of scientific hermeneutics make it a legitimate exercise. People living in biblical times weren't modern scientist. But this doesn't mean that they were unintelligent or irrational. On the contrary, their sophisticated architectural accomplishments, extensive maritime travel, innovative agricultural programs, and countless other cultural achievements demonstrate that people in biblical days dealt with facts and thought rationally about the world, much like modern scientists do.
For this reason, Biblical authors interpreted other scriptures with an orientation toward factual and logical analysis [Romans 4.3-5]. As this one example illustrates, time and again biblical authors presented this kind of careful interpretation of scripture. And their approach to Scripture indicates that scientific biblical hermeneutics is firmly rooted in the Scriptures themselves.

Devotional hermeneutics is the Christian tradition of emphasizing our need to draw near to God as we interpret the scriptures. Devotional hermeneutics focuses primarily on the divine authorship of scripture. Christians have acknowledged that the human words of scripture are also word of God. As 2 Timothy 3.16 tells us, the scriptures were inspired by God, or more literally were ''God-breathed.'' This fact makes biblical hermeneutics distinct from other facets of general hermeneutics because we must interpret the scriptures devotionally, as the living God himself. The biblical authors approached the scriptures devotionally. Followers of Christ are to read the scriptures as the word of God, in the presence of God, in ways that bring about extraordinary even supernatural experiences of God.

There are two important aspects of organic inspiration that helps us orient ourselves to task of interpretation ; first, the fact that the Holy Spirit was the divine source of scripture, and second the fact that he worked through human means to produce scripture. 
1] Divine Source- The Holy Spirit has intimate knowledge of the Bible's meaning and of the way it communicates that meaning. One of the most important implications of the divine origin of scripture is the Bible's unquestionable veracity. 
     a] Critical Interpreter - Reject the divine divine inspiration of scripture and elevate their understanding over the spirit's authority
     b] Submissive interpreter- affirm the divine inspiration of scripture, expecting and assuming it to be true and harmonious even when they can't demonstrate or prove its truthfulness.
2] Human Means- God had the scripture composed by means if human authors. The Scriptures were written by different people, and they reflect the diversity of that human authorship.

Illumination
The Holy Spirit grants us knowledge of His word. And this knowledge isn't purely cognitive.  It also imparts our imagination, intuition, emotion, will, motivation, desire, moral conscience- any part of us that contributes to our understanding of scripture can be illumined by the our understanding of scripture can be illumined by the Spirit. Human beings are so deeply affected by sin that we can't understand the things of God on our own. We desperately need God himself- the Holy Spirit- to illumine us. Without the work of the Spirit, we have no hope of grasping the thoughts of God as we should. This is why the Spirit's personal illumination is so important to our interpretation of the Scriptures.

Location
Both the New Testament and early church fathers suggest that James lived his life of ministry in Jerusalem. And he remained in Jerusalem until he was martyred in A. D 62, so there is no reason to think that he wrote the epistle from any other location.
Date
Acts 12:17 indicates that James became a significant leader of the Jerusalem church by the time of Peter;s release from prison. According to Acts 12:19-23, Peter was released in the year Herod Agrippa I died in A.D 44. So this letter was not written much before this date. 
Second possible date for the epistle is A. D 62, the year of James martyrdom.

Investigating the original meaning of a biblical passage involves exploring the text as if it were still within the historical circumstances of its writer and first audience. This kind of exploration requires a lot of research, careful thinking and imagination. In other words, it requires a lot of human effort because biblical documents no longer exist in their original settings. Bible is organically inspired by God. The Holy Spirit chose to communicate his word through the personalities, experiences, emotion and patterns of thought of human biblical writers. And there are several places in the Bible where the importance of the human writers is mentioned explicitly. 
The Holy Spirit chose to communicate his word through human writers. Focusing on the human writer helps us understand many features of Scripture. Human writer helps us understand many features of scripture. Scripture demonstrates how important it is for us to focus not just on God as the ultimate author of Scripture, but also on the human writers he inspired. And that means that we have to learn as much as we can about the situations, personalities, experiences, skills and intentions of these writers.

The Holy Spirit inspired human authors to write scripture. The doctrine of organic inspiration extends only to the original texts of scripture, only those documents have the full authority of God himself. The changes that have taken place in these texts as they have been copied over the centuries are not inspire by God, and neither are the translations of those texts. Responses to objections made about copies and translations of Scripture. 
The original documents of the Old Testament didn't exist in Jesus' day. Jesus and his apostles believed that the scriptures that had were trustworthy. When we interpret the Bible, we are the subjects, and the object of our study is the Bible. Three major approaches towards the object and subjects of knowledge are, 
First, some people tend toward an approach we call objectivism. Objectivists believe that under the right circumstances, it's possible to arrive at impartial or objective knowledge. 
Second, other people tend toward an approach called subjectivism. Subjectivists believe that our knowledge is always influenced by our personal biases, making impartial objectivity impossible. 
And third, some people have found a middle ground that we might call dialogism. This approach emphasizes the constant ''dialog'' or interplay between objective reality and our subjective perspectives. All three of these approaches have been used in biblical interpretation.

Scientific Rationalism; Objectivism can be identified with the most prominent current in the stream of modern philosophy- the current we'll call scientific rationalism. Rene Descartes, who lived from 1596 to 1650, is often called the father of modern rationalism because he promoted reason as the supreme judge of truth. Francis Bacon [1561- 1626], the father of modern science, applied rational, logical thinking to the study of the physical world.
Structuralism; Structuralists tried to use rational and scientific objectivity to obtain an exhaustive understanding of everything they studied. The concepts of rationality and science have changed in a variety of ways. But the fundamental assumption of objectivism has remained the same, specifically; by following rational scientific analysis, we can arrive at objective knowledge. In the twentieth century, modern objectivism was taken to the extreme by broad philosophical outlook known as structuralism. Structuralists tried to use rational and scientific objectivity to obtain an exhaustive understanding of everything they studied- including sociology, art, language and literature.

1. Authority dialog and objective- Objective and subjective approaches to meaning oppose each other in some fundamentals ways, but they have something very important in common. In the extremes, both models ultimately make the authority of interpreters equal to or even greater than the authority of the Bible itself. Objectivism tends to over estimate how reliable to our rational and scientifically objective views are. Subjectivism tends to overestimate how reliable our personal intuitions and opinions are. But in both cases the result is the same; I acknowledge that objective truth can be found in text of scripture. The authority- dialog model helps us avoid thinking that we can be utterly objective when we approach the scriptures. 
2. Authority- Dialog and Subjective- The authority dialog model resembles objective models in some ways, it also has similarities with subjective models. It acknowledges that we all come to the Scriptures with perspectives and beliefs that influence the way we interpret biblical passages. Moreover, it agrees with scripture and subjectivism that the personal, subjective input we bring to interpretation is valuable. If we don't submit our subjectivity to the authority of scripture, our interpretations of the Bible will be severely hindered. Investigating the bible is a lifelong process in which Scripture  changes us and causes to grow and mature in our Christian faith.
