There are several fundamental connections between the Old Testament and New Testament churches and they all are driven with the same purpose, group of  people and obligations.

 To begin with the purpose, the purpose has never changed between the church of the Old Testament and the New Testament. The history of the world can be summed up in three stages, between the creation, the fall and redemption. Beginning with the creation of the world, man and animals by God. He formed man and the beautiful garden of Eden, and following the creation, there was a mandate or ordinance to follow, and through the failure to abide by this, God has has now created the opportunity for man to redeem itself through redemption and restoration. 

 The goal of the gathering of Israel and the New Testament church remains the same and continues to be that their purpose is to turn the world into God's earthly kingdom. Simply put, the church has a moral purpose to convert the world and the people of this world to be a replica of the kingdom of God. The group of people gathering can also be identified within the implications of the Old Testament and New Testament church, the gathering of the assemblies should included both believers and unbelievers. 

We can clearly see this portrayed within the New Testament throughout several parables and teachings of Jesus as to how no one should be separated or go astray, and if one were to, then the it is our responsibility to bring them to Christ. Lastly, the obligations of the Old Testament and New Testament church are similar in nature. To love God, to spread and advance his kingdom, and to bring him glory.

The word catholic means, universal or including all Christians in all congregations. The reference is not to the Roman Catholic church, rather it is a description of unity that exists between all of the churches that follow Christ faithfully. When we speak of the Apostles' Creed and how it was understood within the creed, it is important to note that there is no organization of all Christian gatherings mentioned. Rather, the creed is referring to the unity of the Holy Spirit and how it should exist between all Christian churches, despite any organizational difference. The term catholic is meant to be inclusive and include  all Christians in all congregations. 

The term catholic is derived from the Latin word, catholicus which means whole or complete. Meanwhile the latter churches were fragmented by divisions and strife, reversing the original intention and causing them to be exclusive. However the creed has the original intention of the unity of the Holy spirit among the churches and continue the covenant with God and under the headship of Christ. In 1 Corinthians 1:2, Paul wrote in his teachings, "To the church of God in Corinth, to those sanctified in Christ Jesus and called to be holy, together with all those everywhere who call on the name of our Lord Jesus Christ - their Lord and ours." As it is mentioned, called to be holy and together in the name of our Lord and theirs can be a clear portrayal of how the church is to be viewed as universal. The creed refers to this as the catholicity of the church, where it does not have in mind a organization of ALL Christian gatherings, rather the unification of the Holy Spirit acknowledging the purpose to be holy and just advancing the kingdom of God among all churches.

The visible catholic church is defined as one worldwide fellowship of all people in covenant with God under the headship of Christ. The catholic church has distinct markers including the word, sacraments, and discipline. The means of grace considered as the tools or mechanisms that God would ordinarily use to apply grace to his people are measured through these three areas, word, sacraments and prayers. The visible catholic church also believes in spiritual gifts for the purpose of building up the church through the Holy Spirit. These spiritual gifts are shared by the entirety of the church through public worship services, sign for the unbelievers, building up the entire church and believing that unbelievers are condemned. The visible catholic church also believes in the sharing of material goods with one another who were in need during the early church and within the Bible. 

To decide which churches should be embraced as part of the catholic church or the universal church should be grounded within the word of God. There is no church, claim, interpretation or proclamation that has the exclusive right to interpret and teach the Scripture. God has given his word to the whole visible church and he has given the Holy Spirit to help us understand the Bible. 

This is a common problem faced today, to know which church should a believer embrace, the catholic church or the universal church of Christ. Either one churches opens their arms too wide and include any church that claims to be a Christian or the other is too exclusive and only accept narrowly defined congregations of denominations. The sacraments to administer and conduct baptism is given to the entire church, not just one denomination or another. Lastly, discipline is granted to all churches and not exclusive to a single denomination or congregation.

The problem of sin is that it takes us away from the blessings of God and places us under his curse. We are not able to overcome this problem on our own, and that is why Jesus had to die. He had to die in order to solve the problem created by our sin. Sin condemns us, we are unable to save ourselves through our own strength or might. Eventually we must suffer the consequences of the sin unless we believe in Jesus and are redeemed. Sin originated with the creation of the human race, and their eating of the of the forbidden fruit of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil. When God had created humankind, we were very good, however man had the ability and the opportunity to sin. 

At any point in time that a human being chooses to think, speak or act in anyway that differs from God's will and violates his law, we sin. We are choosing evil over good and there are dire consequences with sin. With the action of sin committed by both Adam and Eve, God judged and cursed the entire human race. That curse remains until this very day as a result of the corruption in our beings both body and soul. Ultimately the curse continues until death, the curse began as a result of the sin that entered the world through one man and through that sin, all of humankind were born as sinners. 

The main consequence associated with sin is the physical death we all know along with the spiritual death. That is the eternal separation from God and the Scripture teaches us that sin can cause God to hide his face from you so that he will not hear you. Creating that separation is no small fate, it is indeed  the factor that can cause someone to suffer in hell as a result of their separation from God.

Divine grace involves all three persons of the Trinity by first pointing out that God did not want all of the human race to remain under the curse of sin. He felt that humankind was sill worthy of this presence and planned to send a Redeemer to solve the awful problem of sin. The Redeemer is none other than Jesus Christ, the son of God. Forgiveness starts with the one who has the highest authority, our father, our heavenly father. The only way forgiveness came about was because the Father allowed it and planned for it come. The father is also the one who gave authority and empowered Jesus to come as his son to redeem his people. 

The Son, our redeemer, sent by the Father was to fulfill the Father's will and promise, which was to come into this world as a man and die for the sin of humankind. The curse that mankind brought upon themselves, death was taken up by the Son and credited to our own account. He was obedient to the Father and as the Son was punished for our sins. The father had to architect the entire plan and delegate the son to perform the will of the father. 

The Holy Spirit is the third person of the Trinity and is the one applying forgiveness in our lives. The Father was the one who orchestrated and laid out the plans, the Son was able to die for our sins and put the plan into motion, and the Holy Spirit is able to do his work and applies forgiveness in our lives.

Individual responsibility plays a role in the forgiveness of sins by two factors. The first is having the fear of the Lord which can receive his forgiveness. The Bible teaches us that God does not punish us according to our wrong doings and mistakes,  however we must acknowledge that the Lord is slow to anger, compassionate and gracious. He has the ability and authority to not treat us according to our sins. However, with that concept comes the fear of the Lord. If you set your hearts towards seeking him and seeing the true meaning of repentance and forgiveness, God is able to forgive. In a spirit of true brokenness, and repentance, we must be able to express the depth of our sorrow and regret to the king who is the only one able to forgive. 

We must strive to have faith in God, knowing that he is divine and acknowledging his grace. He is able to show mercy and forgiveness to those who fear him. When we do ask for forgiveness of sins, individual responsibility also means to show our brokenness. Our genuine remorse and guilt over the sin we have committed breaking God's law. Forgiveness can be granted through prayer, asking God for forgiveness. Meditate, seek God's face, pray or petition on behalf of one another in your individual responsibility. These are the methods to seek forgiveness of one's sins, rather than mistaking grace as a lifeline, we must understand that the basis is always the merit of Christ. We are able to  inherit this grace through his obedient life and sacrificial death on the cross for us. We are able to earn this forgiveness through this manner.

Man's fall into sin corrupted not only our souls but also our physical bodies as well. Human beings consist of two main parts, one being the human body, and the second being the soul. In Genesis 3:19, God placed a curse on mankind as a result of the sin committed by Adam and Eve, "By the sweat of your brow you will eat your food until you return to the ground, since from it you were taken; for dust you are and to the dust you will return." As a result of the sin of Adam and Eve, God cursed them to be mortal. Until then, they were not supposed to die. However, now the Bible shows us that God declared that they would eventually die and return to dust. This is a clear result of how man's fall into sin corrupted not only their souls, but their physical bodies too. 

God did not create us to die, that was never his intention. Our salvation will never be complete, until Christ returns and redeems our bodies. Death is inevitable, it is a universal human experience that everyone must face at one point in time or another. However, the way to view death is that we are taken directly into the presence of Christ.

As all human beings descend from Adam and Eve, all human kind were born with sin and corruption, and continue to carry that curse. The corruption of sin results in physical hardship, sickness and eventually death. In Psalm 90:10, the Bible refers to how even the greatest of days are filled with trouble and sorrow, the years quickly pass and we are gone. The wonderful promise that we get to hold onto though is that God is our salvation and Jesus died for ours sins. This allows for both our souls and bodies to be redeemed.

The three stages of bodily redemption are composed of the things believers experience during our current life on earth, the second is the intermediate state of our bodies that begins with physical death, and the last is the new life of resurrection which begins when Christ returns. 

According to the Scripture we will experience these three stages quite differently. To begin with the the current life on earth, we refer to redemption on earth with the belief that once we believe in Christ, we are sanctified, or set apart for God and purified. He is able to continue to sanctify us and use our bodies in ways that honor him, resulting in us giving our bodies to God as a living sacrifice. This is experienced as a result of the Holy Spirit. The Holy Spirit's indwelling presence throughout our lives allows our bodies to continue to benefit and live a life pleasing to the Lord. 

The second one we experience is the redemption of our bodies in the present life. The process of redemption continues even after we die, when are bodies are temporarily separated from our souls. This is the stage between life on earth and the lives we will have in resurrection, during this period is when our souls dwell with Christ in heaven. This is revealed in the Scripture in Matthew 17:3 and 2 Corinthians 5:6-8. Death frees the body from sin, while the body may be returning to dust and decaying, our bodies are in a state where they are incapable of any thought, action, or feeling whether it may be good or bad. Whether our bodies are buried or cremated, our bodies continue to  be a part of us. 

The last experience is the new life of resurrection that begins when Christ returns. With the resurrection comes the relief that the consequences of sin will finally and forever be completely put away from us. Our bodies will receive a new and perfect life which allows for a glorious life that allows for perfected human beings. Just as Jesus body had gone through changes in resurrection, our bodies will also be changed and we will finally become the people that God had always intended for us to be.

During the week of creation, one of the things that is taught by Scripture is that when God, the Father was creating the world, God the Son was beside the Father. The Scripture also reveals that the Father created the world through his Son. The role of God the Father was that once the world was created, all of dominium and ownership would be given to Son to inherit and rule over it's entire creation. 

In the book of Colossians, 1:6 we read, "For by him all things were created: things in heaven and on earth, visible and invisible, all things were created by him and for him." Therefore the passage implies that everything that God the Father had created was indeed for God the Son and created with the Son. The Scripture is very clear on the fact that God the Father was the overall designer of the world. He was able to create the world through his ways of what would please him. For example, after each creation, the Scripture states that "God saw that it was good" and he was pleased with what he had created. So for six days, God filled a void, shapeless, world without light to become full of creation, shape, light, sea, land, animals and vegetation. 

During the first three days of creation, God the father began to create and fill the world in ways that would be pleasing to him. He formed the world, and allowed there to be light. He separated the sky from the sea and the dry land from water. During the next three days, God the created the sun, moon and stars. He assigned the sun to rule the day and the moon to rule the night. He created the fish, the birds, and all of the animals that live on Earth. 

At the end of the creation week, God the Father had completed his kingdom. He then appointed humankind to govern over the Earth so that they could bring him glory. God did this with the authority of keeping the God the Son as the heir of all things that was the king of all of the earth who would inherit, and rule over the entire creation.

God's eternal counsel regarding Christ is that humankind has a purpose and redemption is available only through Jesus Christ. The Bible teaches us clearly the purpose that man was created in the Old Testament in the beginning of time. When God designed and Adam and then Eve to have authority over the Earth and gave them free will, they chose to dishonor and disobey God which then allowed for the infamous curse to fall upon them and all of mankind. The ultimate consequence around their sin has been passed down since then leading to death. However, God the Father allowed for his Son to die for our sins, to allow for redemption to take place. 

This redemption has created a hope for humanity. God the Father promised he would send a Redeemer, who we know as his Son. The Redeemer would bring salvation to the sinner and be able to restore the world as well as bring judgement. Jesus will return only at a time that is known to his Father and will return in the same manner that he ascended into Heaven and it will be public and visible for all to see. He will return as a powerful conqueror and all those who have ever died will be resurrected and the last judgement will take place. God the Father gives us this counsel that Jesus will destroy all his enemies and allow the blessing of all of his faithful people. No human being will be exempt from judgement, and sinner will be purged and creation will be renewed. This will then allow for all of creation to be restored to the original plan of God.

The divine promises that made redemption certain can be traced back to the very beginning. If God has declared a promise, that promise remains as he does not ever change. The world may come and go, but the word of God will remain the same forever and ever. We are taught that God's promises are immutable and he will never break them. Regarding redemption, the divine promises that are made fall in line with the original plan of God. That man is to live on earth as it is the kingdom of heaven and the promises that are rooted between the Father and Son will come to pass. The covenant of redemption which is the promise to redeem fallen humanity will take place and secure redemption after the fall into sin. 

There are several examples of promises or covenants that were made which ensure redemption is certain. The initial covenant of redemption is where the Father, Son and Holy Spirit promised to redeem fallen humanity, the covenant of Grace is the arrangement between the Father and Son and redeemed humanity. There were other examples of promises that ensured redemption such as the Adamic Covenant where redemption was offered to humanity when it was not deserved. The Noahic Covenant which promised to preserve humanity until the Son's redeeming work was fulfilled. The Abrahamic Covenant which promised that one of Abraham's descendants would be the Redeemer. 

These examples provide us with the assurance that the promises made by God is eternal and unchangeable. There is no refuting any of the other examples mentioned in the Bible whether it be the Mosaic, Davidic, or New Covenant. These are all examples of how promises surrounding redemption and the covenant between God and mankind were fulfilled and continues to this day.

Jesus was able to accomplish redemption for sinners through his redeeming work by a few different examples. The first example that we can see is through his inauguration of his kingdom. The people of God yearned for the day and time when God would bring his kingdom to earth. Jesus was able to bring the kingdom of God to earth in his day. Which ultimately reveals that we as children of God are still waiting for the kingdom of God. 

Another major example of how Jesus was able to accomplish redemption for sinners was through the obedience and submission to the will of the Father to step in where Adam had failed. Jesus was put through an immense period of humiliation, suffering and ultimately crucifixion and took the place of man to suffer and sacrifice on the cross for one purpose. This freed man from God's condemnation allowing the reward of salvation to be given to us. Through the resurrection of Christ, Jesus conquered death and secured everlasting life for his people. This is the work that Jesus had done for the redemption of sinner, he came into this world, took the place of man, died for their sins, ascended into heaven after his resurrection and promised us salvation. That salvation was paid for on the cross so that we can have eternal life.

The crucial events that Jesus will initiate at the consummation revolve around the end times. The consummation consists of the destruction of all of God's enemies and the ultimate blessing of all his people. This will be the complete renewal of all of creation where the children of God will dwell forever. This will be fulfillment of Gods kingdom finally coming to pass. 

The first crucial event that will initiate the consummation will be the return of Jesus. During his return he will come down from heaven as he went and his return will be public and visible. All will see him and there will be a loud noise from a trumpet and the voice of an archangel. He will come back as a powerful conqueror, and it will be sudden. The timing of his return is only known to God the father.

During Christ's return, all who have died will be resurrected and everyone will be given new bodies that will be endured forever. Our final bodies will be glorious, however the bodies of those who are not redeemed and non-believers will last forever and their bodies will continue to be plagued by the curse of God. 

The last judgement will be exercised by Jesus overall of mankind. He will destroy all his enemies and bless all the faithful people at the last judgement. No one will be able to escape the final judgement. After the last judgement, the final major event that will take place is the renewal of creation. Jesus will judge all of humanity and purge the sinners and those who did not believe and those who do believe will inherit everlasting life in the kingdom of God.

Peter's apostolic confession along with the transfiguration affirms that Jesus was the Christ. Jesus would come to Earth in a unique way that could only be manifested by God the Father alone. Jesus was born to a virgin woman who remained a virgin until she had given birth to Jesus. Through the miraculous intervention of the Holy Spirit, Jesus was born as a true human. 

While Jesus was on Earth, his identity was confirmed by the teachings of the apostles through the miraculous works that he had performed that were specially anointed by God. The miracles demonstrated a strong approval of God's anointing and approval of everything that Jesus had said. Jesus was able to prove that the gospel message was true through miracles and that he wanted to bring the last stage of God's kingdom to earth. Apostolic teachings confirm in Luke 11:20, "If I drive out demons by the finger of God, then the kingdom of God has come to you." The works and miracles performed by Jesus proved that he was Christ and he had come to put an end to Satan's rule over the people of God and his creation. 

At the time of the transfiguration, Jesus was revealed in his glory to his disciples. At that time, Jesus had taken Peter, James and John up to a mountain to intercede and pray. Two men appeared to be with Jesus at that time, both Moses and Elijah. The voice of God the father was heard from heaven at that time and confirmed that Jesus was his son. This was a direct correlation to the affirmation of Jesus being Christ during the time of the transfiguration.

The purpose of Jesus' temptation in the wilderness was to prove that although Jesus took the form of man, he was able to overcome temptation and bring salvation to his people. During this time of temptation, Jesus was fasting for forty days, which means for forty days he disconnected with the world and the required daily consumption of the world so that he connect with God. This time was a period where Jesus would be weak in his physical body, but he continued to remain powerful in both his spirit and mind. 

During this time, Satan took it upon himself to tempt Jesus and wanted to test the limits to see where Jesus would fail. However Jesus failed to give into the tricks of the devil and refused to prove himself. One of the greatest lessons to be taken from the time of temptation of Jesus was that this similar temptation occurred during the days of Adam and Eve. While God had created man and woman, the serpent came and tricked Eve into eating from the tree of knowledge and evil. Eve was not able to sustain her focus on what is pure and moral, but rather fell into the strong temptation of sin. Jesus on the other hand, was able to come into this world, born of a woman and was able to fight through the temptations known to man, which the devil brings upon us, and was able to withstand these temptations whereas Adam and Eve were not able to do. 

Jesus had a greater plan and vision which drove the path forward to salvation for all of humanity. That was to take the sinful path of man, the failures of each test and temptation that humankind failed at, and to redeem all people, the entire human race and bring salvation to his people. Jesus was sinless and did not fall into sin, rather, he  bore the sin and became our substitute so that we did not have to perish. That is why it was necessary for him to be tempted and to show us that he was able to overcome those temptations and save us.

The crucifixion of Jesus was very unique to say, at the very least. During the days of the ancient Roman Empire, crucifixion was when victims were condemned to die, tied to a cross, or at times, nailed to the cross and required to hang on the cross until they died. Around the cross, you would find skulls, and extreme temperatures and birds of the sky looking to peck and eat these wounded flesh. 

The reason that Jesus' crucifixion was unique was because it served as an atoning offering for sin. For Jesus, it was his responsibility to die on behalf of his people. God had appointed Jesus to be the substitute on our behalf for his people and was assigned to take on the guilt of sinners. If we take a look back at the life of Adam and Eve, as a result of their sin and fall into temptation and sin, they were condemned to die as a result, and have a time frame on their on Earth. Death is considered as a judgement against sin, death was not to be there, until sin crept in and caused that sin to be passed on from generation to generation. The death of Jesus was a divine judgement against sin, where Jesus paid our ransom and sacrificed himself per the will of the Father to stand for us. 

His death was unique in the way that he was blamed for our sins even though he never committed any wrong doing. His human physical form was never corrupted by sin , yet God counted Jesus as if he had personally committed each crime and sin committed by man. That is what makes his death and crucifixion so unique. A blameless and perfect man, was punished so harshly for something he did not do, and was assigned a guilty verdict to stand in place of us.

The resurrection of Jesus accomplished a few different things. The first thing that the resurrection accomplished was that Jesus Christ conquered death for everyone. When he was able to rise up from the dead, and out of the grave through the power of the Holy Spirit, he was able to prove to all of humanity that he is who he said he was and that he was the true Son of God. This also ensured another thing, which was taught by Jesus several times, the final resurrection to believers and his faithful followers. 

The Scripture teaches us in many different passages about redemption and the promises of God through salvation. When Jesus was resurrected, we can see that he was able to redeem all of humanity and that nothing else would be able to save them. He created the manifestation of his promise of eternal life after death if you believe in him. Another thing we learn from the resurrection of Jesus is that he was able to show us that we are forgiven as he bore the shame and torture for us. He was able to take on human form, live on this earth and be persecuted and tortured for something he didn't do. This resulted in his death and eventually his resurrection, which shows us that he took on that guilt and bore that punishment for our salvation so that we can be forgiven for our wrongdoings. 

The plan of resurrection was to fulfill the promise of God, which was to establish his kingdom on Earth and redeem his people. As a part of this blessing of salvation, and through his resurrection, we received an eternal inheritance, justification, regeneration, and salvation for believers.

I am able to affirm without a doubt and confess that Jesus is the Christ in my present circumstances and areas of influence clearly by admitting that I have no power, authority or dominion over anything in my life. Looking back to specific instances in my life, I was in places of high distinction and blessings of many sorts, but through the highs and lows, and through many examples, I was able to lose practically everything in my life. Only after complete surrender and proclaiming that Jesus has complete control over my life, did I see the hand of God piecing everything back together again. 

There are many real life examples within my life, where I have sinned, and I have fallen short and I have missed the mark. There are also examples of where I have tried my level best as a human being to achieve certain things, but I have learned through personal failures and struggles that without Jesus being at the center of my life, I am not able to  take a single step in the right direction. Jesus has complete authority over my life, whether it be my family, marriage, career, ministry, without the hand of God over my life and these areas, I fail. I have tasted it and witnessed it with a front row seat. There are no good works and words that can save me and give me any satisfaction, but knowing that I walk with God and he has me in the palm of his hand, gives me the relief that there is nothing that can't be done without him. 

He has literally pieced my life back together again, stitched it so beautifully and allowed for my blessings to multiply and shut the mouth of the devil that tried to destroy me. There was  time when I was not able to stand against the blows that the devil brought against me, and through each blow, I realized at the end that Jesus bore my sins on the cross and fought the battle for me. I don't need to fight this battle, I need to surrender and give it to God. When I did that is when I realized who God was and is in my life. And in all areas of my life and areas of influence, I was able to see the work and hand of God in my life. He was able to do things that not I or any human could do, and as a result of what he did, my testimony continues to be a beacon of hope for many, that God lives and he is still in the business of redemption.

In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God and the Word was God.  The Word was God and that means since the beginning, before the universe was created. The Son Jesus Christ is the radiance of God's glory and the exact representation of his being,sustaining all things by his powerful word. In Colossians 1:16, the writer mentions that for by him all things were created, everything visible and invisible, all things created by him and for him.  God formed and gave shape to the world through Logos which is the power of his word.  God created man in his own image male and female to be fruiful and subdue the earth.  God the Son was active in creation in that he was the heir of all things.  The purpose of creation is to serve as Gods special kingdom.  Trinity thus has a significant role in all creation, because everything was void until God spoke into it. One of the known facts of our Christian faith is Jesus not only redeems us, but he is also more the Creator and the Redeemer.  The whole universe we can consider governed by the Logos of God.  Every created thing is obligated to submit obediently  to God as Son as its King.  The heart of Jesus goes to all of Creation.

Jesus Christ is a distinct person of the Trinity until the New Testament.  Scripture teaches that Jesus has been God from all of eternity.  Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today and forever.  Jesus' divine nature is true in various ways.  God knew everything was going to happen before it did. When Jesus comes back he wil reign as king over the kingdom of God and bring it reverance.  This refers to God's eternal plan for the universe which happened before creation started.  There are various theological beliefs about the nature and extent of God's plan.  Some think that God's eternal plan are meticulous with every historical fact and others say God fixed certain things and not others.  We all believe one thing that what Christ accomplished is central to God's plan, we will all have salvation through Jesus Christ.  Ephesian 1:4 and 11 says God chose us in Christ before the creation of the world to be holy and blameless in his sight, in him we were also chosen, having been predestined according to the plan of him who works out everything in conformity with the purpose of his will. God created the universe in order to display his increasing glory through us his creation. Some theologians have found it helpful to describe Gods eternal decree regarding his glorious kingdom as a covenant of redemption.

God's promises are immutable which will never change.  All of fallen humanity would be redeemed through each individual of the Trinity.  The covenant of grace was an agreement that God the Father on one hand, and the Son and the redemption of humanity on the other hand.  In this covenantial agreement, God the Father vowed to ensure his kingdom plans for creation through Jesus his Son.  In Genesis chapter 2 we read how God had vowed to kill humanity if they ate the forbidden fruit, but God showed his mercy. God did something even greater by promising a Redeemer which many call the first gospel and it was found in the curse God gave the snake after Adam and Eve had sinned.  God made a promise that one day the generation of the woman would be able to rescue all of humanity. The Redeemer was sent to crush the Serpent's head was to come to the rescue of all of humankind from sin that was committed.  The Redeemer came to restore a good and right relationship with God the Father.

John 3:16-18 states this that God so loved the world that he gave his one and only Son, that whoever believes in him shall not perish but have eternal life.  For God did not send his Son into the world to condemn the world, but to save the world through him.  Whoever believes in him is not condemned, but whoever does not believe stands condememned already because he has not believed in the name of God's one and only Son.  Jesus died on the cross of Calvary for my sins, and he conquered death and the enemy so that I wouldnt have to face that.  Jesus motive was for creation to fulfill Gods purpose.  Through what Jesus did on the cross and his resurrection, he was establishing the kingdom of God, showing his love to the Father in obedience.  The Bible says that we were hopeless, without direction, unable to solve the problem of sin and so God the Son becomes a man, lives out a life of complete submission to God.  Jesus represents the resurrected redeemed life.  Jesus represents the new man, the new Adam which has been redeemed from its sinful ways.  The ascension of Jesus allowed him to be our mediator in heaven.  We have salvation in no one else other than Christ Jesus!

The consuming of the heavens and the earth is about Jesus second coming and the final stage of salvation.  In this time all of God's enemies will be destroyed, it will be where there is a renewal of creation.   This is when the world will finally be God's glorious kingdom.  Jesus's first appearance back showed great humility.  1 Thesalonians 4:16 states that the Lord himself will come down from heaven, with a loud command with the voice of the archangel and with the trumpet call of God.  This scripture indicates how Jesus will return, it will be clearly evident and he will return in the same manner that he left.  The second coming will be victorious.  The scripture also says that his return will be imminent, it will never happen when we think it will.  At Jesus' return, everyone that died will be resurrected, he is going to tranform our lowly bodies into his glorious body which Philippians 3:20-21 states.  Judgement will also happen immediately after the resurrection, every person alive will be included in the last judgement. When Jesus comes back he will reward our devotion to him, all those who have been faithful will receive the new heavens and earth and we will be able to enjoy God's presence in a even better way than what Adam and Eve had in Eden.

When all the disciples were asked who Jesus was, some of them said Elijah, some said Moses, but Peter was the only one that confirmed he was the messiah, the Son of God.  This was clearly given to Apostle Peter through the Holy Spirit.  The transfiguration was the revealing of the glory of God through Jesus Christ, where Christ was so bright.  God mentioned at the transfiguration that Jesus was completing the guidelines set by people of leadership in the past of Israel.  The voice of God on this mountain of transfiguration confirmed that Jesus was the second part of the Trinity.

The purpose of Jesus' temptation was to overcome the enemy.  We see that Jesus was fasting for 40 days, he was famished and this is when the Holy Spirit takes him to the wilderness to be tempted by the devil.  Jesus was frail at this time, very vulnerable, he could have gave in to the enemy but he overcame through the word of God orating to the devil.  This proves that Jesus was truly human as well as divine, he had the same tendencies that we as humans have today.  He proved that we can overcome temptation unlike Adam and Eve in the Garden of Eden. Jesus gave us the example on how to overcome temptation by never giving in to the devil.

Crucifixion was the ultimate penalty given in Roman times.  The wooden cross was used as well as nails to put criminals to a gruesome death.  The uniqueness of the crucifixon of Jesus is that he took the place of my sins, he was sinless but paid the ultimate price for me.  Jesus paid it all on the cross, to him I owe, sin left a crimson stain on him, in essence he paid the ultimate sacrifice so never again will any animals have to be slaughtered for my shortcomings as they used to do in the Old Testament times.   His death shows us that he took our judgement on his shoulders!

Jesus resurrection from the dead crushed the enemy's head.  The devil thought the grave could hold Jesus, but it couldnt, this was God the Father's plan all along.  God desired for all of creation to redeemed, his promises wouldnt come true unless Jesus was raised from the dead.  Jesus's resurrection also shows us as Christians what we have to look forward to at the second coming which is the glorious body promises us.  We as Christians no longer have to fear death because Christ conquered it and we have a hope that when the roll is called up, I'll be there in eternity with my Lord!

I affirm that Jesus Christ is in my life by always maintaining a good relationship with him daily.  I am able to walk differently since I know that Christ is in control of my life in every aspect of my life.  In my career, I am able to display the love of God through my words, my deeds and just displaying Gods glory in everything that I do.  I can express Christ via social media platforms just as facebook and instagram which I am currently doing to encourage those around me.  Even in bad times or good times, I am able to have a smile on my face and be positive that God is omniscient, omnipotent, and is sovereign in every circumstance of my life.  In ministry as a minister to students, I am able to be a role model with my wife by being an example in behaviors and actions as well as being present for all those that need me around me.  I affirm that Jesus is my Lord and Savior every morning that I get up, by devoting everything I have for his kingdom cause. My wife and I are able to have small groups weekly with young couples where we encourage each other, we build each other up, have fellowship and in the end pray for each others needs and this is how we are able to influence others.

Many believe that Paul was not the author of Hebrews because he never introduces himself in the book.  Many theologians today reject that Paul was the author because again Paul disliked plagiarism and would make sure that in each of the epistles to introduce himself.  In the Epistles that Apostle Paul wrote he does not refer to Old Testament very much but the writer of Hebrews is different and mentions the tabernacle as well as the High Priest.  The writer has a different way of words that relate to a Greek upbringing which is quite different from the letters that Paul wrote.

There are five characteristics of the original audience of Hebrews.  The author of Hebrews is probably talking to a Jewish crowd due to mentioning generations past and how God spoke through various men of God.  In the first verse of Hebrews it refers to forefathers and a revelation. The 2nd is that it may have been written to a group outside of Palestine which were sound in doctrine. In chapter 2 of Hebrews the writer mentions many who heard from Christ directly and passed it on to future generations.  Third the audience needed to be taught and was probably ignorant as well as childish based on the way it was written.  Fourth we can see that the audience may have been under constant attacks by political leadership at the time.  The writer mentions sufferings and not to throw away their faith in Chapter 10.  The fifth and main thing the author is pointing out is that the problems the church faced was enabling them to turn away from Jesus.  The writer supports the 5th characteristic by pointing out that they were intentionally sinning even after knowing what is right, judgement would be coming.

The Book of Hebrews is a huge sermon to the church and its approach was to persuade dramatically.  The writer is presenting his side like a debate and doing his best to convice the readers to sway to what he is preaching. He mentions the supremacy of Jesus as it relates to the Old Testament priest in Melchizidek. There are many analogies between Christ and the High Priest in the Old Testament and his defense is that Jesus is the ultimate High Priest. The author shows many pictures by mentioning the hall of faith in chapter of 11 of great men and women of God that deserved to stand out for their faith.  The writer is mentionining Old Testament law and how people were punished than and comparing that to of rejecting Christ and making the reader understand how essential it is to acknowledge Jesus as the High Priest.

Some areas in my spritual life where I need to work on is keeping a check on spritual arrogance.  I always have to ensure that I stay humble in every aspect of my spritual walk.  Another area that I need to work on maturing my spiritual walk is respecting my spiritual leadership and being receptive to be shaped under their tutorship.  Just like with Hebrews, I need to be willing to be taught, being open to correction by my spiritual shepherd is something that I am working on and have learned a lot over the last decade.  Another area in my life that need maturity on is being able to forgive completely like Jesus did and not holding any grudges.  These are areas I am constantly in prayer about as well as asking God to give me grace to overcome to be very effective in ministry.

The false teachings that I may face is that once I accept Christ as my Savior there will be no more challenges.  This is a false teaching that prosperity comes after making a decision to follow Christ.  Another false teaching that I face is believing that once saved is always saved and taking scripture out of context when it comes to not having any condemnation for being in Christ.  The way that I constantly battle these false doctrines is by continuing to read the word of God daily, reading books from theological scholars, as well as having a personal relationship with Jesus on a daily basis.  My strategy has always been to be a living testimony, despite many hardships physically, financially and emotionally to keep on pressing on towards the ultimate goal of spending an eternity with Christ Jesus.  The Holy Spirit gives us discernment, I pray daily that it helps me discern false teaching from right teachings.  One other false teaching that I faced growing up especially with my parents was seeking out prophets, but I know that God doesnt have to speak through a prophet, he can speak directly to me through my one on one relationship.

The author of Hebrews refers to Old Testament scripture over a hundred times.  He mentions how Moses led the Israelites tried to bring them closer to God but each time kept falling away from the grace of God.  The Old Testament reference to Mount Sinai was mentioned on how Israel was afraid of God and how this is in relation to what we as New Testament believers have to look forward to in eternity. Hebrews refers to the covenant God made with Abraham, it also refers to God as a burning fire that can devour you. The writer compares the High Priest Melchizedek to Jesus Christ in that he died and paid the ultimate price for each of our sins.  The writer of Hebrews mentions so many in the Old Testament in chapter 11 as those who stood for the faith and persevered.

The author of Hebrews states that Jesus is above the angels because he is the only begotten son of God.  The author states that in the Old Testament angels appeared to various people and if they were not obedient to the angels that they would receive punishment.  So in essence we are unable to avoid the final verdict from God if we continue to ignore who Christ is and that through him we have redemption of our sins.  In chapter 2 the writer mentions that Jesus is over all of the angels.  The author specifically mentions that we as the human race has been set just below angelic beings.  The author is very clear about the genealogy of Jesus is through Abraham and David.  Jesus's human tendencies allowed him to become the High Priest that paid for my sins on the cross of Calvary.

The new covenant is superior to the old because it will never be destroyed.  The covenant that Moses had in the Old Testament was established by the tribe of Levi based on the law given by God.  The priests of the Old Testament failed because Israel kept on sinning.  The new covenant is based on the remission of sins by the ultimate sacrifice of Jesus Christ on the cross.  The Old Testament priest had to continue to offer up animals as sacrifices where as in the new covenant Jesus completed the work of priesthood by laying down his life as a ransom for all.  Jesus became sin so that we would be wiped of it clean, he ultimately became the High Priest for us thus establishing the New Covenant.

I love the Old Testament scripture and do not take it lightly.  There are many promises in the Old Testament and many patriarchs of the faith that I look up to on a daily basis to always encourage me.  Hebrews 11 mentions many of these great men and women of God that persevered in the midst of suffering and trials.  I can see how hard it was for Abraham to be obedient to God, also see and crave the intimacy that Abraham and Moses had with God the Father and I pray daily that God would speak to me like he did with them in the Old Testament. I believe hearing from God on a daily basis is critical just as Moses and Abraham stood in the gap and God couldn't keep his judgement hidden from them.  Without faith it is impossible to please God, I have to believe that God is a rewarder of anyone that seeks him diligently.  My faith in Jesus is the only way that I am able to overcome any obstacle that comes in my way and I can learn from David, despite his constant sins, he repented and he was ultimately a man after Gods own heart.

The way I am able to communicate the sufficiency of Christ is by being a role model in every aspect of my life. Apostles Creed is a statement of Christian belief that is used by churches both Catholic and Protestant. It reflects traditions that were affirmed officially by the entire church. Although its roots are much earlier, in its present form it dates to about eighth century.    The earliest  written from this creed is found in a letter that Ancyra wrote in Greek to Julius, the bishop of Rome. About 50 years later, Tyrannius Rufinus wrote a commentary on this creed in Latin. In it, he recounted the view point that apostles wrote the creed together after Pentecost, before leaving to Jerusalem to preach. The title "Apostles" Creed is also mentioned about 390 by Ambrose, where he refers to the "the creed of the Apostles which the Church of Rome keeps an guard in its entirety.  Whatever we now know as the Apostles creed is an enlargement of the Old Roman Creed. Over the next few centuries, the Apostles Creed in its final form gained acceptance through out France and Germany. The Creed as it exists today consists of three main articles, like the Old Roman Creed divided according to a Trinitarian arrangement. The apostles Creed seems to represent some form of what the early church called the rule of faith.

The church needs to clearly define Christianity in biblical terms, which the Apostles, Creed succinctly provides to us. The Apostles creed is the most historic and universal summary of the Christian faith in the entire history of the church. It instructs, guides, defends and enshrines the most important question of all: "What must I do to be saved?"  Church and Christians must return to historic Christianity, which emerged from the rich doctrinal commitments and evangelical fervor of the apostles. This summary of timeless, biblical truths provides us with the essence of the Christian belief throughout history as followers attempted to construct a worldview and theology based upon the teachings of the Bible. The Apostle's Creed not only enlightens Christians, but it impacts and shapes their lives so that they might live daily in the freedom that the Lord Jesus Christ can provide. Seeking God through popular fads and other half-measures provide  us with nothing but short-term gratification. We can only find the true path to salvation in the historical Word of God.

While the author of Hebrew remains unknown, they used the Old Testament to support their theological views. For example within the book of Hebrews, there is a combination of either quotes or references to the Old Testament nearly 100 times. The historical facts of the Old Testament have been intertwined into the presentation of Christian faith into the book of Hebrews. 

Specific examples that have been referenced in the book of Hebrews with context dating to the Old Testament include: referencing God's son (2 Samuel 7:14), angels as serving spirits (Psalm 104:4), lower than angels (Psalm 8:4-6), blessings of God's vindication (Isaiah 8:17), God as a consuming fire (Deut 4:24). 

The author of Hebrews called attention to the fact that history had reached its last days in the times of Jesus. He did this through referencing the Old Testament as support and then a number of exhortations to continue and prosper in the Christian faith. This was done primarily due to the fact that the author had to challenge the teachings of the local community which was mainly Jewish. The one thing that remained sacred and in common was the Old Testament, and that is why we can see nearly 100 references or quotes from the Old Testament in the book of Hebrews.  In these scenarios, rather than noting just historical facts, the author spent more time on theological beliefs about God himself and the matters in close relation to God.

In the first century, Jewish communities often exalted angels as being powerful, glorious creatures who brought divine revelations to inferior human beings. While the outlooks of the community were rooted in biblical beliefs and passages, they gave excessive honor to angels. This raised a serious challenge to those who followed Christ. 

The author of Hebrews taught his audience that Jesus is superior to angels. This was accomplished in five steps, the first of which the author wrote to the audience that they should follow Jesus because Jesus is God's supreme source of divine revelation. The author declared that God spoke through angels. The second step was through the explanation that Jesus is greater than angels because he alone is God's messianic Son. Thirdly, the author told his audience to heed and pay careful attention to the great message of salvation first announced by Jesus. Fourth, the book of Hebrews supports the belief in the supremacy of Christ by explaining that Jesus is now ruler over all the angels. And in the future all of the believers would reign over them with him. Lastly, the author demonstrated that Jesus is Abraham's descendant, and Jesus will share his glory with Abraham's descendants, not with the angels. 

Through these five steps laid out in the book of Hebrews, the author was able to provide the honor that only Christ brings and how Jesus brought revelation that was far superior to any revelation given through any angel.

This was also referred to as the 'covenant of peace'. 

The New Covenant is based on the ultimate sacrifice of Jesus Christ and providers eternal forgiveness of sins. The Old Covenant would require ongoing animal sacrifices and offerings that could not fully take away the sins of mankind. The New Covenant is focused more on a personal and direct relationship with God rather than a system of laws and rituals. The New Covenant is also not prohibited to just the Jewish people, but rather to people of all nations. 

The New Covenant cannot fail per Hebrews 8:6 as it is founded on better promises. This offers the complete transformation of God's people and the the final eternal forgiveness of their sins. Jesus did away with sin once and for all because of his sacrifice and the shedding of bless. It was not merely sprinkle in a man made sanctuary, but He entered heaven by the sacrifice of himself, just as God had promised. 

Jesus died as a ransom in order to set his people free from judgement, and the author clearly states that Jesus will return but not to bear sin again, rather to bring the fullness of salvation to those who wait for him. 

The New Covenant is considered superior to the Old Covenant because it provides a more complete and personal relationship that is enduring with God through faith in Jesus Christ, which is opposed to the conditional, ritual based system of the old.

The five characteristics of Hebrew's original audience include  Jewish, Hellenistic, Immature, Persecuted, and Near Apostasy. 

For the Jewish audience, Hebrews 1:1 make this clear, "In the past God spoke to our forefathers through the prophets at many time and in various ways." The Old Testament Israelites are referred to as "our forefathers" which are considered to be the ancestors of the author and his audience.

The Hellenistic audience, which interpreters believe have lived outside of Palestine. The content in Hebrews reveals that the audience was familiar with theological teachings that were more common among Jews who lived outside of Palestine than the traditional Jews who lived within Palestine. 

The Immature audience which is known as the original audience of Hebrews was described in Hebrews 5:12, "Though by this time you ought to be teachers, you need someone to teach you the elementary truths of God's word all over again." This interprets to say that the audience has been listening to and exposed to the word of God over and over again for a long time, but they have yet not matured in the word. That is the emphasis the author gives when saying that this audience should have been teachers by now. 

The Persecuted audience is addressed in Hebrews 10:32, "Remember those earlier days after you had received the light, when you stood your ground in a great contest in the face of suffering ... So do not throw away your confidence, it will be richly rewarded." In this passage, the audience mentioned is being praised for their strength and were told to not throw away their confidence. The author of Hebrews mentions this group was facing the threat of more persecution even in the future and this was addressed in Hebrews 12:3-4. 

Lastly the Near Apostasy, this audience was near danger of turning away from Christ entirely. In Hebrews 10:26-27, it reads, "If we deliberately keep on sinning after we have have received knowledge of the truth, no sacrifice for sins is left, but only a fearful expectation of judgement and of raging fire that will consume the enemies of God." The author of Hebrews was not concerned about peccadillos or small sins, rather he was concerned more about those in danger of turning away from God.

The author of Hebrews used different literary devices and methods to reveal and express his exhortations to his audience. Frequency, for example allows us to understand the urgency of his message. The author exhorted to the audience using intensity and the hortatory subjunctive, a Greek verbal form used to urge or implore. At least 30 times these exhortations appear explicitly which would urge the audience often to "let us" do this or that. 

The author also exhorted using imperatives, which is often translated as direct orders. Hebrews 12:12-16  reveals the importance of adopting new attitudes or actions. He did not want to simply inform the audience of theological doctrines, he wanted them to adopt different viewpoints and attitudes towards it all. 

The author of Hebrews is described as highly rhetorical, meaning there was a persuasive or urgent debate mechanism in the first century. This is found more often in Hebrews than in any other book in the New Testament. This helped the author accomplish their purpose, containing a strong literary argument, using lots of different structural features to accomplish that, drawing readers in and convincing them of the argument that he is making. Some of these rhetorical devices included synkrisis, exempla, and qol wahomer.
