Living as a witness, in way that reflects the values of God's kingdom, such as love, humility, forgiveness, and service. Living in a way that is aligned to God's teachings and the powerful testimony of Jesus Christ. Kingdom oriented values, shifting focus from worldly success, to kingdom values, and reframing success in terms of faithfulness to God's will rather than society's standards. All while having eternal perspective, living with the mindset that earthly life is temporary, and eternal life with God is the ultimate goal, make decisions that reflect eternal significance.

Luke had a twofold purpose for writing the book of Acts, starting with the stated purpose which was to capture a historical view of the early church. Secondly, his intention was to convey the reality and power of the gospel message in the book of Acts. When we take a look at the historical account, we can see on more than one occasion of how Luke mentions that he had 'carefully' examined and investigated the details that he recorded. He also ensured to write an orderly account of the truth was reported so that it would be communicated clearly and accurately. He was very much concerned about recording true history because he understood the importance of a basic principle and how it repeated throughout the Bible. God revealed himself in real history, space and time and worked throughout all of history to ensure that his salvation and judgement were brought about. Luke ensured that he was not trying to write fiction, rather report real history. When Luke goes on to write the book of Acts, he wanted to confirm what Theophilus and others had been taught. This means that the book of Acts may be characterized as a didactic history. Luke was viewing the world and all of history as Christ's lens of lordship and kingdom. When reading the book of Acts, this purpose should impact the reader as we are not just reading true fact, rather we should draw out attention to teachings that were foundational to the early church and it was from reliable witnesses to the Holy Spirit.

The structural elements that reveal the structural pattern of the book of Acts can begin with the geographical spread of the gospel. In Acts. 1:8, there is a thematic outline which states, "you will be my witnesses in Jerusalem,  and in all Judea, and Samaria, and to the ends of the earth." In chapters 1-7, Jerusalem is referenced where the early churches activities and growth took place. Going on into chapters 8-12, the expansion of the gospel to Judea and Samaria is mentioned, and in chapters 13-28 the missionary journeys of Paul, symbolizes the gospel reaching the heart of the unknown world. Key figures are revealed such as Peter and Paul, church growth is also mentioned. This is all done through summary statements, and Luke would provide this in the book of Acts to highlight the successful stages of the gospel and the growth of the church. This pattern helps us understand the message of the book as it draws attention to specific features of history through summary statements, and the pattern of church growth emerges from this.

We should take into account the kind of literature that Acts is when we make modern application of Luke's message. The literary character of how Luke portrayed the book of Acts can be revealed by how he highlighted selective content in what he reported. He also designed the book of Acts to be episodic, and he also communicated many of his teachings in implicit ways. With the selective nature of how Luke displayed the book of Acts, he had to consider that there were too many facts, people and events in the world that any human being can efficiently provide a report on, so he had to take the significant events which took place in the church and take a fraction of that which was led by the Holy Spirit to bring forth to his readers. In an episodic account, distinct details describing how the church is to continue building God's kingdom in Christ through the gospel is portrayed, and we need to pay attention to both the small picture and the big picture. Lastly, being implicit allows the author to be direct with the reader and Like would comment explicitly on the significance of elements of his stories.

God is our true reality, and he requires to live according to his personality. Revelation from God is what allows us to obey God and have an understanding on the how.  The government that we are a part of is an example of how we abide by its laws and we have a duty to the government. In the same manner God is our ultimate authority, his personality is perfect.  God

God is our ultimate fact, which creates the baseline for ethics as a whole.  God's mere presence reigns over every right and wrong decision and mandates us to live according to his standard.  In order for us to realize our responsibilities towards God we have to first receive the revelation of God from above. We have to understand who God is, how he is in order for us to be able to live according to his standard.  God is perfect, blameless and without sin and he wants us all to live like him a righteous and upright life.  There is a saying that says what would Jesus do, this is not just a saying but when we go through the ups and downs of life we have to really examine how we come across making decisions in our life.  Are we making decisions that are wise according to the counsel of God or are we making rash decisions without seeking God's answer to whatever question we are going through.  God is the ultimate moral standard and this is why God is critical in us making right decisions to be able to accomplish what goals that he has intended for our life.

Goals when it comes to ethics have to do with the results behind our actions.  We all have goals that we set in life such as an alarm clock to wake up at a certain time daily, or to buy a thoughtful gift for my loved one on their birthday.  Goals have to do with where are we headed in life and the actions we take along that journey.  Goals can have two levels one is the immediate effect and the longterm such as building a tree house, we would need to measure the wood and cut it and eventually build the treehouse.  Our ultimate goal in life is to give glory to God such as Apostle Paul mentions it in 1 Corinthians 10:31. Even in the minute things of our life like what we should wear, or eat, this should never dishonor God.

A rigorous approach to revelation is when we are overly thinking on how to prevent sin.When we respond to the the word of God's instructions in a restrictive manner, we often neglect things that God allows and many other commands that God gives.  There are many bad results to this approach of rigor one of these is that it breaks freedom by limiting actions that are wrong under certain situations and good under other situations.  Secondly rigor instills chaos in that it prevents us from understanding our responsibility and to take happiness in God for our salvation.  The rigorous strategy denies Christian freedom and drives us into confusion.

The teachings on the mount about being blessed all have to do with the teachings of Jesus.  Our behavior, actions and overall mentality can determine what blessings we receive from God and indeed if we will receive them.  Jesus began the sermon by mandating the people to live morally. He described blessings in terms of the kingdom of God.  In Matthew 5, the kingdom of heaven is used multiple times and many theologians believe this is referring to the kingdom of God.  In verse 5 Jesus refers to receiving the earth, this was a kingdom blessing because it actually refers to the new earth that God will create when it comes in all of its glory.  In verse 9 it mentions about being sons of God which refers to kingship.  We often call God our father because in a sense he is our royal father. Jesus always presented the kingdom of God as a primary view point for our walk as Christians.

The first part of the kingdom of God is when we speak of the status of the King.  Second is about turning to the people of the kingdom and third we will look at all of the binding agreements between the king and his people.  Many have a hard time recognizing God as the king but in the Scripture God is our supreme emperor who is over all that he created.  Psalms 47:9 we read that the kings of the earth belong to God, he is greatly exalted.  God is king over all countries, he is special in that when the throne of David was established, it showed the power of God himself.  Since God is the ruler over all people, his people are referred to as those that he has called to himself in sharp contrast to those of this world.  God intended for Adam and Eve to have rule over everything. Through the good news, salvation spread so rapidly beyond the walls of Israel that the church now includes all races.

The history of God's kingdom goes beyond the period of inital peach to a time of aggresion against God.  This is a time when all people broke their binding agreements to their king.  We know in the garden of Eden, Eve was tempted by the snake, they ate the forbidden fruit and it violated the covenant.  In the new testament when God sent his only son to die on the cross this established a heavenly kingdom that we should all strive to be a part of.

I always think of Gods law as a joy and delight.  The more and more I study the word of God, the more i feel inclined to share the love of Christ with others.  Retribution is not taught in the Bible and so we have to able to align our actions with those of Christ Jesus  He is the author and finisher of our faith and we need to ensure that we live according to his purposes.  We need to always be kingdom minded, how can i be a blessing to someone, not just with words but with actions.  If I know that someone is struggling with any issue, finances, and or family life, step in and be the hands and feet of Jesus.

From every book in the scripture we know that God has complete dominion over everything. This is a privilege that comes from God the Father has created the whole universe.  There are three traits og God that we can remember in Christian ethics, first that his dominion is complete and its only for those who believe in him, it can also be very tiring.  God has given us a complete mental capacity to think on our own and make good and bad decisions.  In Jeremiah, we read about the potter, we have no right to question the potter because the clay is in his hand and he determines how the shape is to be made.  God is able to do as he wishes over us as he sees is best fit. No one can question God's moral baseline because in him was what right and wrong is based from, there can be found no wrong in him.  We need to understand that Gods character is divine and he knows everything when it comes to our lives.  We have to realize that God is in control over every circumstance of our life and we always tend to question that.  Phillipians 2:12 and 13 says to work out our salvation with fear and trembling, for it is God who works in you to be able to accomplish Gods will in our lives. God will never force us into any situation where we are unable to get out of.  God gives us the ability to avoid sin and overcome templations.  1 Corinthians 10:13 says that when you are tempted that God will provide a way out of it.  We always have to think clearly when we make decisions, does my decision glorify God, does it do God justice.  God has always been present with humanity and he will never leave us. God has an eternal covenant with his people that lasts from one generation to another.  Our ethical decisions must always give credence to Gods physical presence with us as a judge now and always.

The prenatural realm is a reality that is beyond what nature presents.  It is never above God but provides a distinct perspective about creation.  This is the world where angelic beings, evil spirits and the unseen spirits dwell.  In today's day and age we pay little attention to this prenatural realm because it is hard to picture the concept of angelic and evil spirits that are always around us and have personal dealings with us.  We have to realize that this is a huge reality where angels and demons have a huge role in what happens in our personal lives.  We are all living in our own little world not realizing that God dwells in our universe and both demons and angels have an intellect on their own and have the ability to make rational decisions.  We know that when God created angelic beings they were all perfect and righteous, but some turned to rebel against God and this is where blessing turned into damnation.  We have to understand that demons and angels have a huge impact on the daily moral dilemmas that we face and the decisions they bring to make.  Angels are God's personal message givers to us just as the Holy Spirit can speak to us in every situation of our life.  In 2 Kings there is an instance where the angel of the Lord destroyed 185,000 Assyrian troops in in one night in order to stop the invasion of Judah.  Other times angels are preventing us as Christians from falling.  The writer of Hebrews mentions that aren't angels there to minister to us serve those who will inherit salvation. The angels are constantly making sure that we are on our best behavior and do their best to prevent us from making decisions that are rash or abrupt.  Satan can also harm us, in Job he asked God to touch Job because to test him and to prove that Job would betray God but he stood faithful.  We have to be victorious over spirtual warfare because our struggle is not against flesh and blood but against the rulers, against authorities and against the powers of this dark world.

In Genesis 1, the creation of everything was perfect and we are made from the dirt of the ground. God blessed the human race by saying be fruitful and multiply, increase in number, fill the earth and subdue it.  God intended us to rule over all of the earth, he called us to govern the whole world.  God always intended us to have life and growth which would turn the whole world into a place which would have Gods kingdom.  When Adam and Even in the garden listened to what the snake said, this caused an rebellion against God's sovereignty and hard work and toil came as a result of their disobedience to God.  This caused sin to enter the world which caused us to be mean to each other and nature as it was designed to be changed as a whole.  We have to know that the Earth still belongs to God and the earth still shows God's goodness despite of the sin.  We see in Psalms 19 that the heavens declare the glory of God, the skies proclaim the works of his hands.  Paul mentions that everything in creation is good. God is in the business of redemption and is creating a new heaven and and a new earth where he can reside with his people.

The preternatural realm consist of angels and demons their relationship and impact on us in the world.  God has infiltrated thew world with a huge number of spiritual people known as angels and demons in which they both are smart and have characteristics and a will as well.  Angels were created to be pure just like God but when some of them decided to become rebellious towards God this caused them to go towards damnation.  Angels have been given a task to keep Gods children in line and interact with us on behalf of God the father.  Angels have a responsibility to ensure that we behave morally and prevent making decisions that are harmful to us.  God uses our salvation to instruct our angels in heaven. God's original purpose was to make known the wisdom of God to all the rulers and authorities in the heavenly realms.  Demons have the ability to harm us in the natural realm just like what was done to Job.  The demons are in a constant battle with angels, good and evil is always fighting against each other. God has given us an armor of God in ephesians which is there to equip us against every vile of the enemy.  Spiritual warfare is the real battle between forces of good and forces of evil.  Remember that Jesus has torn the evil spirits capability to overcome us, through his death and resurrection all enemies are destroyed.  The demons will continue to attack us until Gods last judgement and we have to be faithful until the end and constantly sharpen our weapons which is be dived in the word of God.

God sees us as all one group of people.  There are similarities in what the people of God go through and we have to look at how society will stand before God.  God had a purpose for Adam and Eve to be the first of many generations that would fulfill the cultural mandate of God.  The cultural mandate was for humanity as a whole to regenerate and build cultures.  We all are a part of a corporate task which involves unity and being considerate of others feelings when we make decisions.  Our decisions work together to achieve the goal of expanding God's kingdom to the ends of the Earth.  One problem of universal sin is that the human race doesnt fulfill the mandate in the way it should.  Sin prevents us from glorifying God and honoring him.  Our responsibility is to build God's kingdom and maintain a vigilatn watch for sin.  God reminds us that we are a chosen people, a royal priesthood, a people that belongs to God. Our primary goal is to live out Gods purpose on this earth by our life, our actions, our behaviors should allow people of this world to see that we are a different breed.  We have a responsibility to make sure everyone of our decisions do bring glory to God.

The fall allowed sin to enter everyone which provided a curse for all of humanity. Sin allows many to walk according to the flesh, set their minds on that which is hostile toward God, which doesnt give room to the law ofGod. and those in the flesh can never please God.  Prior to the fall, humans were perfect and created to reflect God and his character.  With the fall, God gave us the ability to make choices that may not please God.  As God cursed the human race, he messed up our personal wills. Sin is what controls the fallen human race making it literally impossible to satisfy God.  The fall has prevented the human race to have access to revelation of the Holy Spirit because God cursed humanity. Unbelievers have an instinctive knowledge og god's law and many recognize justice and know difference of right and wrong.  The Holy Spirit doesnt provide the same measure of an inward leading that he provides to believers as to unbelievers.  God chooses to reveal himself in ways that bless those who love him and that curses those who hate him. Humanity's fall into sin has provided unbelievers the incapacity to understand the mysteries of God.  Many non cognitive factors shape our ethical decision such as our feelings, inner voice, leadings, affinities, needs, shortcomings, scares and ultimate rejection of God.  The unbelievers heart has become calloused that they hardly hear with their ears and they have closed tehir eye.  The unbelievers heart is so hardened against God and his truth which prevents us from properly understanding his revelation. God desires in loyalty and not sacrifice.

Christians find comfort in the immutablilty of God because it means that God is always the same, he is always faithful, and dependable, he never changes his characteristics or his promises.  God provides a steady rock in which we can focus on in challenging and uncertain times.  God is not like the ocean's waves when it comes to his faithfulness, he will never abandon his promises upon our live and will alway remain loyal to them.  God's personality will never based on our actions but will always be the same. Being knowledgeable in the Scripture allows his love and mercy to remain as the anchor that brings us strength.  No matter what happens in our life, we will have assurance that God is soverign and he has our best interests at heart.  Psalms 102:27, states like this, they will perish but you will remain, they will all wear out like a garment. You will change them like a robe and they will pass away, but you are the same, your years have no end.  This verse describes God's unchanging character.

When I battle sin as a Christian, my prayer life is critical to me being victorious over sin. Diving into scripture, meditating on it day and night, have a core group of people in my life that keep me accountable to prevent me from wandering into sin.  I have to constantly remind myself of the end goal which is my eternity and remember that sin will take me away from that goal. I have to constantly train my mind to think positively because the devil always wants me to think that God is out there to get me. I have to understand where my weakness lies and where the devil takes a hold in my life and be actively conscious about avoiding those temptations and avoiding those people or environments that may lead us to that temptation.  What doesnt help is trying to rely on my own will power to overcome sin, it isnt possible because without God's grace it is never attainable.  I always tend to beat myself up when I make a mistake and this is something that will not help me become an overcomer and this is something that the enemy desires for me to dwell in that completely.  The last thing I would say that is harmful that my parents growing up did was comparing myself to others and wanting to become like so and so, this is truly harmful to my spiritual growth and this is not something that God truly desires.  The Holy Spirit that dwells inside of me is what gives me the strength to avoid harmful situations that will ultimately effect me reaching eternity.  My focus and aim should always daily start with prayer and end with prayer, we have to have an attitude of gratitude and know that there our outside forces that will try to influence me in the wrong way and I have to make a conscious effort not to engage in those deeds or behaviors that is unlawful to God.

Our intentions serve as a reason and our deeds are the results of them.  Our intentions come from within and shape our characteristics.  One's love for their family will give them a mandate to go to work to provide for their loved ones.  There will be an internal conflict that happens for the man of the home to stay at home be lazy but the intentions are all there to avoid tension and live with unity with one another.  Our desire to share Jesus Christ with those who dont know the gospel is showing our loyalty to God and shows that we take ownership in others coming to the faith as well.  In 1 Chronicles chapter 28 David is associating intentions are related to one's personal heart. God is a searcher of our hearts and understands every intention and we have to be willing to serve God with our whole heart.  David taught Solomon that obedience is better than sacrifice and this must come from the deepest parts of our soul.  God doesnt want our partial love, he expects us to love him with all of our heart, soul and every ounce of our strength. The Bible mentions that we used to be slaves to sin but now are slaves to righteousness.  We have to remember that our every action that we take do have consequences, ultimately thinking how we glorify God should be our only intention when doing anything.

God's actions of atoning grace and commong grace serve as models for our own behavior by leading us to forgive, have empathy, and being able to give to others when their merit don't deserve it.  God gives us his grace with no bounds, no conditions, by showing his deep affection to everyone despite their deeds and convictions.  We are always called to be immitators of God by showing others grace with every interaction with have with anyone. God sent his only son down to the earth to die for our sins so that we may have eternal life in that way expressing his intimacy towards us.  We have to be able to give grace when needed, many hurt us, many break us, but as Christians we have to show them the love that Jesus showed us.   God is about restablishing broken relationships and asking us to mend fences with those who seek rectification.  God let go of his pride by sending his son as a human into this world and to be able to serve those who were destitute, those who would never be looked at, it is our responsiblity to become the hands and feet of Jesus Christ.  God's grace ultimately allows us to do deeds of kindness to others when they really don't deserve it.

My motivation comes from knowing who God is and what he did for me which allows me to live out my faith accordingly.  God gave bestowed upon me an agape love in that in John 3:16 we read that For God so loved the world that he gave his only begotten son to die that whoever believes in him shall not die but have eternal life. My obedience comes from my heart, my genuine passion is to help those in need with my time, my money and resources.  If anyone is in need, my first instinct is to go there and spend time with them and provide for them in the time of need as to what they are needing.  There have been many times I have been down, didnt have anything on me and there were friends of mine that came through in the clutch time show me the love of Christ.  I feel obligated to share my blessings with others. Reading Gods word daily and spending time in his presence allows me to be effective in hearing the voice of God and to be used by an annointing that the Holy Spirit provides.  My intentions have always come with a pure heart, if I do anything I always consider how I can glorify God and not desiring for any recognition.  There have been times that I can remember that my heart wanted the recognition and felt bad when not recognized but than the Holy Spirit convicts me and tells me that its not about me but what God's plan is, the reward is not here, its going to be in heaven.

I remember coming to the faith at the age of 10 years old at our church New Life Church of God in plano, texas at the time.  My uncle Pastor Jose Annicattu was the pastor and he gave a challenging word that morning about Jesus Christ and how he should be our focus in life and that it convicting me to repent that day.  I asked God to forgive me of my sins and invited the Lord Jesus Christ into my life.  I remember going to Pensacola Florida when I was about 12 years old with an assemblies of God church and having an encounter with God in a personal way where all I could do was just cry in his presence and didnt truly understand what transformation was happening in my life.  When I was 13 decided to obey God's commandment of water baptism in my life and this is where tests in my life started to happen.  Once I took this decision, many peer pressures started to happen in my life, there were numerous challenges I faced all throughout high school that God gave me the strenght to overcome.  I know during my senior year of high school when I was 17, I was worshipping and asking God to fill me with the power of the Holy Spirit and God truly instilled in me the gift of speaking in tongues.  This gift has encouraged me and allowed me to speak with God directly in the heavenly language when my own words would fail, it would interced truly on my behalf.  I know there have been many tests regarding my health, regarding accidents, regarding my future, in everything I was able to see the merciful hand of God upon my life.  I have seen ministers in my life give me second chances, and 3rd chances to be able to achieve God's ultimate purpose in my life.  I am grateful to my parents, my spiritual fathers who has led me thus far and showed the example in which I should live by.  My motives and actions for sure after marriage has changed, my wife Sheba has motivated me to think from a heavenly perspective and not an earthly perspective.  Sheba has always been the light in my life to remind me that we have a heavenly call, that our reward is in heaven, we shouldnt strive for recognition from man but only desire what comes from God.

Imagination allows us to make a mental picture of ideas that are not evident to our senses.  This imagination is what allows us see the bigger picture, to see possiblilites despite things being impossible.  This imagination allows us to find an area to expand our knowledge, and to have a personal and spiritual encounter with God.  We have to be able to see the unseen, in my personal life, I have been married for 12 years with promises that God will honor me with children.  Many years it was prophesied over us, but we gave up, but one thing is for sure God never gave up and blessed us with a son this year for God's glory.  We have to allow the word of God to come alive in our lives when we go through our darkest times, knowing that God was there for Abraham, Isaac,Jacob, Joseph, David, and Daniel and many others in the Bible.  Our imagination will allow us to be truly changed because we think positively.

Having knowledge allows us to know right and wrong when issues arise, having and understanding that our actions can have various consequences for the choices that we make. We have to make educated choices that align with the principles that are outlined in the word of God.  There will be situations that arise in our life where we have to make a critical decision and without knowledge this will never be possible to make the right choice.  God asks us to put ourselves in the shoes of the other individual to understand where they are coming from and to be able to make a wise decision as a result.  We have to be able to have the ablility to analyze what my actions would do, what will be the end result.  Our responsiblity in life should be to minimize losses and prevent others from being hurt when we make these decisions.  Every one of our decisions should be based on the moral standard that God has placed.  When we make decisions based on morals it allows us to build trust with others, it shows that we respect others, and ultimately displays the example of compassion that Christ showed upon us.

The basic definition of one's will is referring to the inner voice inside of us to make decisions. Our will shows our determination to not give up when situations get tough.  Our will is a motivating force, it is shaped by our values, our faith and will always give us directions on how we ultimately make a decision.  When making decisions we always have to weigh the consequences and how it may affect others around us.  When we consider others' feelings this is when we show the love of God.  There is a saying that where there is a will there is a way, the will gives us strenght to make the wise decision when others may say its not the right decision.  God is sovereign and knows the decisions that we make have an impact and will give us the free will to make the call  God ultimately knows that we will come back to him and his purposes will come to pass in our life.

I have always wanted to store up things here on earth, accumulate wealth, have all the best things of this world in essence to keep up with the jones family.  This is all futile is what I realized and is vanity just like Solomon said.  I realize that my treasure is not here it is in heaven and I have to strive for that.  We should not be concerned about acquiring all things of this world where moth and rust will destroy but solely be concerned about the treasure that is being prepared in heaven for me.  I have come to the realization that I shouldnt compare myself to others and what others have, but but consumed about he desires of me.  Romans 12 is one of my favorite chapters in which Paul asks us to not be conformed to this world but be transformed by the renewing of the mind according to Christ Jesus.  My actions on this world have consequences and my heart needs to be led by God in that my intentions need to be always to glorify God.   My actions should display God and should show his love in my deeds my words as well.  I have to always consider what I say can hurt others and make sure that I understand how I can be a blessing in ministry.

Historical analysis is a direct correlation about every act that God has done.  Confession describes that he works through an event, God achieves his will in history by acting through us. In the Scripture that we see that God inflicts sickness on Job and heals him with out any instruments.  The Confession also talks about taking the mundane and making it exceptional.  Like Sarai was 90 years old and her womb was closed when God revealed that she will bear Abraham a son.  Confession also speaks to how God works in the unconventional way as in the book of Joshua how the sun stood still until Joshua won the war. Historical analysis refers to the unordianary miracles of God that is way beyond what our minds can comprehend.

The factual approach to bible history is specifically geared towards the dates of when events occurred. The purpose of a fact based approach is very candid and to develop a record which puts together what we learn from the Bible and what we get from outside the Bible witnesses.  There are two sides to theology concerns, one being a description of other topics which can be linked to God. There is another category that goes over the foundational teachings of humanity,salvation, our moral code and the body of Christ.  The study of the Bible enables us to broaden our knowledge of all these subjects mentioned above such as our salvation, and the overall difference between right and wrong.

There was a German philosoper in the 17th century named Hegel who was famous for his presentation that every part of reality is captured in logical patterns of development known as the dialectic.  He stated the entire world was ordained by a history of logic. For example the study of rocks was used to understand the age of the earth.  Also biology became a part of history as many were introduced to Darwin and the concept of evolution. Changes in the culture caused a shift in how the study of scripture developed to bring the truth of Christ to the western world when it was dominated by various philosophies.  The study of the Bible is responding to a significant move to the challenge of the mind in the modern era.

History has had numerous impacts on the modern teaching of the Bible.  The sad thing is many students of the Bible have diluted basic Christian doctrines, while many others have included essential tid bits from history that has been sustained and broadened our knowledge of faith in Christ. Modern history led many teachers of the Bible to explore it with an open mind with new goals. Gabler's point of view on the Bible was to understand what the old writers and people in the Scripture understood about God and the universe that they are a part of. Gabler also mentioned that followers of Christa should also have belief in the current world by introspection on science and religion.

Synchronic refers to steps, for example when my son got a dehumidifier,it came with a manual which has various steps to insure that it is assembled appropriately. We are able to take apart the history of the Old Testament scriptures into bits and pieces and be able to focus on how it all comes together. Synchronic is rooted from the words with or together with.  Synchronic refers to how teachers of the Scripture look into various events in the Old Testament that occurred simultaneously. For example, there are plots to a storyline and every small event tells a portion of the story. Synchronic can refer to limited periods of time or other time focus on the lengthier periods of time.  For example, I might say I spoke a long time with my wife just a moment ago, making this event of talking a single event.  Many other instances we might recap the things we did in a week or a year in a small statement.

Synthesis is not hard to understand.  We allow synthesis daily in our practical lives which means to bring together various items of something into one. Synthesis is all about summarizing and not going into every specific detail of an even that has happened. In the 20th century many used common sense in disciplines presented by the study of Scripture. We aknowledte the common sense of the personality of the Old Testament on two basises. Old Testament Scriptures will remain shocking to many since the mind of God is not ours. God reveals to us his vision about certain events but also directs them to common sense, ways of understanding and and understanding about God.

Poets in the time period of the Old Testament were absorbed in two different aspects that spekd of history. On one side, they gave heed to the world they wrote which allowed poetry to go into the past. One example is when Moses and Miriam on what happened to the Red Sea. Being in deep thought about the word of God it allows us to know the value of the law of God.  Writers also took us to the future which showed a time when captives will finally come back to their land of promise. Miriam sang a song which motivated the children of Israel to keep going despite all of the challenges.

Since the 17th century Enlightenment in Europe, many that studied students of history tried to apply science to the writings. Old Testament stories were only as detail oriented as they needed to be. For example the writer of Chronicles doesnt write everything about Solomon and leaves out various things like him marrying the Pharaoh's daughter and building the temple for God. The writers of the Old Testament felt no need to mention every truth.The stories of the Old Testament are not objective by today's standards. God prompted the Old Testament writers to influence the perspective of those that read it.

The writer of Chronicles put together the history of King Solomon's life.  The writer left out the negative aspects of his kingship, left out the marriage to the daughter of Pharaoh,and the other foreign women. Solomon's failures led to the division of the nation but despite that the writer of Chronicles wanted to focus on the positives, despite that, the stories are factual about the past. In our day to day lives, we often talk embellishing what actually happened. Let us remember the fact the narratives of the Old Testament are not objective to the standards of modern day.

Diachronic comes from two words in the Greek language which means through or to go throughout. Diachrony refers to a timeframe being past which involved change that may evolve over months or years.  Looking at the Old Testament diachronically is similar to focusing on a book from chapter to chapter. This perspective to the Bible refers to how events unfolded over time. The diachronic approach is focused on how frameworks have changed. Diachronic analysis goes hand in hand with a sequence of events.

The reason we use development is because of two main concepts. Changes in the Old Testament theological structures lead us towards accomplishing God's divine will for history. The second thing is theological changes happen only through God's divine touch. The Bible is all about accomplishing God's divine chapter in all of our lives.  Isaiah 46:10 states that my purpose will stand and God will do all that he pleases. God has short term and long term goals over our lives such as David being king over Israel. God's goal was to establish David and his generations to come to fullfill God's short term goals. David's kingdom had a future goal of extending God's kingdom to every part of the Earth. God is always going to be involved in our lives and he provides for us in mysterious ways. God asked Moses to do certain things to make his people holy such as him. God always shows himself through his deeds and his actions.

The covenant with Adam and Noah were considered universal because it was between God and all of mankind. The bond that Adam and God had put significance on all of mankind having the basic responsiblity which shows our dedication to God. There was a covenant that was made with Noah that God will never curse the ground.  God knows that we are evil from infancy and that sin is running rampant in our lives.  God intended to redeem mankind with a new grace to be able to fulfill God's purposes. God established a national covenant with the people of Israel, God shortened his covenantal attention to just one group of people such as Israel which would lead all of mankind to service to God. The covenant to Abraham is considered the covenant of assurance.  Israel in the future became a huge kingdom under the rule of David and God made a covenant with him as well. God's choice of David's family would never be cast away. The new covenant was made to rule the people of God, when God accomplished his promises, was to reinstate his people after slavery to spread the kingdom to the ends of the earth. Typology refers to an order of being controlled such as studying such as science and studies of Scripture. Baptism in the New Testament is derived from the flood in Noah's time. Paul mentions a shadow of things to come which refers to being with Christ. Jesus made a comparison about Moses lifting up the snake in the desert, so the Son of Man must be lifted up, that everyone who believes in him may have eternal life. Jesus showed the bronze serpent in correlation to his crucifixion. Typology can be seen as a figure of speech. Typologies is a venn diagram of important people and events in history. We should allow the Scriptures to come alive in our lives.  The moral law in the Old Testament is a guideline for us to follow which shows God's own character, his integrity, love and his faithfulness. The Old Testament teaches us to worship the Lord with gladness, come before him with joyful songs, knowing that he is the Lord our God. God is the one who made us, and we are his people, the sheep of his pasture, we are to enter his gates with thanksgiving and his courts with praise. As Paul states in Romans 12, our bodies should be given as a living sacrifice, not being conformed to the ways of the world and be transformed by the renewing of our mind and this would be your reasonable service. We have the Lord's supper in church which reminds of the ultimate sacrifice that Jesus paid on the cross of Calvary and reminding us to live according to how Christ did while on the Earth. Jesus has given us the Holy Spirit which is alive and well in our hearts daily which allows us to speak to God in a heavenly language as well as comforts us when we are most distraught. God revealed himself during the Old Testament in two forms; one through revelations and word revelations. The New Testament reveals many works of God such as Jesus's ministry while on Earth, and how the Holy Spirit is evident in the first church. It also reveals to us that Christ is coming back. The Gospels show what God talked through Jesus's words which than revealed his actions. Old and New Testament biblical theology both emphasize on the acts of God and also his word revelations. The parables of Jesus give account to what he does as well as is a shadow of his works that will happen in the future.

There are major changes between the ministry on earth of Jesus, the past of the church, and the second coming of Jesus Christ. The New Testament usually treats these as one which displays a portrait of Jesus and his acts. For example, the Gospels only tell us about the life of Jesus and refers to the continuance of the ministy after Jesus leaves. Acts of the Apostles express what happens after Jesus leaves and Revelation only talks about the glorious return of Christ. New Testament scholars focus on the return of Jesus Christ and the church being reunited with our Savior.

God revealed himself through act and word revelations which caused developments in theology.Escatology teaches about the end times and what is yet to happen. The Old Testament set the standard for what New Testament scholars have found out about what is to come. In the beginning when God created us, he created us in his image. We have a call to be his preisthood to be fruitful and multiply. There are two forces fighting in the time of Adam, one is the seed of the serpent and the other being the seed of the woman. These two groups of people will always be at battle for victory.

The writers of the New Testament tested both personal and group eschatology that focused on the people of God being redeemed into the presence of God in the new Jerusalem, which refers to Eden. The majority of Jews in Palestine when the first church was established had views reflecting that of the Old Testament. Israel suffered so much but throughout these centuries, many Jews were waiting in the fullfillment of Old Testament prophesy.

My knowledge of the kingdom of God always affects how i do ministry.  I always have to think what would Jesus do, how will my actions affect others.  The kingdom of God mindset will not avoid life and it will allow me to be true to my responsibilities which will involve Christ in every aspect. The kingdom mentality will allow me to trust God blindly knowing that he will provide and being content regardless of what we have or not. My ministry will change because I allow the Holy Spirit to direct our paths.

Eschatology refers to the end times.  Eschatology is the studying of the final things or the teaching of them.  It goes over a period of time of the final days of Jesus's life and his ministry and what will happen when he does come back to receive his church. In the Old Testament, there are three steps which are: the inception of the world and all of its beings, period of salvation after the fall due to sin, and finally when the heavenly kingdom is fulfilled.

Genesis chapter one instructs us that God established the heavens and the earth. God created every aspect of the universe including the oceans, the Earth, the heavens, every living creature such as all of the animals.  He also created the human race to be able to have dominion over all of creation which included the Earth and every living thing on it. God ultimately created us in his own likeness, which was both man and woman, and gave the command to bear fruit and establish generations to come. God had a purpose for all of the human race to be his instruments or essentially rulers of the world. The mandate placed on all people was to build a way of life throughout the universe but also creating the family unit and every part of society which includes governments and sciences. God's ultimate was for us to fill the world with a mirror that show we are community minded in giving glory to God.

Proto-euangelion refers to the first gospel, because it serves as the first opportunity of being saved after being subject to failing to meet the mark. The intent first for our salvation shows in Genesis chapter 3 verse 15 because immediately following that the lapse of judgement, there is a promise of one who rescues us from our difficulty with sinning. In the same chapter in Genesis we read that there will be fighting between the two seeds in which the snake will make a mark on the woman's child, but that child will eventually trample the head of the snake. The remainder of the Bible displays for us the salvation story that the destroying of the head of the snake will finally happen on the cross of Calvary.

God's first major redemptive covenant was with Adam who missed the mark in the Garden of Eden. From the inception of humanity, God had intentions for all of humanity and he knew that there will be two groups of people, one in which follow after God and the other group that rebel God.  The second redemptive covenant was made with Noah which he guaranteed that he would never ever destroy the world with a flood anymore. Through this promise, he did this to allow all of humanity to serve God's purposes.  God made his third redemptive covenant to Abraham to serve God in a special way.  Abraham and his generations to come played a role in the end times coming to pass. In Genesis chapter 22, God establishes that through his seed all the nations on the earth will be blessed. God's covenant with Abraham created the expectation that his earthly kingdom would not just include the nation of Israel but all peoples of the earth. God made his 4th redemptive covenant with Moses, that if the people of Israel follow God and all of his commands he will bless them. He mentioned to Moses that he will never abandon his people and will restore them to favor. The final covenant was with David that he would establish his house as a permanent dynasty ruling over God's earthly kingdom. God promised never to violate the covenant in Psalms 89 and it will be established like the moon and the faithful witness in the sky.

The two great ages were the present age which is marked by sin and the resiliance of Gentile nations which is seen as the the slavery of Israel. There is also an age to come which is when God will establish his heavenly kingdom on Earth.  In the Gospel of Mark 1:15 it tells us that the kingdom is to come, so we should repent and hear the good news. Luke 17:10 states that we have the kingdom of God within us which shows our future assurance of Jesus coming back. In Matthew chapter 25 we read that the Son of Man will come in glory to establish his kingdom. In Daniel chapter 12 we hear there is a belief that there will be a resurrection of the dead.  Jesus and his apostles disagreed with those students of the word about the age that is to come. Jesus and the apostles taught that the ages to come would not happen quickly. In revelation 1:5-6 Jesus has freed us from our sins by his blood and has made us to be a kingdom and priests to serve God. God is preparing a new heaven new earth for all of his church to go to.

The term regenerate is a symbol of the human race's current state or it refers to those in faith. The uregenerate refers to those individuals that do not believe and experience a lot of difficulties of today's day and time.  Regenerate also refers to being born again or we can refer to the people that are living in the spiritual realm and the unregenerate would be the opposite of that which refers to them being without life. The Bible talks about the fall through Adam and being dead until being renewed by the Holy Spirit.  The consequences of sin is referred to in Romans 6:23 which states the wages of sin is death but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ.

The unregenerate still have the ability to have thoughts, to have emotions, to have aspirations, to make decisions, and have conversations with the world just like the regenerate does.  God instructed not to eat from one particular tree which is the tree of knoledge of good and evil, in the garden of Eden and you will surely die, what he meant was not physically but spiritually.  We have to realize that when we sin, it takes us away from God and his glory. God has only two perspectives and that is either we live in Adam's sin or we are free from sin by the redemption in Christ Jesus. According to Augustine, Adam and Eve had the ability to prevent sin completely, but also had the ability to choose to sin. Through Adam all of his descendants including us lost the ability to prevent sin in our lives.  God essentially cursed the human race and humans became spiritually corrupt which leads to death spiritually.

In order for us to be reborn or to have life spiritually, our inner souls have to go from a dead state into being alive. We are born through our mothers womb initially but there is a second birth that comes from us accepting Jesus Christ as our personal savior and accepting him into our hearts.  Nicodemus who was wise beyond years, had a hard time understanding what it meant to be born again but Jesus was able to explain it to him. Jesus emphasizes us to be born of the Spirit which gives death to our flesh. Titus 3:5 states that God saved us through the renewing of the Holy Spirit and the blood of Jesus. God restores our moral ability to be obedient to the purposes of God and to go after the blessings of his heavenly kingdom. Ephesians 2:4-5 states that God who is rich in mercy, made us alive with Christ even when we were dead in our sins and it is by grace we are saved.

The intermediate state refers to the period that happens between when we die and the resurrection. This intermediate state are for the ones in faith and also to those not in the faith alike. When we all pass away, we go to the intermediat state which is waiting for the resurrection. The  unregenerate, their souls still are alive which causes fear.  When the spirit returns to God who gave it, their punishment is in hell. Luke 12:4-5, Do not be afraid of those who kill the body and after that can do no more, fear him who, after the killing of the body, has power to throw you into hell. Hell is a reality because Jesus Christ mentioned it many times. In hell, the the rich man was in torment who saw Abraham far away with Lazarus by his side. This is shown in Luke 16 how the rich man asks for mercy from Abraham and he states to him to remember your lifetime and now you are in despair. Being apart from Christ leads to eternal damnation or Hades, the lake of fire.

In Luke 23:43 Jesus told the thief on the cross that this very day they would be together in paradise. Revelation 6:9 mentions the souls of those who died for the sake of the Gospel being very near to the altar in God's heavenly tabernacle.  Paul mentions in Philipians 1:23 that his decision would be to away from his physical body and to be in eternity with his heavenly father. Jesus says that he leaves us to prepare a place for us and that he will come back and take us to be with him. Jesus says that I am the way, the trutght and the light in essence he takes us right by his side to the ultimate spot which is heaven. Jesus through the cross of Calvary and dying on the cross, allows our sins to be washed, and we find our place in heaven with him.

In the first century there are two dominant schools of thought concerning the resurrection of the dead, the Pharisee view and the Saducean view.  The Pharisee view was that at the end of time, the righteous and wicked will be judged and the righteous will be raised. Their belief is grounded in the re-establisment of Israel. Daniel 12:2 states that many of those who are who sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt. The Sadducees view rejected the idea that the dead would be resurrected, as well as belief in angels and anything of heaven. They held firm to the teachings of the Torah, and they were an elite priestly class.since they were only focused on the worship in the Temple.  Acts 23:8 states that the Saduccees say that there is no resurrection, nor angel, nor spirit, but the Pharisees acknowledge them all. In Matthew 22:23 the Sadducees approach Jesus mocking the resurrection. Jesus view on the resurrection is stated in John 11:25 I am the resurrection and the life and anyone who believes in me, though he die, will live. Paul says is 1 Corinthians 15 that if Christ hasnt been raised that our faith is in vain. In Acts 24, we read that Paul is saying there will be a resurrection for the just and the wicked.

Divine authority means the complete, and sovereign power that God has to govern, and give life according to his divine plan.  The divine authority is built in God's character which he has created all things and is our sustainer. God's authority can never be questioned. John 5:28-29 states that do not marvel at this, for the hour is coming, in which all who are in the graves will hear his voice and come forth. Jesus has divine power to call people from the dead. God has an authority to be the ultimate judge of our lives.  Revelation 20:12 states that everyone both small and great will stand before the throne and the books were opened. Heaven is where God lives, and hell he has rule over as well. God has power to give us eternal life and he determines where our eternity will be whether in heaven or the lake of fire. Ultimately Jesus is our advocate for God, and all authority has been given to him as mentioned in Matthew 28:8. Jesus victory over death which allows God to raise us from the dead and judge all of humanity.

The general resurrection is seen as a restoration of the universe. Romans 8:19-23 speaks of creation groaning in expectation of given freedom from sin. God will renew the physical world in removing the curse of sin and death shown in Genesis 3. There is a new heaven and a new earth that is established where there will be no more tears, no more pain, and we will be free from suffering. The general resurrection also refers to the wicked, and has impacts on a final judgement. Revelation 20 states that there will be a separation for all who reject Christ. Revelation 21 shows the heaven is established on Earth and the new Jerusalem is established which is the final image of God dwelling with humanity again like before the fall in Eden. Philippians 3 states that we will have glorified ressurected bodies like the one Jesus had. Heaven is a place where we will have a perfect fellowship with God once and for all.

There are three groups of people that will be judged: the righteous, the wicked, and the fallen angels. In Matthew 25, Jesus states to come, you who are blessed by my Father, take your inheritance, there is a kingdom that is being prepared from the creation of the world. The righteous who have obeyed all of God's commands, demonstrated their affection for Jesus Christ and showed it through their actions will receive the crown of righteousness. The second group is the wicked who are those who live in rebellion and reject God and deny he exists, they will also be judged. The wicked are ultimately separated from God forever and has an eternal punishment. The third group that will be judged will be the fallen angels which is the devil himself. In Revelation 20 it mentions that God will through them into the lake of fire and they will be tormented day and night forever.

God will consider every piece of evidence in our final judgement in that God will be fair and just. God does not show any partiality like humans and he sees our inner most being which is our heart. God will look at the circumstances in which we grew up in, as well will take into consideration if we have had opportunities to accept Jesus as our personal savior.  For example someone who grew up in a place where the Gospel was not preached as much will not be judged the same as the person who has access to the Gospel very freely and has a knowledge of the word of God. Luke 12:47-48 shows us about servants who knew the master's will but chose not to do it.  God will keep us in check by our understanding, our access to the gospel.  God's judgement will be full of mercy and is not cookie cutter based but it is based on the individual.  God will take into consideration our situations and our accountability will be different based on our backgrounds.

The word trinity means essentially tri-unity which means three in one. The teaching of the Trinity can be described as three holy individuals in one divine essence. There is only one God, but God shows his identity through the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit. We understand that God the Father is the one who sent the Son who was crucified and risen, who than goes to be with his Father in heaven and promises us the comforter which is the Holy Spirit. We have to understand that there is only one God but displayed in three different persons.

With respect to the Trinity, the person is a specific individual as being related to God the Father. A person usually refers to an individual who can make their own choices, and has their own perspectives. The three individuals of the Trinity do not symbolize three different gods, but it represents one with God the Father with one divine essence.  In the teaching of Trinity, a person refers to a unique relationship with God the Father, but still being equal persons with the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit.

Since God is one, we understand that there is one holy essence. God's oneness is refers to God being simple.  John 4:24 says that God is spirit, and as spirit, he is indivisble. God is not one that is hard to understand. We have various ways to describe God's character in that he is omniscient, omnipresent, and omnipotent and also represents love, he is one that sheds mercy and also just in his judgements. God is not made up of man made ingredients which means there is no unrighteousness in our God. God reveals himself to Moses in Exodus as I am who I am, which means he is pure spirit. God is wholly together with all that he accomplishes. God is never in fight between his anger and his mercy. All of God's characteristics work simultaneously, also working individually which makes him without any error.

Christ has always existed based on the teaching of the Trinity.  John 1:1 says that in the beginning was the word, the word was with God and the word was God.  In the same chapter in verse fourteen, we read that the word became flesh and made his dwelling in us. There are those who are against the Trinity that like to quote scripture from Colossians 1 that God has not always existed as Trinity. They believe that he was a created being. In the Old Testament when we refer to the firstborn its not referring to chronologically but it is referred to as priority or supremacy. Jesus symbolizes our access to the God the Father and the Holy Spirit as providing us our salvation. Paul urges the church of Corinth in 1 Corinthians to worship God the Father and God the Son, this is how we be assured that Jesus is God and he establishes that Jesus is a part of creation.

The Great Commission in the last chapter of the gospel of Matthew teaches us to go and baptize people in the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit and so we have one God. In the Old Testament the priests were to bless the children of Israel, as stated in Numbers 6, the Lord bless you, and keep you, make his face shine upon you and make his face turn towards you and give you peace. The Spirit is of heaven which shares equality with the Father and the Son. Whenever we say the benediction we mention Trinity which is only provided through the death and resurrection of Jesus Christ. When God decides to create something, he consults every part of Trinity including the Holy Spirit. In Genesis we read that the Spirit hovered over the waters which means it was present from the beginning of creation. The Holy Spirit is always alive in every part of creation, inlcuding our very salvation because it is the Spirit at work to give us new life. Ultimately there is only one God who co-exists as three individuals which is the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit. Each individual of thte Trinity are one in their characteristics from heaven. Each member of the Trinity are equal in power and glory.

The teaching of the Trinity instructs us that there is one God, one divine essence, and every individual of the Trinity are equal and fully God. Much of the truths about Trinity come from the New Testament. God is showing us in gradual steps more and more about who he is and how he works. Throughout time, God has been on the move gradually to become more intimate with us. God spoke in the Old Testament through creation like the clouds, the burning bush but there was always a space between God and us.  In the New Testament God became closer to us through his son Jesus Christ and the Scripture says through the Holy Spirit, he is now dwelling in us. The same resurrection power that Jesus Christ had we also have through the Holy Spirit. This Holy Spirit allows us to do greater things on the Earth than Jesus did and accomplish the will of the Father. We have to realize that the Holy Spirit helped breath the scriptures into life.

Revelation chapters one and four states that the one who sits on the throne is God the Father. John 1 speaks to the word of God becoming flesh.  Apostle John sees a roll of paper and is told that no one can open the paper. John is crying understanding that this roll of paper needs to be opened in order to understand the inner most revelation of God. The Lion shows kingship, also represents the tribe of Judah. John also sees a lamb which shows us sacrifice which depicts pain. Jesus is the king who has conquered everything and provided us our redemption. The Lion shows majesty while the lamb represents humbleness. The divine nature of Jesus is displayed who died as the ultimate price for our salvation. Revelation 5 puts Jesus in the bucket of being divine. He is not a creature of God but he is one with God who will utterly destroy all of his enemies when he comes back.

The first chapter of John has been well known through out time and gives us evidence that Jesus is the Son which is the second individual of the Trinity. The scripture shows us that Jesus he is God and has been one with God since the beginning. Jesus has also been a part of making all things. John 1:1 teaches us the deity of Jesus Christ. John depicts Jesus as God himself and to refer to Jesus as the Word of God is pointing to his divine nature. John says in Jesus we become a new being and he is the one that brings us life. The revised version of this verse states what God was,the Word was.  John is basically saying that Jesus is equal in every aspect including dominion, and adoration.

1 Corinthians 3:16 says that we are the temple of God this basically means that God abides in us.  Romans 8 mentions that the same spirt that rose Jesus from the dead is the same spirit that is inside of us.  The Spirit examines everything, especially the depth of God. No one is able to understand the mind of God except through the Spirit.  In the upper room the Holy Spirit came down upon the apostles which gave them an authority and a special boldness. The Holy Spirit has emotions, Paul says in Ephesians that we can hurt the Holy Spirit and not to put out its fire.  The Holy Spirit sanctifies us and helps us live righteously on Earth.  In order for us to demonstrate the Holy Spirit, we should be witnesses everywhere we go about who Jesus is in our lives.

The Bible instructs that Jesus is the one and true living God. The thing about Jesus is that he was fully human as well as fully God and it is through his life that we have redemption of our sins. Since Jesus the human is also the eternal God, which has the same authority and glory to the Father, we are able to believe that he is able to give us our salvation. Jesus is awesome because he came to the earth as a human with no blemish, he died and rose again so that we can be identified with God the Father. The reason why Jesus became man is to truly be a presentation of us, he had to be enticed just like we are,

All three members of the Trinity are from heaven and not created. Throughout creation all members of the Trinity existed.  The Father has a special relationship with the Trinity. The Father was never conceived and does not come from any other members of the Trinity. The Bible never mentions every the Son and the Spirit disagreeing with the Father because they will all have the same mindset. The three members of the Trinity will always be in together on every circumstance.  Despite the Father who is the one brought the idea of salvation, Jesus Christ accomplished it for us and it is the Holy Spirit who brings it to application in our lives.  So there will never be any disagreement because it is never shown in God's word.

Every member of the Trinity has a special relationship with the Trinity and so does the Son. The Bible states that the Father begat the Son which can be confusing when we think of it in the human sense.  Revelation chapter 5 states that the Son is from heaven and that he is always been around. God from heaven enabled Jesus Christ come into the world through the Holy Spirit to defy odds. Anything that has to do with our human character, Christ placed it on himself.  Jesus was fully human and fully divine and we would not be saved if the Son did not take on human form. Jesus knew he left the heavenly glory to take upon our sins with his punishment.  The Son was still omnipotent, omnipresent, omniscient, which means he fully knew how salvation would be achieved. The son never gave up any of his divine qualities when he came in the form of a human.

The Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit all are eternal which have no beginning or end, Many early church councils such as Nicea and Constantinople came to the defense of the autonomous character of the Holy Spirit. In 381 the council of Constantinople was summoned to talk about the Macedonian controversy. The bishop of Constantinople said many conflicting things about the Holy Spirit that it was a establised individual like an angel. The Nicene Creed stated that the Holy Spirit is the Lord, gives life and is to be adored just like the Father and the Son. The teaching of the Holy Spirit eternal procession always had controversy. Some scholars had conflicts that the Holy Spirit came from the Father and others said that the Spirit came from both the Father and the Son. Galatians 4:6 mentions that the Holy Spirit is what enables us to be called his children.

In 589 A. D. a church council met in Toledo Spain and met to make a case for the teaching of where the Holy Spirit comes from. They added a latin term which was filoque which meant and the Son to the Nicene Creed.The Byzantine Empire was was the eastern portion of Rome rejected filoque from the West. They were trying to correlate the work of the Holy Spirit, is to glorify the Son,and the Spirit will bear witness to the Son.  Their argument was that all three members of the Trinity will allow God's glory to be fulfilled. What separated the East and the West on the doctine of Trinity was the concept of the filoque, or the double procession of the Holy Spirit.

The word ontological refers to being or existence. All three persons of the Trinity have the same value, authority, and adoration. We know that God is omnipresent and it refers to God is not consumed by time or controlled by it. Augustine gave us a simple explanation to understand in that the Father who loves the Son who is beloved and the Holy Spirit who communicates the love between them and within the very being of God, love is provided and also told of. The ontological Trinity is shown from Scripture as the relationship within God himsely beyond all creation.

There is really no specific person that has wrote the Apostle's Creed. In 200 AD there was a person named Tertullius which relates to a Roman Creed which has similarities with the Apostle's Creed. This creed is developed for candidates that want to be baptized, do you have belief in God the Father, the Son Jesus Christ and the Holy Spirit. The Apostle's Creed was meant to be a measure of faith and to keep the doctrines of the church in tact. The doctrines were meant to train up a set of leaders. The Apostle's Creed was generated to give aid to help people in faith remain faithful to the instructions of Jesus. The Apostle's creed rose to importance in order to fulfill the need, this was meant to be acceptable to every congregation that calls itself Christian. The Apostle's Creed is a story of a Christian's faith. The Apostles Creed was developed to help one share their faith easily.

There are many reasons why its important for the church to use a creed, one being that it is the building blocks of our faith. This creed serves as an anchor that holds a place together in place which gives energy and stability for the entire building. Christ Jesus is our chief cornerstone, in Christ the whole structure is put together and creates a holy temple of God. The church is not able to function without ground rules such as a firm foundation. The teachings of Jesus sets the foundation of our faith, as the disciples introduced Jesus to the world equals the Apostle's Creed. The Apostle's Creed is a summary of of the basic teachings of Jesus of who God is and how the Holy Spirit works out for our salvation. The Creed serves as a baseline which presents the biggest fundamentals of Christianity. The Apostle's Creed come from a logical sense which refers to God being our creator and believing in his divine authority.

The Gospels present the truths behind the birth, the life, ministry, death, the resurrection and the ascension. The Apostle's Creed argues for the divinity of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit. The Creed tells us about the Triune character of God.  God is the Father, God is the Son, and God is the Holy Spirit. The statement of Trinity is a declaration about who our God is in his nature. God is the Father who has ultimate authority who is the creator and sustainer of all things often shown as the loving parent. God the Son Jesus Christ became mortal man to deliver us from sin and its punishment.  God the Holy Spirit gives us a supernatural strength know that God is with us and it also convicts us when we sin. The Trinity is a complex teaching but is an essential part of the teaching of Christ and how we worship.

It is always important to be an active part of church because we are essentially the body of Christ.  We represent the temple of God and so we have to live out our faith daily.  Being involved in various ministries of the church will allow us to strengthen the gifts and talents God has blessed us with to bear fruit for his kingdom. Being an active part of church ministry allows us to fulfill Jesus own description of his church. Being unified with the church allows us to chase after unity with one another despite differences may be there. When we are an active part of church ministry it allows us to stand together with fellow believers of Christ which will make our sharing the gospel more effective. There are many Christians that become martyrs for Christ for standing up for their beliefs in the Word of God. Ephesians 4:11-13 states that Jesus has appointed some to become apostles, some to be prophets, some to be evangelists, and some to be pastors, and teachers, so that the church which is the body of Christ can be built up until we all reach unity in the faith and in the knowledge of the Son of God and become mature, attaining to the whole measure of the fullness of Christ. Being involved in the day to day ministries of the church allow us to keep to the main themes of the teachings of Jesus Christ.

The Apostles Creed is used to affirm that new believers of Christ has the basic teachings of Jesus.  The Creed helped the church worship and understand the basic principles of God. The Creed reaffirmed that God is the Father, God is the Son and God is the Holy Spirit. The Creed reminds us that Jesus came to fulfill the plan of God the Father in redeeming us from our sins by serving as the punishment for our sins on the cross of Calvary. The Apostle's Creed also helps us remember to praise God and remember what he did for the church. The Apostle's Creed served as a declaration of faith and our believe in the Trinity and that each individual of Trinity had an equal part in our salvation.

Scripture defines God as only one true God and that is what we as Christians believe. This equates to God having the ability to create, to punish and to save. Our faith in God is really essential to all that we believe in. We have to realize that God is in the middle of our lives and everything revolves around God. We have to remove our self pride or conceit and be rooted on the mind of Christ Jesus. In the beginning when God created the universe we are able to see God's characteristics that may not be visible but have a divine nature. Ontological Trinity has to do with its being or existence. The idea of ontology, all three persons of the Trinity are infinite, eternal and unchangeable. When we look at the economic Trinity, we see how they all have different roles, as well as things to do. Psalm 145:8-9 says that the Lord is gracious and compassionate,slow to anger and rich in love. The Lord is good to all and has compassion on all he has made. Romans 6:23, Apostle Paul says that the wages of sin is death but the gift of God is eternal life through Christ Jesus.  Sin is a separation from God and it puts us very far from Christ. The farther we go from Christ the more deeper we have got into sin.  Sin can be described in various ways such as missing the mark, being rebellious towards your spiritual authority and just being disobedient to the Scriptures. 1 John 3:4  mentions that everyone who sins breaks the law and in fact sin is lawlessness. Sin started in the garden of Eden with Adam and Eve refused to trust God and ate of the forbidden fruit of the tree of knowledge of good and evil. This is described as the fall for all of humanity. All three persons help us achieve salvation and they also act in love and on the other hand also upholds righteousness and judgement. When we first accept Jesus Christ as our personal savior, we are through the Holy Spirit made right with God by forgiving us of all the sins we have committed up until that point. 2 Thesallonians 2:13 says that God chose us to be saved through the sanctifying work of the Spirit and through belief in the truth.

The Bible states that God will not forgive the sins over every individual. In order for an individual to be forgiven we have to have complete assurance in God. We as an individual have a responsibility to  recognize God is in control, being submissive to him and trust that his mercy will endure forever. In Psalm 103 we read that God is slow to anger and abundant in love, he does not treat us as our sin deserve, for as high as the heavens are above the earth, so great is his love for those who fear him, the lord has compassion on all who fear him. The three stages are justification, sanctification, and glorification.  Justification is the process of redeeming us from our past sins. There were two important events affirmed that Jesus was Christ. In Matthew 16:15-17 as well as Mark 8:27-30 in addition to Luke 9:18-20. Jesus asked His disciples, "who do you say that I am?" Peter boldly replied that "You are the Christ, the Son of the Living God." Jesus blessed him and explained that this truth was not revealed by human understanding but by God the Father. Peter's words showed that he recognized Jesus as more than a prophet or a miracle worker. He was the promised Messiah foretold in the Old Testament. This confession was an important affirmation of the true identity for Jesus being the Christ. The second important even was the Transfiguration which was recorded in Matthew 17:1-8, Mark 9:2-8, as well as Luke 9:28-36. Here we see Jesus taking Peter, James, and John up a mountain where His face shone brightly and His clothes became white. Moses and Elijah appeared with Him, representing the Law and the Prophets. God's voice from heaven declared that "This is my Son." This was significant because Moses and Elijah were two of Israel's greatest leaders, yet God showed that Jesus was greater than both of them. He fulfilled their expectations as the final Davidic heir who came to bring God's kingdom to earth. Both of these events, Peter's confession and the Transfiguration gave the disciples confirmation of the identity of Jesus.

The main purpose of the temptation that Jesus endured was to prepare him for his mission and to prove that he truly was the Son of God. You can see this in both Matthew 4:1-11 as well as Luke 4:1-13. Here we see that after fasting for forty days in the wilderness, Jesus was tempted by Satan. While Adam failed when he faced temptation in the Garden of Eden, Jesus resisted every attack that was thrown at him. This shows perfect obedience even in his weakened physical state.
