Since rival demonic forces from the "kingdom of the air" were constantly fighting against the church, Paul wrote to encourage believers to stand firm. He uses military language to show that they are soldiers who must put on the full armor of God to fight from the position of Christ's ultimate victory. Ultimately, Paul wrote Ephesians to give believers a large scale vision of the Gospel, proving that God's plan is to defeat His enemies and unite the entire universe under the lordship of Jesus Christ.

Knowing the background of Ephesians is very important because Paul's letters were not just random theology papers but rather they were real pastoral messages written to help the first century believers deal with real world problems. When you take the time to learn about who wrote the letters, who received them, and the type of culture they lived in, the text makes alot more sense. When you explore these historical details, it helps us see exactly why Paul chose his specific vocabulary and themes. First of all, knowing that the primary audience was the church in Ephesus explains why Paul talks so much about spiritual powers and glory. Ephesus was a world class Roman city famous for its heavy involvement in occult magic and its deep devotion to the pagan goddess Artemis. You can see in Acts 19 where Paul's ministry directly clashed with these types of dark practices. With this background in mind, you can understand why Paul warns against fruitless deeds of darkness and commands believers to put on the whole armor of God. Because the city legally claimed that Artemis made Ephesus glorious, we can see why Paul flips this cultural imagery by writing that Christ is the true Lord who nurtures the church to make her His glorious bride. Secondly, knowing that the letter was meant to circulate throughout the surrounding churches like Colosse and Laodicea, this explains the unique style of the book. Paul knew the Ephesian church intimately but this is his only letter with absolutely no personal references or greetings. This background shows us that because Paul was writing to an audience that included believers he had never met, he had to speak in a general way. He chose the theme of the Kingdom of God because it was perfect tool that could solve the problems of multiple churches all at once. Some of this was personal sin, racial tension between Jews and Gentiles, and demonic attacks. Understanding this background helps us see that Paul's vision of the gospel was perfectly tailored to teach early Christians how to live under the rule of Jesus.

In the overall structure of Ephesians, Paul's opening sections of praise and prayer serve as the important theological foundation of the entire letter. Ephesians is divided into five major parts, saluation, a section of prayer, the main body, and final greetings. Unlike this other letters where he normally includes warm personal greetings to his friends, Paul uniquely uses extended praise and prayer right after his salutation to introduce his naming theme. By doing this, he sets up the big picture of what Christ has accomplished before giving any deadly rules to the church. First of all, the praise section in Chapters 1:3-14 serves as a grand celebration of God's sovereign rule, benevolence, and kingdom blessings. The part acts alot like an official ancient document honoring a great king. Paul praises God for choosing and pretesting His special people before time began. This shows His absolute authority over creation. He also focuses on the King's generosity. He highlights spiritual blessings like adoption, redemption through Christ's blood and the forgiveness for sins. Finally he points out to our secure inheritance in Christ which was a legal benefit only given to citizens of a kingdom. Secondly the prayer section in chapter 1: 15-23 shifts from praising the King to asking the Holy Spirit to mentally enlighten the readers. Paul prays that the believers will truly grasp the unmatched power of God which raised Jesus from the dead and enthroned Him far above all rival spiritual or demonic governments. This functions structurally to show that Christ is ruling as King specifically for the benefit of the church, which is His prized possession and physical body. To sum up, Paul's teaching on praise and prayer functions structurally to open the eye of believers to their royal identity, giving them the exact understanding and motivation they need to obey the strict kingdom code for living found in the rest of the letter.

In the main body of Ephesians, Paul explains how the kingdom of God works by breaking it down into three main areas; citizenship, administration, and a code for living. He goes on to use these concepts to contrast God's righteous kingdom of light with Satan's sinful kingdom of darkness. First of all, Paul describes citizenship as a total rescue mission from our old life. He reminds the readers that before salvation, all human beings are spiritually dead and trapped in the kingdom of darkness serving Satan. But because of His great mercy, God uses His royal power to breathe new life into believers and transfer their citizenship into the kingdom of light. This new citizenship completely destroys old racial and ethnic walls. Gentile delivers are not longer treated as second class outsiders or foreigners but through union with Christ, they are now full, equal co-citizens with Jewish believers in God's household. Secondly, Paul explains that a functional kingdom needs an administrative structure which God provided through church offices. In the early church, God managed His kingdom through the foundational office of the apostle. Men like Paul were personally chosen by God and given direct, perfect revelation through the Holy Spirit to teach the church and overrule false teachers. Today, while that specific office has ceased, the church still submits to this apostolic administration by following the teachings of the Scripture. Thirdly, Paul gives a strict code for living which acts as a practical handbook for kingdom citizens. This code covers church life where Christ gives spiritual gifts and leaders to equip ordinary citizens to serve one another. It commands moral purity, telling believers to strip off their old sinful habits and put on a new self that reflects the King's holy character. It also sets up domestic order showing that family and work relationships must be shaped by loving leadership and respectful submission. Finally, it drafts every citizen into a spiritual army suiting them up in the armor of God to stand firm against demonic forces. In the end, Paul teaches that because believers have a new royal identity, they just completely change how they live to honor their true King.

The reason Christians should work to build the kingdom of God is because helping it grow is an essential part of our calling and our response to God's grace. While humans do not create the kingdom by their own power, God explicitly calls believers to participate in His great building plan. Working to expand the church on earth allows us to honor our King, love our neighbors, and push back spiritual darkness. First of all, we need to build the kingdom because God created us new in Christ for the exact purpose of doing good works. Good works are not how we earn our salvation but rather they are the primary tools God uses to expand, purify, and care for His kingdom. When Christians actively preform these tasks, they accept their appointments and callings as servants of the King, adopting His goals and bringing Him real glory. Secondly we build the kingdom by preserving deep unity and breaking down social barriers. Paul uses the picture of a holy temple where Christ is the cornerstone and every Christian is an individual building stone. Building this temple means destroying pride, racial divisions, and wealth gaps, as well as treating all believers as equals. Thirdly, we build the kingdom by using our unique spiritual gifts to serve the church. Paul also compares the kingdom to a body where Christ is the head and the believers make up the physical parts. Church leaders are there to equip ordinary citizens for ministry so that every single member can do their part. This mutual service builds up the church in truth and love, protecting it from false teachings and helping it mature. In the end, working to build the kingdom allows the church to grow into a perfect dwelling place for God's spirit which progressively brings the entire world under the rule of Jesus.

Before this lesson, it was easy to think of the Gospel as a small personal message. Most people think it just means that Jesus forgives their individual sins so they can go to heaven when they die. While those personal beliefs are partially true, Paul shows that the real biblical gospel is actually alot bigger than that. His teachings connects our personal faith to a massive, universe sized plan centered entirely on the kingdom of God. Paul explains that the gospel is a royal announcement from a powerful King. It is the good news that King Jesus has arrived to defeat sin, conquer His enemies, and rescue His people from the control of Satan. Instead of just saving individuals one by one, Jesus is building a brand new kingdom community. This big picture connects our personal faith to big actions like stopping arguments between different races, staying morally pure and using our special spiritual gifts to help our local church family grow together. Paul also talks about living in a time where two ears overlap. We already belong to Jesus but we still have to live in a broken world where Satan's kingdom of darkness is active and trying to make us fail. That is why good deeds, testing our families with love and fighting spiritual battles are so important. They are not just extra rules that we have to follow to get to heaven but rather they are practical ways we show our true loyalty and devotion to our King. Paul shows us that the gospel is not just a private contract but rather a solid promise that Jesus will fix the entire universe and rule over us in peace.

How does understanding the diachronic trace of biblical events enrich your understanding of Scripture?

fields.title: About Us
fields.description:
Who We Are?

At Trinity Theological Seminary, you will not be a normal aspirant who takes admission, completes the course and leaves. Instead, we believe in building a relationship that lasts longer than most things do. Our aim is to build a leader out of the aspirant, preparing for the world that needs God’s grace.

That is the reason our faculties are trained in such a way to bring the best of leadership qualities from you, building a strong foundation of faith and faith based skills to be a change in this world.

With that, we will be there to mould your inner leadership qualities for a better tomorrow in the ministry field.

So, whether you are going to start Pastoral ministry or are already into it, building your knowledge base or preparing for higher studies, you will encounter God’s presence in every course we have.

As you now prepare for your pursuit of your Gods calling, we will be inspiring you to walk like our Lord Jesus walked at every step you encounter. We will be emphasizing and empowering your academic growth and spiritual development to prepare a leader for tomorrow out of you.

fields.title: Accreditation
fields.description:
Concerning seminary accreditation, the value of any accredited university accredited bible college or accredited online seminary degree is subjective, depending on the amount of work that went into earning it, the student’s attitude and aptitude, and external circumstances related to the school itself or to the graduate’s working world.

You should be aware that many Christian Private Schools, Bible Colleges, and Seminaries elect not to be governed by Department of Education of the each country and do not seek Regional Accreditation, which is more common among Secular Colleges and Universities. Christian Educational Ministries are automatically exempt from the dictates of both the Government and secular accreditation agencies. Trinity Theological Seminary, like other Christian Education Ministries, has full theological accreditation with ICTA (INTERNATIONAL COMMISSION FOR THEOLOGICAL ACCREDITATION, USA) &  IATA (INTERNATIONAL ASSOCIATION FOR THEOLOGICAL ACCREDITATION, INDIA ) which is recognized and respected as an acceptable form of accreditation for those in pursuit of ministry related avocations.

Trinity Theological Seminary theologically accredited institution of higher learning. Most accredited universities, accredited seminaries, accredited Bible colleges and accredited colleges have their own criteria for recognition and acceptability of online educational credits. The individual should always address specific questions to selected institutions in determining their particular criteria concerning accreditation.

Trinity Theological Seminary is an educational outreach ministry of Savior Foundation’s International Missions Worldwide. United States Government Approval We are recognized by the Government of the United States of America, as a Religious Organization with all rights and privileges as provided by law. Religious Organization with all rights and privileges as provided by law.

 

ABOUT ACCREDITATION

Throughout history there has always been some religious confusion and there is some controversy over the subject of accreditation today. But to clarify the issue:

  • There is secular education and there is religious education.
  • Secular schools seek secular accreditation, and sacred schools receive sacred accreditation – each by their own peers.
  • Religious institutions need no secular accreditation because they offer no secular degrees.
  • Secular accreditation associations in turn are recognized by governmental agencies. They trace their authority back up to the capitol of a country
  • Religious accrediting associations are recognized by the Church of Jesus Christ, which has no supreme central office on earth. Our authority is derived from Heaven.
  • Civil and religious interests are different and have separate realms of jurisdiction.
  • The state is not superior to the Church. The Church need not wait for approval from the secular world.
  • Civil agencies should not be dictating standards of Christian education, any more than a police officer should be directing the worship of God.
  • Theological Seminaries should not be accredited by accrediting associations that are “recognized” by an agency of the federal government, because it is contrary to the Biblical principle of “Separation of Church and State”, indicated by Christ when he said, “render to Caesar the things that are Caesar’s and to God the thing that are God’s.” Mark 12:7.
  • What business does a Christian educator have, going to the world of unbelievers for recognition and acknowledgment as II Cor. 6:14 says, “Be not equally yoked together with unbelievers: For what fellowship hath righteousness with unrighteousness?”

Trinity Theological seminary is affiliated with two major Accrediting Agencies viz INTERNATIONAL COMMISSION FOR THEOLOGICAL ACCREDITATION (ICTA) & IATAINTERNATIONAL ASSOCIATION FOR THEOLOGICAL ACCREDITATION (IATA).

As a theologically accredited Biblical seminary, we are not required, by the U.S. Dept. of Education or any other agency, to have regional accreditation nor are we subject to governmental or secular oversight. As such, our educational programs are not required to qualify our students for either governmental or secular certification. However, legally, our degrees are classified as theologically accredited and state authorized as exempt, which fully qualifies all degrees from Trinity Theological Seminary to be recorded professionally both on your resume and in personal employment records. You can be proud of the legitimacy of your Degrees from Trinity Theological Seminary.

Our ministries are recognized by the Government of the United States, as a Religious Organization. Since we are considerate of and obedient to all of the laws set by our government, as a Christ-centered biblical education ministry, our ultimate authority is God and as such we choose to remain free in our rights to teach degree programs based on the word of God as found in His Holy Bible. However, Because of our legal position based on the U.S. Constitution, NO outside agency has any authority over our educational content regarding our right to teach Bible-based educational programs leading to the award of appropriate certificates and degrees.

In the United States, accreditation of universities and seminaries is a voluntary process with accreditation granted by private, non-governmental agencies. Governmental agencies never provide theological accreditation.

Additionally, there is no national standard for educational accreditation, and the educational world is currently re-examining criteria for accreditation, focusing less on institutional inputs and more on educational outcomes.

There is no such requirement as Federal or State accreditation of a religious institution because the civil government has no authority to regulate religious teachings or which certificates or religious degrees upon completion of such education may be issued. This is a matter of separation of Church and State. Politicians and civil authorities must never be allowed to officially endorse or disapprove directly or indirectly the beliefs and practices of churches or their schools. A casual survey of Church history shows that such linkage with “Caesar” eventually leads to infringement upon conscience, bondage, and corruption. Therefore, to be accredited by any agency, which in turn is controlled by the U.S. Department of Education, would to some degree be a compromise of the separation principle and constitute a violation of the Church’s sovereignty. And Jesus came and spake unto them, saying, All power is given unto me in heaven and in earth.  Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost: Teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have commanded you: and, lo, I am with you alway, even unto the end of the world. Amen.Matt 28:18-20 (KJV)

We work with all of our students as close as we can to meet their particular budget.

fields.title: Doctoral Program
fields.description:
Doctor of Ministry (D. Min), Doctor of Divinity (DD), Doctorate in Theology (Th.D), Doctor of Philiosophy (Ph.D)

The Doctor of Ministry (D.Min), Doctorate in Theology (Th.D), Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D), Doctor of Divinity (DD)  are the highest professional degree for those in parish or related ministries. It is designed for educated, experienced practitioners of Christian faith, who desire to stimulate renewal in themselves, and in their ministries through advanced training, research and reflection. Busy ministry leaders need a tailor-made program that leverages high-impact online education and maximum practical application.

The International Association for Theological Accreditation (IATA) has authorized TTS to run its Doctoral programs. Hence, TTS’s Doctoral program in association with IATA has been designed to fulfill the vision God has given for your ministry and to provide advanced training and skills to reach there. This program has been designed with your specific needs in mind and our program specializes in the kind of personal and ministry transformation that is necessary to keep you alert and realize God’s best for your life and ministry. Our goal is to help you be all you need to be as a leader so you can do all God has for you to do in ministry.

The Doctorate degree is an advanced professional degree program designed for the continuing development of those involved in vocational ministry. This program is designed to enhance professional competence by expanding upon an initial foundation of theological studies and ministry experience, to enable those in vocational ministry to enhance current strengths, address areas of weakness, and increase overall effectiveness. Open to ministerial leaders anywhere in the world who meet qualifications for admission, have access to the Internet, and are proficient in online work.

Admissions Requirements

Ordinarily, applicants for the Doctoral program will be required to:

  • hold a bachelor’s degree from a regionally accredited college or university.
  • hold an M.Div.. M.Th., or any Masters degree or its equivalent from an accredited institution.
  • have spent at least FIVE YEARS in active ministry.
  • have earned a grade average of at least B+ (50%+) in their master’s program.
  • submit two letters of reference from people capable of assessing the applicant’s intellectual and academic ability, and two letters of reference (one from an ecclesial/church official and one from a lay person) that address the applicant’s performance in his or her current position of ministry.
  • submit two essays, one (two pages) describing their goals in undertaking doctoral study, including an indication of your proposed focus, and another (maximum 15 pages) that is a sample of their academic writing (e.g., an article, term paper, etc.)

ACADEMIC INFORMATION

Masters Program is used to define the study of different faiths and belief systems. In Christian theology, this degree prepares students to work as a pastor, priest, or in other parts of the ministry. This is the path for students who are interested in religious studies and pursuing work in the professional ministry. For students interested in teaching, an advanced degree can prepare you for a career in religious studies.

This program generally requires students to complete 91 Credit hours and focuses on various theologies, Old Testament, New Testament, church history, Pastoral Counseling, and more. TTS, Masters Program requires a thesis, upon completion of the program.

ACADEMIC INFORMATION:

Trinity Theological Seminary offers different Masters Program through online mode, which is fully accredited by the IATA (International Association of Theological Accreditation). Bachelor of Theology – B.Th

The Bachelor of Theology program is designed to prepare students for various Church ministries. This four year or 8 semester degree program is based on a solid Biblical and theological foundation. A wide range of practical and pastoral units allows specialization in a specific area of ministry.

In order to equip them with the advanced ministry skills and personal transformation necessary to lead their ministry to new levels of effectiveness, TTS, B.Th Program has been designed to help them:

  • Rethink the way you do ministry by giving you new critical and analytical thinking tools to effectively address the leadership-needy areas of your ministry.
  • Refocus on calling for your life and ministry to align them with your core values and best gifts with the goal of greater effectiveness and impact in ministry.
  • Retool with the advanced visioneering, leadership and management skills that provide new ways of addressing ministry for greater impact and effectiveness.

fields.title: A Message from the Founder
fields.description:
A Message from the Founder

Welcome to Trinity Theological Seminary!

Thank you for taking the time to visit us. It is a privilege to share with you the vision that God placed on my heart more than two decades ago.

In 2002, while serving as a missionary in India, I met many sincere believers who longed to study God's Word but were unable to attend a Bible college because of financial limitations, family responsibilities, ministry commitments, or geographical barriers. As I prayed about this need, the Lord gave me a clear vision: to make quality theological education accessible to everyone He has called into His service.

By God's grace, what began as a small ministry has grown into an international theological seminary, equipping pastors, missionaries, church leaders, and believers from around the world through affordable, fully online, and biblically faithful education.

At Trinity Theological Seminary, we believe education is more than earning a degree. It is about knowing Christ more deeply, understanding His Word more faithfully, and serving His Church more effectively. Our passion is to prepare leaders who are grounded in Scripture, empowered by the Holy Spirit, and committed to advancing the Kingdom of God with excellence and integrity.

Whether you are taking your first step into theological education or pursuing advanced ministry training, we would be honored to be part of your journey.

I warmly invite you to join the TTS family as, together, we equip lives, strengthen churches, and transform communities through the power of God's Word.

I look forward to welcoming you personally to Trinity Theological Seminary.

May God richly bless you.

In His Service,
Dr. Shibu Thomas, B.Sc., B.D., D.Min., Ph.D., MACMHC.
Founder & President
Trinity Theological Seminary

fields.title: Church Partnership Program
fields.description:
Church Partnership Program

At Trinity Theological Seminary, we believe in the vital role of the local church in cultivating disciples, equipping leaders, and expanding God's Kingdom. Our Church Partnership Program is designed to build a strong alliance between the seminary and local congregations to make quality theological education accessible and affordable for your church members.

Benefits of Partnership

  • Group Tuition Discounts: Custom scholarships and pricing structures for cohorts from partner churches.
  • Customized Cohorts: Study together in groups with dedicated mentorship.
  • Local Church-Centered Internships: Practical ministry requirements are completed directly in your local church context under pastoral guidance.

For more details on how your church can partner with TTS, contact our admissions office at trinitytheologicalseminary@gmail.com.

I am honored to write this personal statement in support of my friend Jaivi as he applies for Bible school. I have known Jaivi for many years and during that time I have seen his faith, character, and love for God grow in steady and meaningful ways. He is someone who lives out his faith daily and I truly believe God has called him to prepare for ministry. Jaivi has a sincere heart for God that shows in the way he lives. His faith is not just something he talks about, but something he practices through his actions, choices, and relationships. He values prayer, seeks wisdom, and desires to follow Godâs Word. Jaivi is humble, teachable, and always willing to learn, which are important qualities for someone pursuing ministry. One of the strongest examples of Jaiviâs calling is his role as a worship leader. He is musically talented, but his true strength is his heart for worship. When Jaivi leads, his focus is not on himself, but on pointing others to God. He leads with sincerity and respect for Godâs presence, helping others connect with Him through worship. Many people are encouraged and blessed through his leadership. Jaivi also has a strong desire to serve beyond the worship team. At one point, Jaivi and I served together in a church council setting. During that time, I was able to see his leadership skills up close. He listened well, shared thoughtful ideas, and approached decisions with prayer and care for the church. That experience showed me that Jaivi is a natural leader who values unity and seeks what is best for others. Jaivi is deeply committed to his family and understands that ministry begins at home. As a husband and father, he leads with love, patience, and integrity. He is a strong role model for his children and sets a positive example of what it means to follow God. This same example carries over into the church, where he is a positive influence on youth and others around him. Beginning in 2026, Jaivi and his wife will step into a leadership role in the childrenâs church ministry. This role shows their shared heart for serving God together and for investing in the next generation. Jaivi understands how important it is to teach children about God in a clear, loving, and safe environment. He and his wife are committed to helping children grow in their faith and to supporting the volunteers who serve alongside them. Jaivi has shared with me his desire to pursue ministry more fully. I told him about TTS because I am currently a student on the same ministry pathway and have seen how valuable the training has been. This opportunity fits well with Jaiviâs calling and desire to grow in his knowledge of Scripture and leadership. Jaiviâs desire to attend Bible school comes from a place of obedience and preparation. He wants to be equipped to serve God and others well. I believe he would be a great addition to your school and would use what he learns to bless others. I highly recommend Jaivi for this program. I am confident God is guiding his steps, and I believe this is an important part of his journey. Jaivi has the character, heart, and calling to make a lasting impact for Godâs Kingdom.

GRADUATE DIPLOMA IN MINISTRY

The Graduate Diploma in Ministry is a two-year Bible training program that provides you with an excellent foundation in theology and Christian ministry. It will equip you to serve in your church and community with a more informed attitude to ministry. However, it is not intended to provide sufficient training for people preparing for full-time ministry. The hardest thing about the Graduate Diploma is choosing just three electives. That's probably why many students who complete the diploma then move into the second year of the M.Div degree, as the same is considered as the first year (first 2 semesters of M. Div).

FRIT Graduate Diploma of Divinity requires the students to complete 64 credit points in full.

fields.post_content:
Bachelor of Theology - B.Th

The Bachelor of Theology program is designed to prepare students for various Church ministries. This four year or 8 semester degree program is based on a solid Biblical and theological foundation. A wide range of practical and pastoral units allows specialization in a specific area of ministry.

In order to equip them with the advanced ministry skills and personal transformation necessary to lead their ministry to new levels of effectiveness, TTS, B.Th Program has been designed to help them:

  • Rethink the way you do ministry by giving you new critical and analytical thinking tools to effectively address the leadership-needy areas of your ministry.
  • Refocus on calling for your life and ministry to align them with your core values and best gifts with the goal of greater effectiveness and impact in ministry.
  • Retool with the advanced visioneering, leadership and management skills that provide new ways of addressing ministry for greater impact and effectiveness.
  • Renew your passion for a healthy holistic and balanced approach to spiritual disciplines, relationships and your personal relationship with God.
  • Reorient your perspective in with a global and prophetic focus on reaching the lost with world-changing and Spirit-led influence and impact.

Admission Requirement for Bachelor of Theology

Candidates for the B.Th must have successfully completed the pre-university or its equivalent and must have 2-3 years ministry experience. Students who are appearing for exams or awaiting results may also apply. Such candidates may be given provisional admission and will have to produce the grades for the previous course completed. They should produce proof of successful completion before the end of the first semester. The duration of this course will be four years.

If the applicant is a matured candidate, he / she then must be above 18 years of age and must have passed 10th Standard + 3-5 years of ministry experience.

Diploma holders & Certificate holders in Theology (D.Th & C.Th) from a recognized theological institution can also apply.

Bachelor of Theology

Courses 20 = 60 Credits
1 Assignment for each Course 2 X20 =40 Credits
Two Readings for each Course 1X 20 = 20 Credits
Total = 120 Credit

Cost

Admission Form = $30.00
Enrolment Fee =$75.00
Tuition Fee for Each Course = $200.00 X 22 = $ 4400.00
Exam Fee for Each Exam = $50.00
Certification Fee =$250.00

ADMISSIONS TO B.Th IS YET TO START.

YOU ARE FREE TO E-MAIL US YOUR QUERIES TO: trinitytheologicalseminary@gmail.com

fields.post_content:
Doctor of Ministry (D. Min)

The Doctor of Ministry (D.Min) is the highest professional degree for those in parish or related ministries. It is designed for educated, experienced practitioners of Christian faith, who desire to stimulate renewal in themselves, and in their ministries through advanced training, research and reflection. Busy ministry leaders need a tailor-made program that leverages high-impact online education and maximum practical application. The International Association for Theological Accreditation (IATA) has authorized TTS to run its D.Min program. Hence, TTS's Doctor of Ministry (D.Min) program in association with IATA has been designed to fulfill the vision God has given for your ministry, and to provide advanced training and skills to reach there. This program has been designed with your specific needs in mind and our program specializes in the kind of personal and ministry transformation that is necessary to keep you alert and realize God's best for your life and ministry. Our goal is to help you be all you need to be as a leader so you can do all God has for you to do in ministry. The Doctor of Ministry degree is an advanced professional degree program designed for the continuing development of those involved in vocational ministry. This program is designed to enhance professional competence by expanding upon an initial foundation of theological studies and ministry experience, to enable those in vocational ministry to enhance current strengths, address areas of weakness, and increase overall effectiveness. Open to ministerial leaders anywhere in the world who meet qualifications for admission, have access to the Internet, and are proficient in online work.

Admissions Requirements

Ordinarily, applicants for the D. Min program will be required to:  
  • hold a bachelor's degree from a regionally accredited college or university.
  • hold an M.Div. degree or its equivalent from an accredited institution.
  • have spent at least FIVE YEARS in active ministry.
  • have earned a grade average of at least B+ (50%+) in their master's program.
  • submit two letters of reference from people capable of assessing the applicant's intellectual and academic ability, and two letters of reference (one from an ecclesial/church official and one from a lay person) that address the applicant's performance in his or her current position of ministry.
  • submit two essays, one (two pages) describing their goals in undertaking doctoral study, including an indication of your proposed focus, and another (maximum 15 pages) that is a sample of their academic writing (e.g., an article, term paper, etc.)

ACADEMIC INFORMATION

D. Min is a three year program, designed for Pastors and Christian Leaders. The Doctoral student is expected to take 10 courses out of the 22 courses offered, which should be 1,890 class hours* + Dissertation. The courses offered are the following:

[vc_row full_height="yes" columns_placement="top" content_placement="top" parallax="content-moving-fade" parallax_image="3406" u_row_style="1" u_row_paralax="0" u_row_scheme="1"][vc_column][u_heading]A complete online Theological Educational Institution Accredited by International Association for Theological Accreditation[/u_heading][vc_column_text]
Trinity Theological Seminary online seminary is run by Saviour Foundation Inc. Registerd under the law of USA. Programs offer both Undergraduate and Graduate studies in a number of Christian majors. Bachelor Degree, Master Degree, and Doctorate Degree Programs are offered with courses that build foundational blocks to allow students to easily move not only from one course to another, but also provide the incentive to move on towards the next level of degree studies with accomplished core courses. The courses are structured in a simple format to provide students basic understanding of the main principles allowing the students to move through their degree courses, and in turn their programs at a faster pace. Since online students study independently at their own pace., TTS Model allows those that are motivated to complete their studies much sooner than in traditionally controlled programs. Although you study at your own pace, their is always access to a personal academic advisor that will assist you when needed. Students will work from the TTS Model. Course instructions, textbooks, and required assignments are provided for each course in the TTS Model. Students even upload their completed assignments directly to the TTS Model making it a secure way to submit course work. No need to postal mail your completed work, simply upload to the TTS Model system. Structure within the Graduate Studies in the Accelerated Academic Degree Programs (AADP). This program allows students that have completed previous studies in compatible courses to complete their program in as little as 12 weeks to 1 year. With the online program structure and format, self-paced courses, and the support systems in place for completing the degree programs in the least amount of time possible, TTS has become a leading online seminary.

[vc_row][vc_column][vc_column_text]A Complete online Theological Educational Institution Accreditated by International Association for Theological Accreditation[/vc_column_text][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row][vc_column][vc_column_text]

Trinity Theological Seminary online seminary is run by Saviour Foundation Inc. Registerd under the law of USA. Programs offer both Undergraduate and Graduate studies in a number of Christian majors. Bachelor Degree, Master Degree, and Doctorate Degree Programs are offered with courses that build foundational blocks to allow students to easily move not only from one course to another, but also provide the incentive to move on towards the next level of degree studies with accomplished core courses. The courses are structured in a simple format to provide students basic understanding of the main principles allowing the students to move through their degree courses, and in turn their programs at a faster pace. Since online students study independently at their own pace., TTS Model allows those that are motivated to complete their studies much sooner than in traditionally controlled programs. Although you study at your own pace, their is always access to a personal academic advisor that will assist you when needed. Students will work from the TTS Model. Course instructions, textbooks, and required assignments are provided for each course in the TTS Model. Students even upload their completed assignments directly to the TTS Model making it a secure way to submit course work. No need to postal mail your completed work, simply upload to the TTS Model system. Structure within the Graduate Studies in the Accelerated Academic Degree Programs (AADP). This program allows students that have completed previous studies in compatible courses to complete their program in as little as 12 weeks to 1 year. With the online program structure and format, self-paced courses, and the support systems in place for completing the degree programs in the least amount of time possible, TTS has become a leading online seminary.
[/vc_column_text][/vc_column][/vc_row]

ABOUT ACCREDITATION

Throughout history there has always been some religious confusion and there is some controversy over the subject of accreditation today. But to clarify the issue:

  • There is secular education and there is religious education.
  • Secular schools seek secular accreditation, and sacred schools receive sacred accreditation - each by their own peers.
  • Religious institutions need no secular accreditation because they offer no secular degrees.
  • Secular accreditation associations in turn are recognized by governmental agencies. They trace their authority back up to the capitol of a country
  • Religious accrediting associations are recognized by the Church of Jesus Christ, which has no supreme central office on earth. Our authority is derived from Heaven.
  • Civil and religious interests are different and have separate realms of jurisdiction.
  • The state is not superior to the Church. The Church need not wait for approval from the secular world.
  • Civil agencies should not be dictating standards of Christian education, any more than a police officer should be directing the worship of God.
  • Theological Seminaries should not be accredited by accrediting associations that are "recognized" by an agency of the federal government, because it is contrary to the Biblical principle of "Separation of Church and State", indicated by Christ when he said, "render to Caesar the things that are Caesar's and to God the thing that are God's." Mark 12:7.
  • What business does a Christian educator have, going to the world of unbelievers for recognition and acknowledgment as II Cor. 6:14 says, "Be not equally yoked together with unbelievers: For what fellowship hath righteousness with unrighteousness?"

Trinity Theological seminary is affiliated with two major Accrediting Agencies viz INTERNATIONAL COMMISSION FOR THEOLOGICAL ACCREDITATION (ICTA) & IATAINTERNATIONAL ASSOCIATION FOR THEOLOGICAL ACCREDITATION (IATA).

As a theologically accredited Biblical seminary, we are not required, by the U.S. Dept. of Education or any other agency, to have regional accreditation nor are we subject to governmental or secular oversight. As such, our educational programs are not required to qualify our students for either governmental or secular certification. However, legally, our degrees are classified as theologically accredited and state authorized as exempt, which fully qualifies all degrees from Trinity Theological Seminary to be recorded professionally both on your resume and in personal employment records. You can be proud of the legitimacy of your Degrees from Trinity Theological Seminary.

Our ministries are recognized by the Government of the United States, as a Religious Organization. Since we are considerate of and obedient to all of the laws set by our government, as a Christ-centered biblical education ministry, our ultimate authority is God and as such we choose to remain free in our rights to teach degree programs based on the word of God as found in His Holy Bible. However, Because of our legal position based on the U.S. Constitution, NO outside agency has any authority over our educational content regarding our right to teach Bible-based educational programs leading to the award of appropriate certificates and degrees.

In the United States, accreditation of universities and seminaries is a voluntary process with accreditation granted by private, non-governmental agencies. Governmental agencies never provide theological accreditation.

Additionally, there is no national standard for educational accreditation, and the educational world is currently re-examining criteria for accreditation, focusing less on institutional inputs and more on educational outcomes.

There is no such requirement as Federal or State accreditation of a religious institution because the civil government has no authority to regulate religious teachings or which certificates or religious degrees upon completion of such education may be issued. This is a matter of separation of Church and State. Politicians and civil authorities must never be allowed to officially endorse or disapprove directly or indirectly the beliefs and practices of churches or their schools. A casual survey of Church history shows that such linkage with "Caesar" eventually leads to infringement upon conscience, bondage, and corruption. Therefore, to be accredited by any agency, which in turn is controlled by the U.S. Department of Education, would to some degree be a compromise of the separation principle and constitute a violation of the Church's sovereignty.

And Jesus came and spake unto them, saying, All power is given unto me in heaven and in earth. Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost: Teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have commanded you: and, lo, I am with you alway, even unto the end of the world. Amen.Matt 28:18-20 (KJV)

Doctor of Ministry (D. Min)

The Doctor of Ministry (D.Min) is the highest professional degree for those in parish or related ministries. It is designed for educated, experienced practitioners of Christian faith, who desire to stimulate renewal in themselves, and in their ministries through advanced training, research and reflection. Busy ministry leaders need a tailor-made program that leverages high-impact online education and maximum practical application. The International Association for Theological Accreditation (IATA) has authorized TTS to run its D.Min program. Hence, TTS's Doctor of Ministry (D.Min) program in association with IATA has been designed to fulfill the vision God has given for your ministry, and to provide advanced training and skills to reach there. This program has been designed with your specific needs in mind and our program specializes in the kind of personal and ministry transformation that is necessary to keep you alert and realize God's best for your life and ministry. Our goal is to help you be all you need to be as a leader so you can do all God has for you to do in ministry. The Doctor of Ministry degree is an advanced professional degree program designed for the continuing development of those involved in vocational ministry. This program is designed to enhance professional competence by expanding upon an initial foundation of theological studies and ministry experience, to enable those in vocational ministry to enhance current strengths, address areas of weakness, and increase overall effectiveness. Open to ministerial leaders anywhere in the world who meet qualifications for admission, have access to the Internet, and are proficient in online work.

Admissions Requirements

Ordinarily, applicants for the D. Min program will be required to:  
  • hold a bachelor's degree from a regionally accredited college or university.
  • hold an M.Div. degree or its equivalent from an accredited institution.
  • have spent at least FIVE YEARS in active ministry.
  • have earned a grade average of at least B+ (50%+) in their master's program.
  • submit two letters of reference from people capable of assessing the applicant's intellectual and academic ability, and two letters of reference (one from an ecclesial/church official and one from a lay person) that address the applicant's performance in his or her current position of ministry.
  • submit two essays, one (two pages) describing their goals in undertaking doctoral study, including an indication of your proposed focus, and another (maximum 15 pages) that is a sample of their academic writing (e.g., an article, term paper, etc.)

In Christian theology, this degree prepares students to work as a pastor, priest, or in other parts of the ministry. This is the path for students who are interested in religious studies and pursuing work in the professional ministry. For students interested in teaching, an advanced degree can prepare you for a career in religious studies.

This program generally requires students to complete 91 Credit hours and focuses on various theologies, Old Testament, New Testament, church history, Pastoral Counseling, and more. TTS, M.Div. requires a thesis, upon completion of the program.

ACADEMIC INFORMATION:

Trinity Theological Seminary offers Master of Divinity (M.Div.) through online mode, which is fully accredited by the IATA (International Association of Theological Accreditation). B.Th. graduates from accredited / affiliated colleges.

Doctor of Ministry (D. Min)

The Doctor of Ministry (D.Min) is the highest professional degree for those in parish or related ministries. It is designed for educated, experienced practitioners of Christian faith, who desire to stimulate renewal in themselves, and in their ministries through advanced training, research and reflection. Busy ministry leaders need a tailor-made program that leverages high-impact online education and maximum practical application. The International Association for Theological Accreditation (IATA) has authorized TTS to run its D.Min program. Hence, TTS's Doctor of Ministry (D.Min) program in association with IATA has been designed to fulfill the vision God has given for your ministry, and to provide advanced training and skills to reach there. This program has been designed with your specific needs in mind and our program specializes in the kind of personal and ministry transformation that is necessary to keep you alert and realize God's best for your life and ministry. Our goal is to help you be all you need to be as a leader so you can do all God has for you to do in ministry. The Doctor of Ministry degree is an advanced professional degree program designed for the continuing development of those involved in vocational ministry. This program is designed to enhance professional competence by expanding upon an initial foundation of theological studies and ministry experience, to enable those in vocational ministry to enhance current strengths, address areas of weakness, and increase overall effectiveness. Open to ministerial leaders anywhere in the world who meet qualifications for admission, have access to the Internet, and are proficient in online work.

Admissions Requirements

Ordinarily, applicants for the D. Min program will be required to:  
  • hold a bachelor's degree from a regionally accredited college or university.
  • hold an M.Div. degree or its equivalent from an accredited institution.
  • have spent at least FIVE YEARS in active ministry.
  • have earned a grade average of at least B+ (50%+) in their master's program.
  • submit two letters of reference from people capable of assessing the applicant's intellectual and academic ability, and two letters of reference (one from an ecclesial/church official and one from a lay person) that address the applicant's performance in his or her current position of ministry.
  • submit two essays, one (two pages) describing their goals in undertaking doctoral study, including an indication of your proposed focus, and another (maximum 15 pages) that is a sample of their academic writing (e.g., an article, term paper, etc.)

ACADEMIC INFORMATION

D. Min is a three year program, designed for Pastors and Christian Leaders. The Doctoral student is expected to take 10 courses out of the 22 courses offered, which should be 1,890 class hours* + Dissertation. The courses offered are the following:

fields.post_content:
GRADUATE DIPLOMA IN MINISTRY

The Graduate Diploma in Ministry is a two-year Bible training program that provides you with an excellent foundation in theology and Christian ministry. It will equip you to serve in your church and community with a more informed attitude to ministry. However, it is not intended to provide sufficient training for people preparing for full-time ministry. The hardest thing about the Graduate Diploma is choosing just three electives. That's probably why many students who complete the diploma then move into the second year of the M.Div degree, as the same is considered as the first year (first 2 semesters of M. Div).

FRIT Graduate Diploma of Divinity requires the students to complete 64 credit points in full.


CURRICULUM OF GRADUATE DIPLOMA IN MINISTRY

YEAR 1

1st SEMESTER Credit Hours
Introduction to Old Testament 4
Introduction to New Testament 4
Life & Ministry of Jesus Christ 4
Book of Acts 3
2nd SEMESTER Credit Hours
Contemporary trends in Mission 3
Major World Religions 3
Theology 1 4
Church History 1 4
3rd SEMESTER Credit Hours
Book of Romans 3
1 & 2 Epistles to Corinthians 3
Theology 2 4
Church History 2 4
4th SEMESTER Credit Hours
Major World Religions 3
Pastoral Care & Counseling 3
Thesis - 15,000 words 20
TOTAL CREDIT HOURS 69

Admission Requirements

The Graduate Diploma provides a two-year program of study for all who has completed 12th Standard with no formal qualifications in theology, Plus...One year of Ministry experience

Or

Graduate in any discipline

Trinity Theological Seminary online seminary is run by Saviour Foundation Inc. Registerd under the law of USA. Programs offer both Undergraduate and Graduate studies in a number of Christian majors. Bachelor Degree, Master Degree, and Doctorate Degree Programs are offered with courses that build foundational blocks to allow students to easily move not only from one course to another, but also provide the incentive to move on towards the next level of degree studies with accomplished core courses. The courses are structured in a simple format to provide students basic understanding of the main principles allowing the students to move through their degree courses, and in turn their programs at a faster pace. Since online students study independently at their own pace., TTS Model allows those that are motivated to complete their studies much sooner than in traditionally controlled programs. Although you study at your own pace, their is always access to a personal academic advisor that will assist you when needed. Students will work from the TTS Model. Course instructions, textbooks, and required assignments are provided for each course in the TTS Model. Students even upload their completed assignments directly to the TTS Model making it a secure way to submit course work. No need to postal mail your completed work, simply upload to the TTS Model system. Structure within the Graduate Studies in the Accelerated Academic Degree Programs (AADP). This program allows students that have completed previous studies in compatible courses to complete their program in as little as 12 weeks to 1 year. With the online program structure and format, self-paced courses, and the support systems in place for completing the degree programs in the least amount of time possible, TTS has become a leading online seminary.

Doctor of Ministry (D. Min)

The Doctor of Ministry (D.Min) is the highest professional degree for those in parish or related ministries. It is designed for educated, experienced practitioners of Christian faith, who desire to stimulate renewal in themselves, and in their ministries through advanced training, research and reflection. Busy ministry leaders need a tailor-made program that leverages high-impact online education and maximum practical application. The International Association for Theological Accreditation (IATA) has authorized TTS to run its D.Min program. Hence, TTS's Doctor of Ministry (D.Min) program in association with IATA has been designed to fulfill the vision God has given for your ministry, and to provide advanced training and skills to reach there. This program has been designed with your specific needs in mind and our program specializes in the kind of personal and ministry transformation that is necessary to keep you alert and realize God's best for your life and ministry. Our goal is to help you be all you need to be as a leader so you can do all God has for you to do in ministry. The Doctor of Ministry degree is an advanced professional degree program designed for the continuing development of those involved in vocational ministry. This program is designed to enhance professional competence by expanding upon an initial foundation of theological studies and ministry experience, to enable those in vocational ministry to enhance current strengths, address areas of weakness, and increase overall effectiveness. Open to ministerial leaders anywhere in the world who meet qualifications for admission, have access to the Internet, and are proficient in online work.

Admissions Requirements

Ordinarily, applicants for the D. Min program will be required to:  
  • hold a bachelor's degree from a regionally accredited college or university.
  • hold an M.Div. degree or its equivalent from an accredited institution.
  • have spent at least FIVE YEARS in active ministry.
  • have earned a grade average of at least B+ (50%+) in their master's program.
  • submit two letters of reference from people capable of assessing the applicant's intellectual and academic ability, and two letters of reference (one from an ecclesial/church official and one from a lay person) that address the applicant's performance in his or her current position of ministry.
  • submit two essays, one (two pages) describing their goals in undertaking doctoral study, including an indication of your proposed focus, and another (maximum 15 pages) that is a sample of their academic writing (e.g., an article, term paper, etc.)

Master of Divinity (M. Div)

Master of Divinity is used to define the study of different faiths and belief systems. In Christian theology, this degree prepares students to work as a pastor, priest, or in other parts of the ministry. This is the path for students who are interested in religious studies and pursuing work in the professional ministry. For students interested in teaching, an advanced degree can prepare you for a career in religious studies.

This program generally requires students to complete 91 Credit hours and focuses on various theologies, Old Testament, New Testament, church history, Pastoral Counseling, and more. TTS, M.Div. requires a thesis, upon completion of the program.

ACADEMIC INFORMATION:

Trinity Theological Seminary offers Master of Divinity (M.Div.) through online mode, which is fully accredited by the IATA (International Association of Theological Accreditation). M.Div. requires 91 credit hours. The program is exclusively online. Courses consists independent study, where the student simply takes courses without traveling to a physical classroom. Performance of the candidate is evaluated on the basis of assignments and reading reports thesis and an online VIVA conducted at the end.

FRIT Master of Divinity is a six semester (3 year) course.


Admission Requirements:

Candidates who are applying for the M.Div. degree must qualify under one of the following categories: Be a graduate of any recognized university. While students who have successfully completed their degrees are preferred, students who are in the final year of studies or awaiting results may also apply. Such candidates will be given provisional admission. They should produce their pass certificate before the end of the second semester (within 1 year of provisional admission at FRIT, otherwise the admission will stand cancelled and all the payments done to FRIT will stand forfeited, i.e., no refund).

B.Th. graduates from accredited / affiliated colleges.

Candidates, who do not have the necessary academic requirements but are above 20 years of age, are eligible to apply as mature candidates. They will be required to pass the online entrance examination in English, Bible and General Knowledge.

Bachelor of Theology - B.Th

The Bachelor of Theology program is designed to prepare students for various Church ministries. This four year or 8 semester degree program is based on a solid Biblical and theological foundation. A wide range of practical and pastoral units allows specialization in a specific area of ministry.

In order to equip them with the advanced ministry skills and personal transformation necessary to lead their ministry to new levels of effectiveness, TTS, B.Th Program has been designed to help them:

  • Rethink the way you do ministry by giving you new critical and analytical thinking tools to effectively address the leadership-needy areas of your ministry.
  • Refocus on calling for your life and ministry to align them with your core values and best gifts with the goal of greater effectiveness and impact in ministry.
  • Retool with the advanced visioneering, leadership and management skills that provide new ways of addressing ministry for greater impact and effectiveness.
  • Renew your passion for a healthy holistic and balanced approach to spiritual disciplines, relationships and your personal relationship with God.
  • Reorient your perspective in with a global and prophetic focus on reaching the lost with world-changing and Spirit-led influence and impact.

Admission Requirement for Bachelor of Theology

Candidates for the B.Th must have successfully completed the pre-university or its equivalent and must have 2-3 years ministry experience. Students who are appearing for exams or awaiting results may also apply. Such candidates may be given provisional admission and will have to produce the grades for the previous course completed. They should produce proof of successful completion before the end of the first semester. The duration of this course will be four years.

If the applicant is a matured candidate, he / she then must be above 18 years of age and must have passed 10th Standard + 3-5 years of ministry experience.

Diploma holders & Certificate holders in Theology (D.Th & C.Th) from a recognized theological institution can also apply.

Total = 120 Credit

GRADUATE DIPLOMA IN MINISTRY

The Graduate Diploma in Ministry is a two-year Bible training program that provides you with an excellent foundation in theology and Christian ministry. It will equip you to serve in your church and community with a more informed attitude to ministry. However, it is not intended to provide sufficient training for people preparing for full-time ministry. The hardest thing about the Graduate Diploma is choosing just three electives. That's probably why many students who complete the diploma then move into the second year of the M.Div degree, as the same is considered as the first year (first 2 semesters of M. Div).

FRIT Graduate Diploma of Divinity requires the students to complete 64 credit points in full.


CURRICULUM FOR CERTIFICATE IN THEOLOGY

YEAR 1

Concerning seminary accreditation; the value of any accredited university, accredited bible college or accredited online seminary degree is subjective, depending on the amount of work that went into earning it, the student's attitude and aptitude, and external circumstances related to the school itself or to the graduate's working world.

You should be aware that many Christian Private Schools, Bible Colleges and Seminaries elect not to be governed by Department of Education of the each country and do not seek Regional Accreditation, which is more common among Secular Colleges and Universities. Christian Educational Ministries are automatically exempt from the dictates of both the Government and secular accreditation agencies. Trinity Theological Seminary, like other Christian Education Ministries, has full theological accreditation with IATA (INTERNATIONAL ASSOCIATION FOR THEOLOGICAL ACCREDITATION ) which is recognized and respected as an acceptable form of accreditation for those in pursuit of ministry related avocations.

Trinity Theological Seminary theologically accredited institution of higher learning. Most accredited universities, accredited seminaries, accredited Bible colleges and accredited colleges have their own criteria for recognition and acceptability of online educational credits. The individual should always address specific questions to selected institutions in determining their particular criteria concerning accreditation.

Trinity Theological Seminary is an educational outreach ministry of Savior Foundation's International Missions Worldwide. United States Government Approval We are recognized by the Government of the United States of America, as a Religious Organization with all rights and privileges as provided by law. Religious Organization with all rights and privileges as provided by law.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row][vc_column el_class="about_left"][vc_column_text css=".vc_custom_1494014141390{background-color: #f4f4f4 !important;}"]

ABOUT ACCREDITATION

Throughout history there has always been some religious confusion and there is some controversy over the subject of accreditation today. But to clarify the issue:

  • There is secular education and there is religious education.
  • Secular schools seek secular accreditation, and sacred schools receive sacred accreditation - each by their own peers.
  • Religious institutions need no secular accreditation because they offer no secular degrees.
  • Secular accreditation associations in turn are recognized by governmental agencies. They trace their authority back up to the capitol of a country
  • Religious accrediting associations are recognized by the Church of Jesus Christ, which has no supreme central office on earth. Our authority is derived from Heaven.
  • Civil and religious interests are different and have separate realms of jurisdiction.
  • The state is not superior to the Church. The Church need not wait for approval from the secular world.
  • Civil agencies should not be dictating standards of Christian education, any more than a police officer should be directing the worship of God.
  • Theological Seminaries should not be accredited by accrediting associations that are "recognized" by an agency of the federal government, because it is contrary to the Biblical principle of "Separation of Church and State", indicated by Christ when he said, "render to Caesar the things that are Caesar's and to God the thing that are God's." Mark 12:7.
  • What business does a Christian educator have, going to the world of unbelievers for recognition and acknowledgment as II Cor. 6:14 says, "Be not equally yoked together with unbelievers: For what fellowship hath righteousness with unrighteousness?"

Trinity Theological seminary is affiliated with INTERNATIONAL ASSOCIATION FOR THEOLOGICAL ACCREDITATION (IATA). IATA is recognized worldwide for Theological Accreditation and more than 800 Theological Institutions throughout the world are affiliated to IATA.

As a theologically accredited Biblical seminary, we are not required, by the U.S. Dept. of Education or any other agency, to have regional accreditation nor are we subject to governmental or secular oversight. As such, our educational programs are not required to qualify our students for either governmental or secular certification. However, legally, our degrees are classified as theologically accredited and state authorized as exempt, which fully qualifies all degrees from Trinity Theological Seminary to be recorded professionally both on your resume and in personal employment records. You can be proud of the legitimacy of your Degrees from Trinity Theological Seminary.

Our ministries are recognized by the Government of the United States, as a Religious Organization. Since we are considerate of and obedient to all of the laws set by our government, as a Christ centered biblical education ministry, our ultimate authority is God and as such we choose to remain free in our rights to teach degree programs based on the word of God as found in His Holy Bible. However, Because of our legal position based on the U.S. Constitution, NO outside agency has any authority over our educational content regarding our right to teach Bible based educational programs leading to the award of appropriate certificates and degrees.

In the United States, accreditation of universities and seminaries is a voluntary process with accreditation granted by private, non-governmental agencies. Governmental agencies never provide theological accreditation.

Additionally, there is no national standard for educational accreditation, and the educational world is currently re-examining criteria for accreditation, focusing less on institutional inputs and more on educational outcomes.

There is no such requirement as Federal or State accreditation of a religious institution, because the civil government has no authority to regulate religious teachings or which certificates or religious degrees upon completion of such education may be issued. This is a matter of separation of Church and State. Politicians and civil authorities must never be allowed to officially endorse or disapprove directly or indirectly the beliefs and practices of churches or their schools. A casual survey of Church history shows that such linkage with "Caesar" eventually leads to infringement upon conscience, bondage, and corruption. Therefore, to be accredited by any agency, which in turn is controlled by the U.S. Department of Education, would to some degree be a compromise of the separation principle and constitute a violation of the Church's sovereignty.

And Jesus came and spake unto them, saying, All power is given unto me in heaven and in earth. Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost: Teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have commanded you: and, lo, I am with you alway, even unto the end of the world. Amen.Matt 28:18-20 (KJV)

[/vc_column_text][/vc_column][/vc_row]

ABOUT ACCREDITATION

Throughout history there has always been some religious confusion and there is some controversy over the subject of accreditation today. But to clarify the issue:
  • There is secular education and there is religious education.
  • Secular schools seek secular accreditation, and sacred schools receive sacred accreditation - each by their own peers.
  • Religious institutions need no secular accreditation because they offer no secular degrees.
  • Secular accreditation associations in turn are recognized by governmental agencies. They trace their authority back up to the capitol of a country
  • Religious accrediting associations are recognized by the Church of Jesus Christ, which has no supreme central office on earth. Our authority is derived from Heaven.
  • Civil and religious interests are different and have separate realms of jurisdiction.
  • The state is not superior to the Church. The Church need not wait for approval from the secular world.
  • Civil agencies should not be dictating standards of Christian education, any more than a police officer should be directing the worship of God.
  • Theological Seminaries should not be accredited by accrediting associations that are "recognized" by an agency of the federal government, because it is contrary to the Biblical principle of "Separation of Church and State", indicated by Christ when he said, "render to Caesar the things that are Caesar's and to God the thing that are God's." Mark 12:7.
  • What business does a Christian educator have, going to the world of unbelievers for recognition and acknowledgment as II Cor. 6:14 says, "Be not equally yoked together with unbelievers: For what fellowship hath righteousness with unrighteousness?"
Trinity Theological seminary is affiliated with INTERNATIONAL ASSOCIATION FOR THEOLOGICAL ACCREDITATION (IATA). IATA is recognized worldwide for Theological Accreditation and more than 800 Theological Institutions throughout the world are affiliated to IATA. As a theologically accredited Biblical seminary, we are not required, by the U.S. Dept. of Education or any other agency, to have regional accreditation nor are we subject to governmental or secular oversight. As such, our educational programs are not required to qualify our students for either governmental or secular certification. However, legally, our degrees are classified as theologically accredited and state authorized as exempt, which fully qualifies all degrees from Trinity Theological Seminary to be recorded professionally both on your resume and in personal employment records. You can be proud of the legitimacy of your Degrees from Trinity Theological Seminary. Our ministries are recognized by the Government of the United States, as a Religious Organization. Since we are considerate of and obedient to all of the laws set by our government, as a Christ centered biblical education ministry, our ultimate authority is God and as such we choose to remain free in our rights to teach degree programs based on the word of God as found in His Holy Bible. However, Because of our legal position based on the U.S. Constitution, NO outside agency has any authority over our educational content regarding our right to teach Bible based educational programs leading to the award of appropriate certificates and degrees. In the United States, accreditation of universities and seminaries is a voluntary process with accreditation granted by private, non-governmental agencies. Governmental agencies never provide theological accreditation. Additionally, there is no national standard for educational accreditation, and the educational world is currently re-examining criteria for accreditation, focusing less on institutional inputs and more on educational outcomes. There is no such requirement as Federal or State accreditation of a religious institution, because the civil government has no authority to regulate religious teachings or which certificates or religious degrees upon completion of such education may be issued. This is a matter of separation of Church and State. Politicians and civil authorities must never be allowed to officially endorse or disapprove directly or indirectly the beliefs and practices of churches or their schools. A casual survey of Church history shows that such linkage with "Caesar" eventually leads to infringement upon conscience, bondage, and corruption. Therefore, to be accredited by any agency, which in turn is controlled by the U.S. Department of Education, would to some degree be a compromise of the separation principle and constitute a violation of the Church's sovereignty.   And Jesus came and spake unto them, saying, All power is given unto me in heaven and in earth. Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost: Teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have commanded you: and, lo, I am with you alway, even unto the end of the world. Amen.Matt 28:18-20 (KJV)[/vc_column_text][/vc_column][/vc_row]

ABOUT ACCREDITATION

Throughout history there has always been some religious confusion and there is some controversy over the subject of accreditation today. But to clarify the issue:

  • There is secular education and there is religious education.
  • Secular schools seek secular accreditation, and sacred schools receive sacred accreditation - each by their own peers.
  • Religious institutions need no secular accreditation because they offer no secular degrees.
  • Secular accreditation associations in turn are recognized by governmental agencies. They trace their authority back up to the capitol of a country
  • Religious accrediting associations are recognized by the Church of Jesus Christ, which has no supreme central office on earth. Our authority is derived from Heaven.
  • Civil and religious interests are different and have separate realms of jurisdiction.
  • The state is not superior to the Church. The Church need not wait for approval from the secular world.
  • Civil agencies should not be dictating standards of Christian education, any more than a police officer should be directing the worship of God.

Mark 12:7.

Master of Divinity (M. Div)

Master of Divinity is used to define the study of different faiths and belief systems. In Christian theology, this degree prepares students to work as a pastor, priest, or in other parts of the ministry. This is the path for students who are interested in religious studies and pursuing work in the professional ministry. For students interested in teaching, an advanced degree can prepare you for a career in religious studies. This program generally requires students to complete 91 Credit hours and focuses on various theologies, Old Testament, New Testament, church history, Pastoral Counseling, and more. TTS, M.Div. requires a thesis, upon completion of the program.

ACADEMIC INFORMATION:

Trinity Theological Seminary offers Master of Divinity (M.Div.) through online mode, which is fully accredited by the IATA (International Association of Theological Accreditation). M.Div. requires 91 credit hours. The program is exclusively online. Courses consists independent study, where the student simply takes courses without traveling to a physical classroom. Performance of the candidate is evaluated on the basis of assignments and reading reports thesis and an online VIVA conducted at the end. FRIT Master of Divinity is a six semester (3 year) course.  

Admission Requirements:

Candidates who are applying for the M.Div. degree must qualify under one of the following categories: Be a graduate of any recognized university. While students who have successfully completed their degrees are preferred, students who are in the final year of studies or awaiting results may also apply. Such candidates will be given provisional admission. They should produce their pass certificate before the end of the second semester (within 1 year of provisional admission at FRIT, otherwise the admission will stand cancelled and all the payments done to FRIT will stand forfeited, i.e., no refund). B.Th. graduates from accredited / affiliated colleges. Candidates, who do not have the necessary academic requirements but are above 20 years of age, are eligible to apply as mature candidates. They will be required to pass the online entrance examination in English, Bible and General Knowledge.

Bachelor of Theology - B.Th

The Bachelor of Theology program is designed to prepare students for various Church ministries. This four year or 8 semester degree program is based on a solid Biblical and theological foundation. A wide range of practical and pastoral units allows specialization in a specific area of ministry. In order to equip them with the advanced ministry skills and personal transformation necessary to lead their ministry to new levels of effectiveness, TTS, B.Th Program has been designed to help them:
  • Rethink the way you do ministry by giving you new critical and analytical thinking tools to effectively address the leadership-needy areas of your ministry.
  • Refocus on calling for your life and ministry to align them with your core values and best gifts with the goal of greater effectiveness and impact in ministry.
  • Retool with the advanced visioneering, leadership and management skills that provide new ways of addressing ministry for greater impact and effectiveness.
  • Renew your passion for a healthy holistic and balanced approach to spiritual disciplines, relationships and your personal relationship with God.
  • Reorient your perspective in with a global and prophetic focus on reaching the lost with world-changing and Spirit-led influence and impact.

Admission Requirement for Bachelor of Theology

Candidates for the B.Th must have successfully completed the pre-university or its equivalent and must have 2-3 years ministry experience. Students who are appearing for exams or awaiting results may also apply. Such candidates may be given provisional admission and will have to produce the grades for the previous course completed. They should produce proof of successful completion before the end of the first semester. The duration of this course will be four years. If the applicant is a matured candidate, he / she then must be above 18 years of age and must have passed 10th Standard + 3-5 years of ministry experience. Diploma holders & Certificate holders in Theology (D.Th & C.Th) from a recognized theological institution can also apply.
